cards.name: The Fool
cards.image_prompt: A young traveller at a cliff edge under a midnight-blue sky, small dog at heel, champagne-gold sun and fine-line stars, elegant minimal style.

upright.summary: A new chapter is opening, and you don't need the full map before you set out. The Fool asks you to go in curious, carry only what's useful, and let experience teach you as you go. Not having every answer yet isn't a flaw here, because it leaves room to discover something you didn't plan for. Pay attention to where you're stepping, and enjoy the feeling of starting.
upright.love: Put down the script about how this should go and let the connection find its own rhythm. Lightness, humour and plain honesty will win more trust than polished efforts to impress. If you're single, say yes to a casual coffee or a new circle of people without loading it with expectations. If you're attached, try something new together, even something as simple as a different hawker centre or an unplanned weekend walk.
upright.career: A new role, project or skill may be worth saying yes to, even if you feel slightly underqualified. Let yourself be a beginner for a while: ask the basic questions, take notes and accept that the learning curve is part of it. People often respect honest curiosity more than pretend expertise. Keep your first steps small and visible so you build confidence along with results.
upright.money: Fresh ideas about earning, saving or organising your money may come up, and it's fine to explore them. Keep a simple written plan beside the excitement so you know what you're trying and why. Small, sensible steps that you can review are enough for now. Curiosity works best with a clear limit you set in advance.
upright.health: Your energy tends to lift when something feels new, like a different walking route, a beginner's class or a fresh morning habit. Keep it playful rather than strict, so you actually want to come back to it. Notice how your body responds and adjust without judging yourself. Enjoying it matters more than intensity right now.
upright.family: Home life may benefit from a fresh approach to an old routine or a familiar disagreement. A relaxed, curious attitude can loosen habits that have gone stiff over the years. Try asking family members what they would like to change instead of assuming. Small experiments, like a new weekend ritual, can bring back some warmth.
upright.general: This is a time for trust and a modest leap. Waiting for complete certainty may only keep you where you are, while starting will teach you what you need to know. Bring common sense with you, but don't let it turn into fear. Treat what happens next as an exploration rather than a test.
upright.yes_no: Leans yes. The timing supports a first step, especially one that is small and easy to adjust later. Go ahead, but keep your eyes open and stay aware of practical details. Starting will make things clearer than thinking about it any longer.
upright.timing: These are early days, and things may start moving faster than you expect. The details tend to sort themselves out once you're in motion. Think of this as the opening of a season rather than its peak. Momentum builds from the first step, not from the planning.
upright.advice: Take the first step, even if it's a small one, and stay curious about what you find. Pack light, both practically and emotionally, so you can adjust as you learn. Let go of needing to look like you know everything. Wonder and good sense can go together.
upright.thread: a fresh start taken with open curiosity and light luggage

reversed.summary: You may be rushing ahead without looking, or freezing because the first step feels too big. Both come from the same unease about the unknown. Reversed, The Fool asks you to pause, look honestly at the ground in front of you, and then move with a bit more care. The beginning is still there for you, and it simply needs some preparation.
reversed.love: Check that you and the other person want the same kind of adventure before you go further. Assumptions, whether hopeful or anxious, can lead to mismatched expectations. A calm, direct conversation about pace and intentions will help more than guessing. If you've been holding back, ask what you're protecting yourself from.
reversed.career: Think the plan through before you commit to a new role or project. A little research, a conversation with someone experienced or a rough timeline can save you repairs later. If you've been hesitating for a long time, set a date to decide so the delay doesn't become the decision. Preparing well is different from avoiding the move altogether.
reversed.money: Watch for impulse choices driven by excitement or boredom. Giving any purchase or new commitment a few days to settle usually shows whether you really want it. Check that you understand what you're agreeing to before you say yes. Being careful now protects the freedom you're hoping for.
reversed.health: Going from doing too much to doing nothing at all can wear you out. Look for a steady, realistic routine you can actually keep through a busy week. Notice whether you're ignoring tiredness or avoiding something you need to start. Gentle consistency will serve you better than bursts of effort.
reversed.family: A hasty word or a decision made without checking with others may cause friction at home. Slow down and ask how a change affects everyone before you act. If someone else is being careless, a patient chat will help more than a lecture. Small check-ins prevent bigger misunderstandings.
reversed.general: Naivety or hesitation is getting in the way of a good idea. The idea itself may be fine, but the approach needs more thought or a little more courage. Ask yourself honestly which one it is. Then adjust and continue rather than dropping it entirely.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, leaning not yet. The idea may be sound, but it needs a closer look before you commit. Fill in the missing details, or face the fear that's stalling you. Ask again once you feel steadier about it.
reversed.timing: Things are moving more slowly than you hoped. Use the pause to prepare, gather information and settle your nerves. This is a waiting stretch before the start, not the end of the road. Once the groundwork is done, you can begin with more confidence.
reversed.advice: Look before you leap, then leap kindly, both toward yourself and others. Take an honest moment to check the facts and your motives. Don't let caution grow into paralysis. Prepare well, then move.
reversed.thread: a leap that needs a pause and a closer look first

cards.name: The Magician
cards.image_prompt: A figure raising a gold wand beneath a midnight sky, table with cup, sword and coin, infinity symbol glowing champagne gold above.

upright.summary: You already have most of what you need, including skills, contacts and ideas. The Magician asks you to bring them together and point them at one clear aim. This is a card about turning thought into action through focus and follow-through. Once you begin with intent, results become possible.
upright.love: Clear, sincere words carry weight right now. Show up as yourself and make sure your actions match what you say. If you're interested in someone, a simple, direct invitation works better than hints. In a relationship, small acts of follow-through build more trust than grand promises.
upright.career: This is a good moment to pitch an idea, build something or take the lead on a project. People can see what you're capable of, so back it up with steady delivery. Prepare your points, gather the right people and set a clear next step. Confidence based on real work is persuasive.
upright.money: Look at the tools, skills and resources you already have before reaching for anything new. A practical idea, such as tidying a budget or using a skill more fully, can grow steadily with attention. Keep it concrete and track what you do. Steady, focused effort tends to pay off better than chasing novelty.
upright.health: Your focus is strong, which makes this a good time to set up a routine you can actually keep. Start with something small and specific, like a regular bedtime or a short daily walk after dinner. Put it in your schedule so it doesn't depend on mood. Over time, small actions add up.
upright.family: You may be the person who can move a household matter forward by taking initiative. Practical help, like sorting a schedule, fixing a problem or coordinating relatives, counts for more than promises. Explain your plan clearly so others feel included rather than managed. Your resourcefulness can ease the load for everyone.
upright.general: Skill, timing and resources are lining up for you. The open question is which direction you choose and whether you commit to it. Pick one aim and use what you have deliberately. Action is what turns potential into something real.
upright.yes_no: Leans yes. You have the means and the ability, so it mostly comes down to whether you act. Make a clear decision and follow through. Hesitating is the main thing that could weaken this.
upright.timing: Things can move quickly once you start. Don't wait for a perfect moment, because the useful energy is here now. Early action builds momentum that carries you forward. This season rewards initiative.
upright.advice: Gather your tools and start today. Name the one thing you want to make happen and take the first concrete step toward it. Trust the skills you've already earned. Let your actions speak for you.
upright.thread: skill and focus turned into deliberate, practical action

reversed.summary: Your energy may be spread across too many things, or a real talent is sitting unused. Reversed, The Magician points to effort without direction, or to doubt quietly undermining you. Bringing your attention back to one clear goal changes a great deal. Your ability hasn't gone anywhere and only needs to be pointed at something.
reversed.love: Mixed messages could creep in, from you or from the other person. Say plainly what you mean and gently ask for the same in return. If words and actions don't match, notice that calmly instead of explaining it away. Clarity is kinder than charm.
reversed.career: Finish one task before you start three more. Your ability needs direction more than extra hours. If you feel underused or doubt yourself, list what you're actually good at and look for one place to apply it. Be careful with shortcuts that look impressive but don't hold up.
reversed.money: Be wary of clever-sounding offers, schemes or shortcuts. Read the details slowly, ask questions and talk to someone you trust before agreeing to anything. If something feels rushed or too polished, take a step back. Being clear protects you better than being quick.
reversed.health: Scattered habits and a racing mind can wear you down without you noticing. Simplify your day where you can and give your attention some rest. Doing one calming thing consistently helps more than trying five at once. Notice when you're running on adrenaline and slow down.
reversed.family: Say what you mean at home, and don't bend the facts to keep the peace. Small half-truths tend to complicate things later. If someone is being less than straightforward, ask gently and plainly. Honesty keeps family matters simpler.
reversed.general: Doubt or distraction is blocking skills you already have. You may be busy without getting anywhere. Choose where to point your effort, and let some lesser tasks wait. Focus will bring back your sense of capability.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, leaning no for now. The goal or the facts aren't clear enough yet to move with confidence. Get clear on what you want and check the details. Once that's settled, the answer may change.
reversed.timing: Progress stays uneven until you narrow your focus. Expect some delay while you sort out priorities. This pause is useful if you use it to decide what matters most. Things speed up once your direction is clear.
reversed.advice: Choose one aim and give it your full attention. Drop or postpone what's pulling you in too many directions. Be honest with yourself and others about what you can deliver. Focused effort will show you what you're capable of.
reversed.thread: talent that needs focus instead of scattered effort

cards.name: The High Priestess
cards.image_prompt: A serene seated figure between two pillars, crescent moon at her feet, veil of champagne-gold pomegranates against deep midnight blue.

upright.summary: Your quiet inner sense knows more than you're giving it credit for. The High Priestess asks you to listen before you speak or act. Not everything is visible yet, and that's fine. Stillness and patient attention will bring the answer to the surface in its own time.
upright.love: Feelings are running deeper than words right now, for you or for them. Give them time to surface instead of pushing for quick answers or labels. Pay attention to what's shown, not only what's said. A calm, unhurried presence invites more honesty than pressure does.
upright.career: Watch and listen before making your move. There may be dynamics or information at work that aren't visible yet. Patience will show you more than rushing to act would. Trust your read of people and situations, and keep your own counsel for now.
upright.money: Hold steady and gather the facts quietly. A calm, considered choice will serve you better than a quick reaction to news or pressure. Take time to understand your own situation clearly. Let your judgement settle before you commit to anything.
upright.health: Rest and quiet are restoring you now. Notice what your body and mood have been telling you, such as tiredness, tension or a need for space. Even a short stretch of silence each day, away from screens, can help. Treat these signals as useful information.
upright.family: There may be unspoken feelings in the household. Be a calm, steady presence and let people share when they're ready. Pushing for explanations may make them close up. Quiet attentiveness shows them you're safe to talk to.
upright.general: The answer is forming below the surface. Stillness and reflection will help you hear it more clearly than outside opinions will. Trust your sense of what feels right, even if you can't fully explain it yet. Some knowledge comes slowly.
upright.yes_no: Mixed. The picture isn't complete yet, so it's too early for a firm answer. Wait, observe and listen to your own instincts. The right response will become clearer with patience.
upright.timing: Things are slow and still unfolding. This is a season for waiting and watching rather than forcing. Let things become clear on their own. Insight tends to arrive quietly once you stop chasing it.
upright.advice: Make space for quiet and listen inward. Spend a little time each day without input, whether that's walking, journaling or simply sitting. Trust what you notice there. Act once your inner sense feels settled.
upright.thread: quiet intuition and answers that arrive when you are still

reversed.summary: Outside noise may be drowning out your instincts. Too many opinions, too much scrolling or a habit of second-guessing can leave you feeling disconnected from what you know. Reversed, The High Priestess asks you to step back and reconnect with your own judgement. The clarity is still there under the clutter.
reversed.love: Something unspoken may need a gentle airing. Instead of guessing or reading into silence, ask kindly and directly. If you've been ignoring a feeling, give it honest attention. Openness, offered without pressure, can bring you closer again.
reversed.career: Hidden details may matter more than they appear to. Ask clear, polite questions rather than relying on office gossip or assumptions. Check the facts directly with the people involved. Your instincts are useful, but they work best alongside real information.
reversed.money: Don't make decisions based on rumours, hype or pressure from others. Check the facts yourself and take your time. If something feels off, trust that and look more closely. Quiet verification protects you.
reversed.health: Too much input may be leaving you drained and unsettled. Switch off screens earlier and give yourself some real quiet. Notice signals you may have been brushing aside, like tiredness or restlessness. Reconnecting with your own rhythm helps restore your energy.
reversed.family: Secrets or long silences may be creating distance at home. A gentle, private conversation can clear the air without anyone feeling exposed. Choose a calm moment and listen more than you speak. Respect people's pace while making it clear you're open.
reversed.general: You may be ignoring a gut feeling or collecting too many opinions. Reconnect with your own reading of the situation. Ask yourself what you'd think if no one else were watching. That answer is worth trusting.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, leaning unclear. There's too much noise or missing information for a confident answer. Gather what you need and reduce outside influence. Ask again once your own view feels clearer.
reversed.timing: Things will stay murky until you cut down the noise. Give yourself some time to clear your head before deciding. This delay is for sorting things out inside, not a sign of failure. Clarity will come back with quiet.
reversed.advice: Turn down the noise and trust your gut. Step away from the voices that cloud your judgement, even if only for a while. Ask direct questions where facts are missing. Your inner sense is still there and needs room to speak.
reversed.thread: an inner voice that is being drowned out by noise

cards.name: The Empress
cards.image_prompt: A gracious figure in a flowing gown seated in a wheat field at night, gold stars in her crown, lush champagne-gold foliage.

upright.summary: This is a season where things grow because they are looked after, not because they are forced. Whatever you have been tending, whether a relationship, a skill or a quiet plan, responds well to steady warmth. Comfort and creativity are easy to reach right now, and you don't need to apologise for enjoying them. Keep giving your attention to what matters and let it ripen in its own time.
upright.love: Affection flows more easily now, and small gestures carry real weight. A packed lunch, a message checking in after a long day or an unhurried dinner can say more than big declarations. If you are single, warmth and openness make you approachable without any effort to impress. Let closeness build through everyday care and shared comforts.
upright.career: Work that involves making, caring or growing something does well under this card. Treat your projects like plants on a windowsill: water them a little each day rather than flooding them once a month. Colleagues may respond to a more generous, supportive approach from you. Ideas that have been sitting quietly may now be ready to take shape.
upright.money: Steady, gentle growth is favoured over quick wins. It's fine to enjoy some comfort, like a good meal out or something nice for the home, as long as it fits sensibly within your means. Think of your resources as something to cultivate patiently. Small, regular habits tend to add up more than you expect.
upright.health: Your energy responds well to simple nourishment: proper meals, enough sleep and time outdoors, even just an evening walk at the park connector. Treat your body as something worth caring for rather than something to push. Slowing down to enjoy food and rest can restore you more than you think. Kindness to yourself is practical here, not indulgent.
upright.family: Home feels warmer and more welcoming, and people may gather more naturally. Shared meals, cooking together or simply sitting in the same room can bring everyone closer. You may find yourself in a nurturing role, and it suits you right now. Small acts of care keep the household feeling settled and supported.
upright.general: Things are maturing through patient attention, and you can see signs of progress. Comfort, creativity and generosity are all within reach. This is a good time to make things, host people or let yourself enjoy what you have built. Growth here is natural and unforced, so trust the process.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. Conditions are favourable for growth, and what you are asking about has fertile ground beneath it. The key is to keep caring for it rather than expecting it to finish itself. With steady attention, the outcome looks warm and positive.
upright.timing: Progress comes gradually, like a plant through its growing season. You may not see daily change, but over weeks things clearly fill out. Rushing won't help and may even disturb what is developing. Let it unfold at a natural, unhurried pace.
upright.advice: Look after yourself with the same tenderness you give others. Make room for comfort, beauty and creative play in your days. Nurture what matters most and let the rest wait. Growth that is cared for tends to last.
upright.thread: patient care, everyday comfort and creativity that steadily grows

reversed.summary: Care has slipped out of balance somewhere. You may be giving so much to others that your own needs have dropped off the list, or comfort has turned into a way of avoiding things. This isn't a failing, just a sign to rebalance. Gently bring some of that nurturing energy back towards yourself.
reversed.love: Love may feel a little heavy, either because one person is doing all the caring or because care has become hovering. Healthy closeness leaves room for both people to breathe and be themselves. Notice whether you are giving to be needed rather than because it feels right. Allowing some space can actually bring you nearer.
reversed.career: Creativity may feel blocked or flat, often because you are running on empty. Forcing ideas rarely works when you're tired. Step away for a bit, take a walk or do something unrelated, and return with fresh eyes. You may also be carrying others' tasks that are not yours to hold.
reversed.money: Watch for spending that stands in for rest, like late-night online orders or treats bought to soothe stress. A little comfort is fine, but notice when it becomes a habit that drains rather than restores. Balance is the aim, not strictness. Ask what you actually need beneath the urge.
reversed.health: Overgiving can quietly wear down your energy. If you've been skipping meals, sleeping late or never having time to yourself, this card asks you to put those basics back first. Rest is not something you earn after everyone else is sorted. If tiredness lingers, it's sensible to check in with a doctor.
reversed.family: You may be doing everything at home yourself, or caring so closely that others feel crowded. Either way, the load needs sharing more fairly. Let family members take on tasks, even if they do them differently from you. Stepping back a little can help everyone grow.
reversed.general: Nurturing has tipped out of balance. Look honestly at where your energy goes and where, if anywhere, you are being replenished. Creativity and warmth return once you stop running on reserves. This is inner work rather than a setback.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed. It could work, but not while you are overextending yourself or holding on too tightly. Once you rebalance your energy and give things some space, the answer becomes more hopeful. For now, care for yourself first.
reversed.timing: Things are moving more slowly for now. Rest and recovery come before progress, and that pause is useful. Pushing ahead while depleted will only stretch the delay. Momentum returns once you have refilled.
reversed.advice: Refill your own cup before pouring for everyone else. Say no to one thing this week so you can say yes to rest. Let others help, even imperfectly. Care that includes you lasts longer.
reversed.thread: care that has tipped into overgiving, smothering or self-neglect

cards.name: The Emperor
cards.image_prompt: A crowned ruler on a stone throne carved with rams, midnight mountains behind, champagne-gold armour and orb, strong geometric lines.

upright.summary: Order, steadiness and clear leadership bring results now. This is a time to build foundations that will hold, with plans you can actually follow. Responsibility suits you, and others may look to you for direction. Firm structure today makes the next steps much easier.
upright.love: Reliability is quietly attractive right now. Turning up when you said you would, following through on promises and being consistent builds deep trust. A relationship may benefit from clearer agreements about time, plans or expectations. Steadiness here is a form of affection.
upright.career: Take charge where it's yours to lead, and do it fairly. Clear plans, sensible routines and accountability help you move forward. You may be asked to organise a team or bring order to a messy project. People respond well to leadership that is calm, consistent and transparent.
upright.money: Structure works in your favour. Budgets, simple records and regular reviews help you see where things stand. Discipline here isn't about deprivation; it's about knowing your numbers and acting with intention. For bigger decisions, a qualified professional can help you plan.
upright.health: A steady routine of sleep, meals and movement supports your energy more than bursts of intensity. Regular habits, even modest ones, build a strong base. Think of it as laying foundations rather than chasing quick changes. Consistency is your quiet strength here.
upright.family: The household benefits from clear roles and dependable routines. You may be the steady one others rely on, which is valuable as long as you stay warm rather than strict. Agreed schedules for chores or caregiving can ease tension. Fairness and predictability help everyone feel secure.
upright.general: Structure and responsibility are strengths now. You can get a great deal done by organising, deciding and following through. Foundations laid carefully today support whatever comes later. Lead your own life with a steady hand.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes, as long as you plan and follow through. The situation responds well to order, clear steps and commitment. Vague hopes are less likely to succeed than a concrete approach. Put structure in place and the outcome looks solid.
upright.timing: Progress is steady and methodical rather than quick. Results come from regular effort applied over time. Each step builds on the last, so skipping stages won't help. Expect dependable movement rather than sudden leaps.
upright.advice: Set clear boundaries and keep them kindly. Decide what matters, plan for it and follow through. Lead by example rather than by force. Firmness and fairness together earn real respect.
upright.thread: structure, steady leadership and foundations built to last

reversed.summary: Control is off balance, either too tight or too loose, and it's causing friction. You may be gripping hard to feel safe, or avoiding structure altogether. Someone else's rigidity could also be part of it. The aim is a fairer middle ground where order serves people.
reversed.love: Tension may come from needing to be right or wanting things done your way. Listening more and deciding less can soften things quickly. If the other person is controlling, calmly naming what you need matters. Partnership works best when power is shared.
reversed.career: A rigid workplace rule or a demanding manager may test your patience. Stay calm, document what matters and stay flexible where it's safe to do so. On the other hand, your own work may lack structure and need tightening. Notice which side of the balance you're on.
reversed.money: Your plan may be too loose, with no clear picture of where money goes, or so strict it's impossible to keep. Either way, it needs a simple review. Aim for a structure that is realistic and adjustable. Small tweaks often work better than overhauls.
reversed.health: Very strict rules and no routine at all can both wear you down. If you've been punishing yourself with rigid habits, ease off; if you've been drifting, add one or two steady anchors. Choose something you can genuinely sustain. Gentleness and structure can go together.
reversed.family: A power struggle may be simmering at home, perhaps over decisions, money or how things should be done. Listen first, before defending your position. Share decisions where you can, and explain your reasons calmly. Respect flowing both ways eases the strain.
reversed.general: Authority is being misused or avoided, whether by you or around you. Rigidity, stubbornness or a lack of discipline are slowing things down. Look for a balance that is firmer in some places and looser in others. Fair structure feels supportive rather than confining.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed, leaning no for now. Without better structure, or with too much control, things are unlikely to settle well. Once the plan is sorted and everyone has more room, the picture can improve. Fix the foundation before expecting a yes.
reversed.timing: Delays come from stubbornness or disorganisation. Holding too tightly, or not holding at all, keeps things stuck. Loosen your grip, replan and set realistic steps. Movement resumes once the structure is fair and workable.
reversed.advice: Lead with firmness and flexibility together. Ask where you are controlling out of fear and where you are avoiding responsibility. Adjust one rule that isn't working. Strong leadership can bend without breaking.
reversed.thread: control or disorder that needs a fairer, more flexible balance

cards.name: The Hierophant
cards.image_prompt: A robed teacher raising a hand in blessing between pillars, crossed gold keys at his feet, midnight-blue arches with champagne-gold detail.

upright.summary: Trusted traditions and experienced people can guide you now. You don't need to invent everything from scratch; a lot has already been learned by those before you. Formal learning, mentors or community wisdom may offer just what you need. Taking the proven path can be a sensible choice.
upright.love: Shared values form a strong base for lasting connection. Conversations about beliefs, family and what you both want long term are worth having. Family opinions may play a role, especially in close-knit households, so listen with respect even where you differ. Commitment and mutual understanding are highlighted.
upright.career: Formal training, certifications or a good mentor can move you forward. Following proper procedures and learning the established way pays off. This is a good time to ask a senior colleague for guidance or join a structured programme. Respecting the system can open doors.
upright.money: Tried and tested approaches suit you better than trends right now. Stick with methods that have a track record and avoid shortcuts. For important decisions, consider speaking with a qualified professional. Learning the basics properly builds lasting confidence.
upright.health: Established routines and proper professional advice serve you well. Reliable habits, like regular meals, sleep and gentle movement, often matter more than new fads. If something worries you, consulting a doctor is the sensible path. Trust what is known to help.
upright.family: Customs, festive gatherings and family traditions bring comfort and a sense of belonging. Respect for elders may be important, and their stories or advice could be valuable. Shared meals and rituals help bind people together. You may find meaning in carrying something forward.
upright.general: Learning from experience and established ways helps you now. Guidance is available if you're willing to ask and listen. Groups, classes or communities with shared values can support you. Structure and belonging go hand in hand here.
upright.yes_no: This is mixed, leaning yes if you follow a proven path. The conventional route has a good chance of working. Going it alone or cutting corners makes the outcome less certain. Seek guidance and do things properly for the best result.
upright.timing: Things move steadily and in proper order. Progress follows the pace of learning, with stages that each need completing. Patience with process is rewarded. Expect a measured, orderly unfolding.
upright.advice: Ask someone wise and really listen to their answer. Respect the knowledge that came before you. Learn the rules well before deciding which to bend. Guidance shared freely is a gift.
upright.thread: guidance from tradition, mentors and values held in common

reversed.summary: You may feel ready to do things your own way. Old rules or expectations feel tight, and you want to understand why they exist. Questioning is healthy when it's thoughtful rather than reactive. Keep what still works and gently reshape the rest.
reversed.love: Your relationship may not follow the usual script, in timing, structure or what others expect. That can be perfectly fine if you both agree on what you want. Pressure from outside may need a calm, united response. Honest conversation matters more than convention.
reversed.career: An unconventional path may be calling, perhaps a different role, a new way of working or self-directed learning. Weigh it carefully before acting, and gather practical information. Rules at work may frustrate you, so pick your battles wisely. Innovation lands best when well prepared.
reversed.money: Don't follow the crowd blindly, whether that's a popular trend or advice that doesn't suit your situation. Think for yourself and check what really fits your needs. Being independent doesn't mean being careless, so do your homework. Qualified advice is still worth considering.
reversed.health: A standard routine may not suit your body or schedule. Adapt thoughtfully, noticing what genuinely helps you. Keep professional advice in view rather than discarding it altogether. Personalising your approach can be wise when done with care.
reversed.family: You may differ from family expectations about choices, beliefs or ways of living. Explain your view calmly and with respect, without needing everyone to agree. Some traditions may feel restrictive while others still bring comfort. Finding your own balance takes patience on all sides.
reversed.general: Old structures feel restrictive, and you're asking honest questions. This is a time to test assumptions and explore new ways. Not every rule deserves keeping, but not every one deserves discarding either. Discernment is the real task.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed. A different route might work, but it needs careful thought. Simply rejecting the usual way won't guarantee success. Think it through, and the answer may become clearer.
reversed.timing: Progress is uneven as you experiment and test new ways. Some attempts may need revisiting. Take time to decide what to keep and what to change. Clarity grows gradually through trial.
reversed.advice: Keep what serves you and kindly release the rest. Question without contempt. Respect others' traditions while honouring your own path. Thoughtful independence is a strength.
reversed.thread: questioning old rules and thoughtfully finding your own way

cards.name: The Lovers
cards.image_prompt: Two figures facing each other under a radiant angel, midnight sky, champagne-gold sun rays and a blossoming tree.

upright.summary: A real bond or an important choice is in front of you, and it asks for more than a quick calculation. What you care about most deeply should guide the decision, not convenience or other people's expectations. When your choice matches your values, it feels steady even if it isn't the easiest one. Pay attention to the connection between you and the people involved, because honesty is what makes it work.
upright.love: There is warmth here, along with honesty and real respect for each other. Both of you seem willing to meet halfway instead of keeping score. If you're single, you may be drawn to someone whose values match yours, not just someone who looks good on paper. If you're attached, this is a good time to talk openly about where you're heading together.
upright.career: Good working partnerships are possible now, whether that's a dependable colleague, a supportive manager or a well-matched team. Lean toward work that fits who you really are, not just what sounds impressive at a family dinner. If you're weighing two options, ask which one you could commit to without quietly resenting it later. Being clear about what you value at work will help others work well with you.
upright.money: Money decisions go better when you make them openly with the people they affect, such as a partner, a parent or a housemate. Shared goals, like saving for a flat or planning family support, keep things calm and fair. Try not to make quiet arrangements that someone might later feel were hidden from them. Talking things through now saves friction later.
upright.health: Your wellbeing improves when your daily habits fit what you actually value. Notice what feels right in your body, not only what looks sensible on a checklist. Maybe it's an evening walk by the park connector instead of another late night at work. Small choices that feel true to you tend to stick.
upright.family: Home feels calmer when everyone feels heard, including the quieter members. A frank but kind conversation over a meal can bring people closer than months of polite avoidance. If there's a family decision to make, include the people it affects. Respecting different views doesn't mean everyone has to agree.
upright.general: This card asks you to choose with your whole self, not only your head. The decision says something about who you are becoming, so it deserves care. Weigh the practical side, but don't ignore what your heart keeps pointing to. A choice you can fully own is worth more than one that only looks safe.
upright.yes_no: This leans clearly towards yes, especially if the option fits your values and everyone involved is being honest. If you feel a quiet sense of rightness about it, trust that. The yes gets stronger when both sides want the same thing. Just make sure you're choosing it for its own sake, not to please someone else.
upright.timing: You're close to a decision point, and things are ready to move. The pace will follow honest conversation, not pressure or deadlines set by other people. Once the important things are said aloud, matters tend to settle quickly. Give it the time a sincere talk needs, then go ahead.
upright.advice: Choose what you could stand behind even if no one were watching. Then say it plainly and kindly to the people who need to hear it. Don't overcomplicate a choice your values have already answered. Let honesty lead and let the details follow.
upright.thread: a meaningful bond or choice that reflects your deepest values

reversed.summary: Something is out of step, either between you and another person or between your choices and your values. Nothing is ruined, but the gap is easy to feel. Take this as a prompt to realign before small differences grow. Honest reflection now saves a harder correction later.
reversed.love: Small misunderstandings may be growing quietly because neither of you has raised them. Assumptions can harden fast when people are tired or busy. Bring things up gently and early, using 'I feel' rather than 'you always'. A short, kind check-in can do more than a big dramatic talk.
reversed.career: A partnership or role may be running on unclear terms. You may assume one thing was promised while others remember it differently. Check that everyone really agrees on responsibilities, credit and expectations, and put the key points in writing. Clarity now protects working relationships you want to keep.
reversed.money: Different views on spending, saving or splitting costs may come to the surface. One person's sensible purchase can look like waste to someone else. Look for common ground before anyone commits to anything. Listening to why someone feels the way they do about money often matters more than the numbers.
reversed.health: You may feel pulled between competing demands, like work, family and your own needs. That tug-of-war can leave you tired and a bit flat. Rest, and decide honestly what matters most this week. Dropping one obligation can give you back more energy than pushing through all of them.
reversed.family: Family members may be pulling in different directions over plans, care duties or old disagreements. It's tempting to take sides fast, but that usually deepens the split. Listen first and ask questions before you give opinions. A calm presence can help the household find middle ground.
reversed.general: Indecision is probably covering a deeper question about what you really want. You might keep circling the options because none of them fully fits. Name the underlying value or need before you try to choose. Once that's clear, the choice often becomes simpler.
reversed.yes_no: This leans no for now. The mismatch, in your own feelings or between the people involved, needs sorting out first. Pushing ahead while things are misaligned tends to create more confusion. Clear up the gap and ask again once you feel steadier about it.
reversed.timing: Things move more slowly until the confusion clears. Expect a stretch of reflection and conversation rather than quick decisions. This isn't wasted time, because it's when the real issues get named. Progress picks up once people are honestly on the same page.
reversed.advice: Pause and ask yourself what you truly value here, without editing the answer. Then compare it with what you've actually been doing. Where the two don't match, make one small change that brings them closer. Act from that answer, not from pressure.
reversed.thread: a gap between your choices and what you truly value

cards.name: The Chariot
cards.image_prompt: A warrior in a canopied chariot drawn by one dark and one light sphinx, midnight city behind, champagne-gold stars on the canopy.

upright.summary: Steady will is carrying you forward. With a clear goal and some self-discipline, you can make real, visible progress. Conflicting feelings may still be there, but you can steer them instead of letting them steer you. This is a card of moving ahead on purpose.
upright.love: Commitment and effort move things forward now. Relationships grow when both of you pull in the same direction, whether that's planning a future or working through a rough patch. If you're single, being clear about what you want helps you recognise it when it shows up. Take the lead gently rather than waiting for things to happen by themselves.
upright.career: Momentum is strong at work. Focus, good preparation and quiet confidence will see you through a demanding push, such as a project deadline, interview or new role. Keep your attention on the main goal and don't get pulled into side battles. Your consistency is what people will remember.
upright.money: Discipline brings results now. Stick to the plan you've already thought through and avoid distractions that pull you off course, like impulse buys or tips everyone is suddenly talking about. Progress may be gradual, but it's real. Checking in on your goals regularly keeps you on track.
upright.health: Routines you keep up now will pay off. Put your energy into a few clear habits instead of spreading it everywhere. Regular sleep, movement and meals give you a steady base. Notice when determination turns into strain, and adjust before you burn out.
upright.family: A shared project at home, like moving house, renovating or planning a big gathering, goes well when someone takes sensible charge. Clear roles and a simple plan keep everyone moving together. If that someone is you, lead with fairness rather than control. People cooperate more readily when they understand the goal.
upright.general: You're in motion and have more control than it might feel like. Direction matters more than speed, so keep checking that you're heading where you mean to go. Opposing pulls in your life can be balanced rather than eliminated. Hold the reins steadily and keep going.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes, provided you keep your focus and put in the work. Success here comes through effort, not luck. If you're willing to commit and stay disciplined, the odds are on your side. Hesitating too long is the main risk.
upright.timing: Things move briskly now. Progress comes as a steady push, not a long wait. Once you commit, you may be surprised how quickly things go. Keep your pace sustainable so the momentum lasts.
upright.advice: Choose your target and hold your course. Keep your emotions steady along the way, so setbacks don't throw you off. Say no to detours that don't serve the goal. Confidence grows each time you follow through.
upright.thread: focused determination steering you steadily toward a clear goal

reversed.summary: Your effort is scattered or pulled in two directions. Progress stalls, not because you lack ability, but because you haven't fully committed to one road. Frustration is a sign to stop and reset. Things move again once you choose a clear direction.
reversed.love: Competing needs may be causing friction, for example one person wants to move faster and the other wants more space. Rushing ahead without agreement usually makes things worse. Talk about where you're each heading before pushing on. Shared direction matters more than speed.
reversed.career: Delays and clashing priorities may be slowing you down. You might be juggling too many tasks or getting mixed signals from different people. Reset the plan, clarify what's truly essential and drop the rest. A narrower focus will get you further.
reversed.money: Rushed decisions are a risk right now, especially ones driven by anxiety or the fear of missing out. Steady and considered beats fast and nervous. If you feel pressured, give yourself time to think. Going back to your basic plan brings calm.
reversed.health: Overdoing it, or trying to do too many things, drains your energy. You may feel restless but tired. Narrow your focus and ease the pace for a while. Recovery is part of moving forward, not a step back.
reversed.family: People at home may want different things, and tempers may get short. If everyone pushes their own agenda, nothing moves. Slow down, sit together and work out who does what. A bit of coordination eases a lot of strain.
reversed.general: Frustration comes from trying to go everywhere at once. Control returns when you simplify and commit to one path. It's fine to let some things wait. A clear direction makes the effort feel lighter.
reversed.yes_no: This leans mixed to no for the moment. The idea isn't hopeless, but the direction isn't clear yet. Fix the plan and settle any inner conflict first. Once you're pointed one way, it can work.
reversed.timing: Expect some delays and false starts. Momentum comes back once you settle on a single course. Use this slower stretch to regroup and plan. Forcing speed now would likely cost you more time.
reversed.advice: Pick one direction and loosen your grip on everything else. Steer gently rather than forcing it. Small, consistent adjustments work better than dramatic swerves. Let go of the need to win every battle at once.
reversed.thread: scattered effort needing one clear direction before it moves

cards.name: Strength
cards.image_prompt: A calm figure gently closing a lion's jaws, infinity sign glowing above, midnight meadow with champagne-gold flowers.

upright.summary: Real strength here is calm and kind. Patience and self-control achieve more than force or pressure. You can face something difficult without hardening yourself. This card reminds you that steadiness is a form of power.
upright.love: Gentleness builds trust now. Be soft and steady with your partner or someone new, and let reassurance do its quiet work. Old fears, yours or theirs, ease with consistent care rather than big gestures. Being both warm and honest is your strength here.
upright.career: Quiet confidence earns respect at work. Handle tense moments, like a hard client or a heated meeting, with composure instead of a show of power. People notice who stays calm. Your patience may resolve problems others couldn't.
upright.money: Calm self-control keeps your finances steady. You can resist pressure from sales, peers or your own impulses without being harsh on yourself. Small, patient habits add up. Trust your ability to wait for what you really want.
upright.health: Be kind to your body and mind while you build resilience. Slow, consistent care works better than intense bursts that leave you worn out. Gentle exercise, regular rest and a calmer pace help. Speak to yourself as you would to a friend you care about.
upright.family: Patience with a difficult relative or a tense household pays off now. Warmth settles more than arguments, even when you're right. Pick your moments and keep your tone soft. Your steady presence can change the mood of the whole home.
upright.general: You have more inner resources than you think. Courage here looks like staying steady, not charging ahead. You can hold your ground and still be gentle. Trust the strength you've built through earlier challenges.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes, as long as you go about it with patience rather than force. Things work out when you stay calm and keep a kind, firm approach. Pushing too hard could undo good progress. Steady effort is what earns the yes.
upright.timing: Results come gradually. Treat this as a slow build, not a sprint. Each patient step adds to the next. You may only see the full effect later, but it's coming together.
upright.advice: Meet the difficulty with a soft heart and firm resolve. Don't confuse gentleness with weakness. Breathe, slow down and respond rather than react. Calm persistence will carry you through.
upright.thread: quiet courage and patience that handle difficulty without force

reversed.summary: Self-doubt is louder than usual, and your energy may be low. This is a dip, not a judgement on who you are. You may feel impatient with yourself or unsure of your footing. It's a time for inner repair before outer effort.
reversed.love: Don't shrink yourself to keep the peace. Your needs count too, and so do your insecurities, which deserve kind attention rather than hiding. If you feel anxious, say so gently instead of testing your partner. A caring relationship can hold your honest feelings.
reversed.career: You may feel drained or unsure of your abilities at work. Comparing yourself to colleagues can make it worse. Rest where you can, and remind yourself of what you've already handled. Confidence returns through small, finished tasks.
reversed.money: Stress spending or panicked choices may feel tempting right now. Buying comfort or rushing to fix a worry rarely helps for long. Wait until you feel calmer before deciding anything important. Simple routines keep you steady in the meantime.
reversed.health: Your reserves are low. Put sleep, regular meals and gentle routines ahead of pushing harder. If you're tired, it's a signal, not a failing. Small acts of care help you rebuild energy over time.
reversed.family: Tension at home may be wearing you down. Patience is harder when you're running on empty. Short breaks, a walk outside and clear, kind limits help you stay steady. It's fine to look after yourself too.
reversed.general: Impatience and insecurity are steering more than usual. You may be quick to judge yourself or others. Rebuild confidence in small, doable steps rather than big leaps. Gentleness toward yourself is the fastest way back.
reversed.yes_no: This leans mixed. The outcome depends on how steady you feel when you commit. If you're acting from fear or fatigue, wait a little. Once you feel more grounded, the answer may become clearer.
reversed.timing: Progress is slow for now. Energy and confidence come back with rest and a few small wins. Don't rush yourself through this phase. Steady recovery comes before forward movement.
reversed.advice: Be patient with yourself, and start with something small. Notice the harsh voice inside and answer it kindly. Rest without guilt. Strength comes back when you stop fighting yourself.
reversed.thread: self-doubt and tiredness calling for gentleness toward yourself

cards.name: The Hermit
cards.image_prompt: A cloaked elder on a snowy peak holding a lantern with a champagne-gold star inside, deep midnight sky, minimal composition.

upright.summary: This is a time to step back from the crowd and listen to your own judgement. Too many opinions and notifications have been drowning out what you already sense is true. When you give yourself some quiet, things that felt tangled start to sort themselves out. Treat the solitude as useful work, not as running away.
upright.love: Some time on your own can show you what you really want from a relationship, without other people's expectations in the way. If you are attached, it is fine to ask for an evening or a weekend to yourself. That is healthy, and it is not the same as being cold. If you are single, use this stretch to understand your own patterns before you start looking again.
upright.career: You do your best work right now when you can focus alone, away from meetings and office chatter. It is a good time to study, research or plan carefully before you commit to anything. Block out quiet hours in your calendar and protect them. The thinking you do now will make your next move steadier and better informed.
upright.money: Sit down quietly with your accounts and look at where things honestly stand. You do not need a dramatic plan. A simple, unhurried review is enough to show you what is working and what is not. Keep the outside noise and comparisons to a minimum so your own priorities stay clear.
upright.health: Your body and mind would benefit from stillness and a slower pace. Cutting back on screens, noise and rushing can help your energy settle. A quiet walk at dawn, an early night or a few minutes of calm breathing can do more than you expect. Pay attention to what your body is telling you when things go quiet.
upright.family: The constant bustle of a busy household may be wearing you down, and you might need a little space. A short walk, a quiet corner or an afternoon on your own can help you come back with more patience. Let your family know this is about rest, not about pulling away from them. Everyone tends to benefit when you return calmer.
upright.general: The answers you are looking for are mostly already inside you. You will only hear them once the noise around you dies down. This card asks for reflection, patience and a willingness to be alone with your thoughts for a while. Wisdom builds up slowly when you slow down too.
upright.yes_no: The answer is mixed for now. It is neither a clear yes nor a firm no, because you still need to think the matter through. Give yourself more time and quiet before you decide. Once you have reflected properly, your own judgement will most likely give you the answer.
upright.timing: This is a slow, reflective season, not a quick one. Answers come gradually as you think, so rushing will only muddy them. Allow a little extra time before you commit. Things will become clearer once you have had a proper pause.
upright.advice: Switch off the noise for a while, whether that is your phone, the news or other people's opinions. Take a quiet walk or sit somewhere calm and let your thoughts settle. Write down what keeps coming back to you. Trust the clear sense you get from that quiet, even if it is a gentle one.
upright.thread: a need for quiet reflection and trusting your own inner guidance

reversed.summary: Time alone may have slipped into isolation or quietly avoiding things. What started as rest might now be keeping you away from support and fresh ideas. This is not a failing, just a sign that it is time to come back out a little. Reach out to one person you trust and see how it feels.
reversed.love: You might be keeping people at arm's length, perhaps to protect yourself from being hurt. That makes sense, but too much distance can leave both you and a partner feeling lonely. Let someone in a little, at a pace that feels safe to you. Even a short honest message can soften the walls.
reversed.career: Ideas that you keep to yourself cannot grow or get noticed. You may be working in isolation because you are afraid of criticism or think you have to do it all alone. Share a draft, ask a colleague for their view, or join the conversation in meetings. Feedback will strengthen your work more than more hours alone will.
reversed.money: Avoiding your bank app or bills tends to make the worry bigger than the numbers really are. Set aside fifteen calm minutes to look at where things stand. Most of the time, knowing the facts brings relief, even if some things need attention. If you need it, talking to someone you trust can help you keep going.
reversed.health: Pulling back too much can deepen low moods and drain your energy. Gentle contact with others, daylight and fresh air can help you feel more like yourself. Try something small, like a kopi with a friend or a walk around the block. If heaviness lingers, it is wise to speak to a professional or someone you trust.
reversed.family: You may be drifting away from relatives, or they may have gone quiet with you. Distance like this often builds up through busyness rather than any real conflict. A short call, a message in the family chat or a simple meal together can ease it. You do not need to fix everything at once to reconnect.
reversed.general: Time alone has stopped helping and started hiding you from things. The quiet that once gave you clarity may now be keeping you stuck. Reconnect with the world in small, manageable steps. Company and conversation can offer perspective that thinking alone no longer gives you.
reversed.yes_no: This leans no for now, mainly because something is being avoided rather than faced. Moving ahead while you are still withdrawn is unlikely to feel right. Deal with the thing you have been putting off, then ask again. Once you engage with it, the answer may well change.
reversed.timing: Things are likely to stay stuck for as long as you stay tucked away. The pace picks up once you reach out, share and take part again. You do not need a big gesture to get things moving. Small steps outward are what set the next phase in motion.
reversed.advice: Balance your time alone with good company. Make one small contact today, such as a message, a call or an invitation. Notice how it changes your mood and your view of things. Keep the solitude that restores you, and let go of the kind that only isolates you.
reversed.thread: withdrawal that has turned into avoidance and needs gentle company

cards.name: Wheel of Fortune
cards.image_prompt: A great rotating wheel with symbols etched in champagne gold, clouds and four winged creatures in the corners, midnight-blue sky.

upright.summary: Life is turning, and right now the timing seems to be on your side. Changes you did not plan for may open doors you could not see before. Going with the movement usually works better than resisting it. Stay alert and ready to act when a good opening appears.
upright.love: A new chapter, a lucky meeting or a fresh energy in an existing relationship could be on the way. Stay open and curious rather than holding tightly to how you think things should go. Say yes to the invitation or the conversation you would usually skip. Some connections show up at unexpected moments.
upright.career: The timing at work seems to be in your favour. A new opening, project or contact is worth taking seriously, even if it came from nowhere. Make sure your CV and portfolio are current so you are ready when chances come. Momentum tends to reward people who are prepared.
upright.money: Positive changes in your finances are possible, though nothing is guaranteed. While things are moving, keep your habits sensible and your records in order. Do not let a good turn tempt you into careless decisions. Steady choices help you hold on to the benefits of good timing.
upright.health: A change in routine or outlook could do you good now. Try a new walking route, a different sleep schedule or a fresh way of eating, and see what suits you. Keep whatever works and let go of what does not. Being willing to adapt is your strength in this phase.
upright.family: A new phase at home may be arriving, such as a milestone, a move, a new family member or changed arrangements. Even good changes can unsettle routines for a while. Being flexible and talking openly will make the transition easier for everyone. Mark the moment together if you can.
upright.general: A cycle is turning and new options are opening up. You cannot control every part of it, but you can be ready and willing. Watch for patterns and small signs that things are moving. This is a good time to take part rather than stand on the sidelines.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. Conditions seem to be moving in your favour, and the timing looks supportive. Act thoughtfully, but do not hold back out of habit. If an opening appears, it is probably worth taking.
upright.timing: In terms of the cycle, change is coming soon. A turning point is near, and things are starting to move. Expect momentum rather than a long wait. Be ready, because the opening may arrive quickly.
upright.advice: Welcome change with an open hand rather than a clenched fist. Stay adaptable and keep your plans loose enough to adjust. Notice which opportunities line up naturally. Say yes to good timing when you recognise it.
upright.thread: a turning point where timing and change begin to favour you

reversed.summary: You may be in a dip or a delay, and it can feel as though nothing is moving. This is part of the cycle, not a permanent state. Downturns pass, especially when you use them well. Be patient with yourself while the wheel turns again.
reversed.love: Old relationship patterns may be repeating, such as the same arguments or the same type of person. Noticing the loop is the first step to breaking it. This time, try responding differently, even in a small way. Changing your own part can shift the whole pattern.
reversed.career: Setbacks at work, such as a delayed promotion, a cancelled project or a no, are not failures. They are pauses in a longer cycle. Use this quieter period to build skills, tidy your portfolio or strengthen your network. When things turn again, you will be ready.
reversed.money: Unexpected costs or slower income may show up. A small buffer and steady habits can soften these bumps. Focus on the basics rather than trying to win it all back quickly. This phase will pass, and careful choices will help it pass smoothly.
reversed.health: Your energy may go up and down more than usual. Keep your routines gentle and consistent rather than chasing quick fixes. Rest when you need to and move when you can. If changes concern you, a check-in with a doctor can give you peace of mind.
reversed.family: Family plans may slip or change at short notice, which can be frustrating. Patience and a sense of humour help keep the mood light. Have a backup plan where you can, and avoid blaming anyone. These hiccups usually settle once the busy stretch is over.
reversed.general: Fighting the change only makes it harder. Accept what is outside your control and put your effort into what you can influence. The wheel keeps turning, even when it feels slow. Use this phase to rest, reflect and prepare.
reversed.yes_no: This leans no for now. The timing does not look right yet, and pushing could bring frustration. That does not mean never. Wait for the next turn, then ask again.
reversed.timing: Things are moving more slowly than you hoped. You may be waiting for a cycle to finish before the next one starts. Do not force it, because the wheel will keep turning. Use the wait to get ready for the next phase.
reversed.advice: Get through this turn calmly, without panic or self-blame. Keep doing the steady, useful things that prepare you for what comes next. Let go of trying to control the timing. Trust that phases change, because they always do.
reversed.thread: a temporary setback in a cycle that will keep turning

cards.name: Justice
cards.image_prompt: A composed figure holding upright sword and balanced gold scales, seated between pillars, midnight drapery with champagne-gold trim.

upright.summary: Fair outcomes tend to follow honest actions. This card asks you to weigh things clearly, look at the facts and be truthful with yourself and others. Decisions made this way may not always be easy, but they usually hold up. Clarity is on your side when you stay straightforward.
upright.love: Honesty and balance strengthen the relationship now. Notice whether giving and receiving feel even, and talk openly if they do not. Fair agreements about time, effort and expectations build trust. Saying what you mean, kindly, is the way forward.
upright.career: Fair treatment and clear agreements matter at work right now. Keep good records, read contracts and terms carefully, and put important points in writing. If a decision is being made, make sure your contribution is visible and accurate. Acting with integrity strengthens your standing over time.
upright.money: Things tend to balance out when you stay honest and organised. Go through statements, agreements and receipts carefully. Make sure what you owe and what you are owed are both clear. If anything is complex, an appropriate professional can help you understand the details.
upright.health: Cause and effect are easy to see here. Consistent habits around sleep, food and movement tend to bring consistent results. Look honestly at what helps you and what drains you. Small, balanced adjustments work better than extremes.
upright.family: Fairness at home helps calm tension. Share chores, costs and caring duties evenly, and talk about them plainly. When everyone feels heard, resentment has less room to grow. A calm family discussion can reset things.
upright.general: Truth and consequences are in focus. Look at the situation without bias, including your own part in it. Clear facts lead to clearer decisions. What you put in now shapes what comes back.
upright.yes_no: This one is mixed, and it depends on the facts. If the terms are fair and the details hold up, the answer leans yes. If something is unclear or one-sided, it leans no. Check the facts honestly before you decide.
upright.timing: Things will move at the pace of paperwork, process and proper review. Expect them to take as long as they need, no faster. Patience with formal steps pays off. A fair outcome is worth the wait.
upright.advice: Act fairly, tell the truth and keep your records clear. Then let the outcome follow without trying to manipulate it. Ask yourself whether you would be comfortable if everyone saw your choices. If you would, you are on solid ground.
upright.thread: honest, balanced dealings and the consequences of your own choices

reversed.summary: Something may feel unfair, one-sided or not fully honest. Before you judge, look at every side, including your own. Imbalance often builds up from small things nobody has mentioned. Clearer facts and a calm conversation can help put it right.
reversed.love: One person may be giving more time, effort or emotional care than the other. Rather than keeping a silent tally, talk about it calmly and with specific examples. Listen to their side as well. Fairness in love is something you agree on together, not a court case.
reversed.career: Look again at agreements, job scopes or credit for your work. If anything seems vague or uneven, ask for clarity politely and in writing. Stay factual rather than emotional when you raise it. If you need to, find out what proper channels are available.
reversed.money: Check your bills, receipts and statements, since small errors are easy to miss. Mistakes are usually simple to fix when you catch them early. Make sure shared expenses feel fair to everyone involved. Being honest about your own spending matters too.
reversed.health: You may be ignoring the effect certain habits are having on you. Face them kindly rather than harshly, without blame. Adjust one thing at a time so the change can last. If something worries you, a professional can give you clear guidance.
reversed.family: Old grievances about who does what may come back up. Aim for fairness going forward rather than keeping score of the past. Clear agreements about chores, money or care can ease tension. A calm, honest talk tends to work better than hints.
reversed.general: Bias, half-truths or responsibility being dodged are clouding the situation. This can come from others, or from your own reluctance to see something. Clearer facts lead to a fairer result. Being honest, including with yourself, starts to restore balance.
reversed.yes_no: This leans no until the facts are clear and the arrangement is fair to everyone. Moving ahead with things unresolved could cause trouble later. Sort out the details and be honest about your part first. Then the answer may change.
reversed.timing: Delays are coming from unresolved details, missing information or avoided conversations. Things tend to stay on hold until these are dealt with. Focus on clearing them one by one. Progress returns once everything is clear.
reversed.advice: Own your part honestly, without overdoing the guilt. Let go of the parts that are not yours to carry. Ask for clarity where things feel unfair. Aim for balance, not for winning.
reversed.thread: an imbalance or half-truth that needs honest review

cards.name: The Hanged Man
cards.image_prompt: A serene figure hanging by one foot from a living tree, halo of champagne-gold light, calm expression, midnight-blue background.

upright.summary: This card describes a pause you have chosen, or at least can accept, and the clearer view it gives you. While you were rushing, some details were hard to see. Now that things have slowed, you can notice what you missed. Stepping back is not wasted time at the moment; it is the work. Let the quiet show you something before you move again.
upright.love: Let the connection settle instead of pressing for an answer or a label. Listening more than you talk will show you what each of you actually needs, which may differ from what you assumed. If something feels unresolved, give it a few calm days rather than forcing a big talk tonight. Patience here comes from care, not weakness.
upright.career: A project or decision that seems stuck may be giving you useful thinking time. Try looking at the problem from your manager's, client's or colleague's side before you act. You may find a simpler route, or see that the timing was never right. Write down what you notice so the pause turns into a better plan.
upright.money: This is a season to hold off on large commitments until the picture is clearer. Waiting a little is often wiser than deciding under pressure or because of a promotion that is about to end. Use the time to gather information and check your own priorities. When your view settles, the right choice will feel calmer.
upright.health: Your body and mind may be asking for a real break, not just a shorter to-do list. Rest without treating it as something you have to earn. Notice what slowing down shows you about your sleep, your mood and the habits that drain you. If anything worries you, a chat with a professional is a sensible step.
upright.family: Give a family disagreement some room to breathe before you try to settle it. Try to understand why a parent, sibling or partner sees things the way they do, even if you still disagree. A softer conversation after a pause often goes further than an argument during a busy week. Your patience can lower the temperature at home.
upright.general: Things are on hold for reasons you may not fully see yet. Letting go of control for a while, rather than fighting the delay, can bring surprising insight. Turn the situation around and ask what it would look like from the opposite side. What you notice in this suspended moment may change your next step.
upright.yes_no: Mixed. A clear yes or no is less likely right now than not yet. The situation needs more time, and so does your understanding of it. Wait for more clarity before you treat any answer as final.
upright.timing: Slow and suspended. Expect a stretch of waiting where little seems to move on the surface. It tends to end once your perspective has shifted, not because of a date on the calendar. Use the stillness well, and movement will come back on its own.
upright.advice: Stop pushing for a while and look at the situation from the opposite angle. Ask yourself what you would see if your assumptions were wrong. Rest, observe and take notes. A good decision often comes after a pause, not in the middle of a rush.
upright.thread: a useful pause that shows you a fresh way of seeing

reversed.summary: The waiting may have gone on longer than it needed to. Some of the delay now comes from your own hesitation rather than from circumstances. A pause that once helped can turn into a habit of putting things off. It is worth asking honestly what you are still waiting for, and whether it will ever arrive.
reversed.love: Staying in limbo out of habit or fear is not fair to you or the other person. Ask yourself plainly what you want from this connection. Then say it kindly and clearly, even if your voice shakes a little. A clear answer, whatever it turns out to be, is usually easier to live with than endless uncertainty.
reversed.career: A decision at work has sat on the shelf long enough. Choose a reasonable option, even if it is imperfect, and start moving; you can adjust along the way. Waiting for perfect conditions can quietly cost you chances and energy. Small progress will tell you more than another round of thinking.
reversed.money: You may be avoiding small money tasks because the bigger ones feel heavy. Pick one manageable item today, such as checking a statement, sorting a bill or noting your monthly outgoings. Doing one thing breaks the freeze and makes the rest feel lighter. Clarity tends to follow action here.
reversed.health: Resisting rest, or avoiding a change in routine you know you need, may be draining you. You do not have to overhaul everything at once. Start with one small adjustment, like an earlier night or a short walk after dinner. Seek proper advice if something has been bothering you for a while.
reversed.family: Avoiding a family conversation keeps the tension quietly simmering. Everyone may be waiting for someone else to go first. A gentle opening line, such as a message or a shared meal, can ease more than you expect. You don't need to fix everything in one talk, only to begin.
reversed.general: You may be stalling, perhaps because you are afraid of choosing wrongly. The sacrifice you are making by waiting no longer buys you anything useful. Notice where indecision is costing you peace of mind. Even a small choice now can get things moving again.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, but leaning toward acting. More waiting is unlikely to give you a better answer than the one you could find by trying. Take a sensible step and learn from what happens. The answer becomes clearer once you move.
reversed.timing: Overdue. The pause has run its course, even if part of you wants it to continue. Momentum comes back quickly once you take a first concrete step. Expect things to pick up from the moment you stop holding back.
reversed.advice: End the waiting with one small, concrete step today. Send the message, make the call or write the first line. Don't wait for courage to arrive before you start; it usually comes once you begin. Afterwards, notice how much lighter you feel.
reversed.thread: a wait that has gone on longer than it needs to

cards.name: Death
cards.image_prompt: A gentle armoured rider on a white horse at dawn, sun rising between two towers in champagne gold, white rose banner, midnight sky softening.

upright.summary: This card speaks of transformation, not literal death. A chapter of your life is closing so that something better suited to who you are now can begin. Endings can feel unsettling even when they are right. Honour what this stage gave you, then turn gently toward what comes next.
upright.love: An old pattern, or an older version of the relationship, may be coming to a natural close. This could mean letting go of a habit of silence, an outdated expectation or a past hurt. Clearing it makes room for something more honest and caring. If you are single, it may be the end of an old way of looking for love.
upright.career: A role, routine or way of working may be winding down. Rather than holding on tightly, notice what new direction becomes possible once you accept the change. This might be a shift in responsibilities, skills or focus. Approach it thoughtfully, at a pace that feels sensible to you.
upright.money: This is a good time to clear out spending habits or arrangements that no longer fit your life. Old subscriptions, outdated budgets or habits picked up during a different season can all be reviewed. Simplifying now gives you a steadier footing. Make changes calmly rather than all at once.
upright.health: Letting go of an old routine can renew your energy. Habits that suited you years ago may not suit the person you are today. Choose rhythms of sleep, movement and rest that fit your current life. Give yourself time to adjust as the new routine settles in.
upright.family: Family roles may be shifting as children grow up, parents age or new responsibilities appear. These changes can bring both relief and a quiet sense of loss. Accept them with respect for what came before. Talking openly about new roles can help everyone feel less unsettled.
upright.general: An ending is natural and necessary here. Allow yourself to feel whatever comes with it, including sadness or relief. Once you have acknowledged what is closing, turn toward what is arriving. Renewal often begins quietly, just after we stop resisting.
upright.yes_no: Mixed. If you are asking about keeping things exactly as they were, the answer leans no. If you are asking about a changed or renewed path, it leans yes. Consider what is ending and what could take its place.
upright.timing: A genuine turning point. The ending tends to become clear first, sometimes quite plainly. Renewal unfolds more gradually afterwards, like a new season settling in. Allow both stages the time they need.
upright.advice: Let go with thanks for what this chapter gave you. Name what you are ready to release, even if only to yourself. Then make some practical room, in your time, space or thoughts, for the next step. Change is easier when you meet it halfway.
upright.thread: an ending that clears space for real renewal

reversed.summary: You may be holding on to something that has already run its course. Resisting the change does not stop it; it only makes the transition longer and more tiring. This is not a sign that something is wrong with you. It is an invitation to loosen your grip a little.
reversed.love: Holding on to the past, or to who someone used to be, can block new warmth from reaching you. You might be comparing the present with an older, happier version of things. Allow yourself to grieve what has changed. Letting go makes space for honest closeness again.
reversed.career: Fear of change may be keeping you in a habit or role that no longer fits. Change tends to come anyway, so it helps to meet it on your own terms. Think about one skill or step that would make the shift feel more manageable. Move at a pace you can sustain.
reversed.money: Old money habits or attachments may be holding you back. Perhaps you are keeping a routine just because it feels familiar. Try replacing one of them with a new habit that suits your life now. Small changes, kept up, add up to steadier footing.
