reversed.health: Staying in worn-out routines can leave you feeling flat and tired. Your energy may improve with one small, deliberate change, such as a new bedtime or a different way to unwind. Be patient with yourself while it settles. If low energy lasts, it is reasonable to check in with a professional.
reversed.family: Old family patterns may carry on simply because change feels uncomfortable for everyone. You can't change others, but you can try one new way of relating. That might mean listening differently or setting a gentle boundary. Small shifts often invite others to shift too.
reversed.general: The transition feels slow because part of you is resisting it. That is very human, and nothing about it is shameful. What helps now is acceptance rather than force. Once you allow the change, things tend to move more smoothly.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, leaning no if you are hoping to hold on to what is ending. Releasing the old is likely the better answer. Ask yourself what you would choose if you weren't afraid of the change.
reversed.timing: Slow and drawn out. The process stretches on while you resist it. Things begin moving forward once you stop holding back. Your acceptance sets the pace more than outside events do.
reversed.advice: Loosen your grip a little and let yourself breathe. Notice what you are clinging to and ask whether it still serves you. Take one small step toward letting it go. Be kind to yourself as you adjust.
reversed.thread: a change you are slow to accept and release

cards.name: Temperance
cards.image_prompt: An angel pouring water between two gold cups, one foot on land and one in a pool, irises and a champagne-gold sunrise path, midnight tones.

upright.summary: Balance and patience are working in your favour. A steady middle path is bringing calm and good results, even if progress feels quiet. You are learning to blend different needs without swinging to extremes. Keep trusting the gentle pace, because it is serving you well.
upright.love: Give and take comes more easily now. Compromise feels natural rather than forced, and both of you can meet halfway. A calm, unhurried pace lets trust grow on firm ground. If you are single, connections that build slowly may turn out to be the most rewarding.
upright.career: Steady, measured effort is paying off. You may be bringing together different tasks, teams or ideas, and patience is what makes the mix work. Avoid the urge to overcommit or to cut corners. A consistent rhythm will earn quiet respect and good results.
upright.money: Moderation works well for you here. Keep spending, saving and enjoying life in sensible proportion. You don't need dramatic moves; small, consistent choices bring stability. A balanced approach helps you feel secure without feeling deprived.
upright.health: Balanced routines of rest, food and movement support you well right now. Small habits you keep up beat dramatic efforts that fade after a week. Notice what helps you feel even and settled through the day. Gentle consistency is your friend.
upright.family: Home feels more harmonious when everyone gives a little. Mix patience with kindness, especially with relatives whose habits differ from yours. Shared meals, chores or simple routines can bring people together. Small acts of consideration go a long way.
upright.general: Things are coming into proportion. Careful blending of your priorities, along with a calm pace, is leading to a good outcome. You don't need to rush or prove anything. Steady attention is enough.
upright.yes_no: Leans yes, as long as you move steadily and avoid extremes. A balanced, patient approach is likely to bring a good result. Rushing or overdoing it could tip things off course, so keep a measured pace.
upright.timing: Gradual and even. Progress comes through patient, steady steps rather than a sudden leap. Things unfold at a comfortable, natural pace. Trust the slow build, because it lasts.
upright.advice: Find the middle way and stick to it. When you feel pulled toward too much or too little, pause and adjust gently. Blend effort with rest and firmness with kindness. Balance is something you practise each day, not a place you arrive at once.
upright.thread: balance, moderation and patiently blending what matters

reversed.summary: Something has tipped into too much or too little. It could be work, worry, spending or the effort you put into others. When one area takes over, the rest begins to wobble. Now is the time to bring things gently back toward the centre.
reversed.love: Overreacting, or putting in uneven effort, may be causing friction. One person might feel they are giving far more than the other. Take a breath before replying, especially over text, and aim for fair give and take. Calm conversations will help restore the balance.
reversed.career: You may be overworking or swinging between bursts of effort and exhaustion. Rest is part of good work, not a reward for finishing it. Pace yourself, set realistic expectations and protect some time to recover. Steady effort will serve you better than sprinting.
reversed.money: Spending or saving has drifted out of proportion. You might be splurging to cope, or being so strict that life feels joyless. A few small, thoughtful adjustments can restore balance. Look for the middle ground that feels sustainable.
reversed.health: Overdoing something, whether work, late nights, food or screens, may be wearing you down. Pull back toward a steadier daily rhythm. Choose one area to rebalance first instead of fixing everything at once. If you feel persistently unwell, speak to a professional.
reversed.family: Tempers or demands at home may be running high. Before addressing a sore point, give yourself time to cool down. Then speak plainly and listen in return. Fairness in sharing chores and attention can ease a lot of strain.
reversed.general: Haste or excess is throwing things off course. You may be trying to do too much, too quickly. Recalibrate before you push on. A short pause to rebalance will save effort later.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, leaning no for now. Conditions are a little out of balance, which makes a clear yes unwise at the moment. Rebalance first, then reconsider with a calmer mind.
reversed.timing: Uneven and rushed. Things may lurch forward and then stall. They settle once you slow down and correct the balance. A steadier pace returns after some adjustment.
reversed.advice: Slow down and rebalance one area at a time. Notice where you are overdoing or underdoing things. Make a small, realistic correction and keep it for a while. Balance comes back through steady, gentle practice.
reversed.thread: something out of proportion that needs gentle rebalancing

cards.name: The Devil
cards.image_prompt: A stylised horned figure on a dark pedestal, two figures with loose chains they could lift off, midnight shadows and muted champagne-gold accents, not frightening.

upright.summary: Something has a firmer hold on you than you'd like to admit. It could be a habit, a person, a craving for approval or a comfort you keep going back to. The card isn't judging you. It's asking you to look at the pattern honestly. Once you can see clearly what you keep giving away and what you get back, you have a real choice again.
upright.love: Look at patterns in your relationship that feel heavy, possessive or hard to question. Jealousy, keeping score or staying quiet just to avoid conflict can slowly feel normal. Healthy closeness leaves both people room to breathe and to be themselves. Notice where you feel small or watched, and talk about it calmly with someone you trust or with your partner when it feels safe.
upright.career: Work, a title or other people's approval may be taking up more of your life than you agreed to. Maybe you answer messages late at night out of habit, or chase recognition that never quite comes. Ask yourself honestly what you're trading for it, whether that's sleep, friendships or your own sense of worth. Seeing the deal clearly doesn't mean you have to change everything. It just helps you set limits you can actually keep.
upright.money: Small spends that are about keeping up appearances or getting a quick lift can add up without you noticing. Think of the late-night online cart, the upgrade you didn't really need, or commitments you keep paying for out of pride. Track it for a few weeks with curiosity instead of guilt. Once you can see the pattern, it's easier to choose what stays.
upright.health: A comfort habit might be taking more energy than it gives back. That could be scrolling until 2am, too much caffeine, or skipping meals when you're stressed. Watch it without shame, because these habits usually started as ways to cope. Try one small swap or a gentle limit, and notice how you feel after a week.
upright.family: Duty, guilt or old expectations may be setting the rules at home more than real care is. Maybe someone always gives in, or a role you took on as a child still shapes how you act at family dinners. Ask which ties you truly choose and which ones you're just carrying out of habit. Respecting your family and keeping your own boundaries can both be true.
upright.general: You're more free than you feel right now. The chains in this card are loose enough to slip off once you notice them. Naming what holds you, out loud or in writing, already starts to loosen it. You don't need a dramatic break, just honest attention and one different choice.
upright.yes_no: This card leans no. Whatever is pulling at you may appeal mostly because it's tempting, easy or familiar, not because it's good for you. Wait before you say yes, and ask what you'd be giving up. If the answer still feels right once the pull fades, you can come back to it.
upright.timing: Things may feel stuck for now. The pattern tends to repeat until you see it clearly. Once you do, change can come surprisingly quickly, because much of the hold was never as strong as it looked. Don't expect the situation to resolve by itself while you look away.
upright.advice: Name what has a hold on you, plainly and without judging yourself. Write it down or tell someone you trust. Then make one small choice that gives you back a little room, like a pause before you reply, a limit you set, or a night off. The grip loosens when you look at it directly.
upright.thread: an attachment or habit pulling harder than you realise

reversed.summary: You're starting to see the pattern for what it is, and its hold is loosening. You might feel lighter, or a bit exposed, as an old habit or tie lets go. Real change at this stage is often uneven, with good days and slips. What matters is that you're now paying attention, and that's hard to undo.
reversed.love: Old relationship patterns are losing their hold. A calm, honest conversation can clear things that have been building up quietly for a long time. You might both find you've been playing roles neither of you really wanted. Facing it together, or setting a kind boundary, can leave you both more free.
reversed.career: You may be outgrowing a role, a work culture or a habit of over-giving that has been draining you. Notice it, but plan instead of reacting. Think about which skills, conversations or boundaries would make your next step steadier. Freedom at work usually comes in stages, not all at once.
reversed.money: This is a good time to drop a costly habit or untangle a commitment you no longer want. Begin with the easiest one, such as cancelling an unused subscription or setting a pause before online purchases. Small wins build trust in yourself. You'll probably find you miss very little of it.
reversed.health: Breaking a draining habit is within reach. Go gently, because harsh rules tend to backfire, while small, steady changes usually last. Notice and celebrate progress, even one better night's sleep. If it feels heavy, talking with a trusted friend or a professional can help.
reversed.family: You may be stepping out of an old family role, like the peacemaker, the one who always gives in, or the one who carries everyone's worries. Others might push back a little at first. Stay kind and steady, and explain where you can, without turning it into a fight. Over time, the household can adjust to a fairer balance.
reversed.general: Awareness is turning into freedom. You can see what held you, and you're starting to choose differently. It may not feel smooth, and old pulls can return on tired days. That doesn't cancel your progress. Keep coming back to the choice.
reversed.yes_no: This card leans yes to letting go and no to whatever has been holding you back. If your question is about stepping away from a habit or loosening an old tie, the answer leans toward freedom. If it's about going back to that pattern, it leans no. Trust the part of you that feels lighter.
reversed.timing: Things are easing gradually. Relief usually builds step by step, with a few setbacks along the way. Each small choice makes the next one easier. Give it a season of steady effort rather than expecting a clean break overnight.
reversed.advice: Choose freedom one small step at a time. Pick a single habit or tie to loosen this week and be kind to yourself when you slip. Tell someone supportive what you're working on. Progress you're gentle with tends to last.
reversed.thread: a loosening grip and the start of real freedom

cards.name: The Tower
cards.image_prompt: A tall tower struck by a champagne-gold lightning bolt, crown tumbling, midnight storm clouds parting to reveal stars, dramatic but hopeful.

upright.summary: Something that has felt shaky may change suddenly. A plan, a belief or an arrangement that rested on weak ground can't hold up much longer. It may be unsettling, but what's left afterwards is more honest and more solid. You don't have to like the shake-up to learn from it.
upright.love: An unexpected truth may come out, either in a conversation or in something you finally admit to yourself. It can sting, and it may change how you see the relationship. Honesty, even when it's uncomfortable, makes room for something real. Give yourself time to take it in before you decide anything.
upright.career: Plans, team setups or projects might change without much warning. Stay calm and deal with what's in front of you instead of every possible what-if. Flexibility and clear communication will help more than holding on to how things used to be. Sometimes a disruption shows you strengths you didn't know you had.
upright.money: Unexpected costs or changes are possible, so keep a buffer where you reasonably can. Look over your essentials and know where you stand. Being prepared won't stop surprises, but it makes them easier to handle. Avoid making big moves while things are still settling.
upright.health: A jolt may show you've been running on too little sleep, rest or support. Take it as a signal, not a failure. Make steadiness a priority with regular meals, early nights and quiet time while things settle. If something feels off, it's sensible to check in with a professional.
upright.family: A sudden change or revelation at home may upset routines or long-held assumptions. Feelings can run high for a while. Support one another and focus on what still holds, like shared meals, kindness and the bonds that matter. Big conversations can wait until everyone is calmer.
upright.general: A structure built on shaky ground is giving way. It's disruptive, and it's fine to feel rattled. It also frees you to build on more honest foundations. Look at what survives, because that's what was solid all along.
upright.yes_no: This card leans no. Expect some disruption, and don't count on the current plan staying as it is. If you can wait, let things settle and see what's left. A clearer answer usually comes once the dust clears.
upright.timing: The change itself comes quickly, and the clearing afterwards takes longer. The shock may pass in days, while rebuilding plays out over weeks or a season. Don't rush to fill the gap straight away. Let the new shape become clear first.
upright.advice: Let the shake-up show you what's truly solid. Hold on to people, values and routines that stay steady, and let go of what was only being propped up. Breathe, handle one practical step at a time, and ask for help. You can build again on firmer ground.
upright.thread: a sudden shake-up that reveals what is really solid

reversed.summary: The upheaval may be milder or slower than you feared. You might be looking at a near miss, or a change you've been putting off. Either way, you have room to repair and rebuild with care. Use the calm to strengthen what's weak instead of hoping it holds.
reversed.love: Small cracks are showing, like a repeated argument, a hurt nobody has mentioned, or growing distance. They're easier to mend now than later. Kind, honest words and a willingness to listen can do a lot. Don't wait for something bigger to force the conversation.
reversed.career: A near miss or a warning sign gives you a chance to strengthen your plans. Fix weak points while there's no crisis, whether that's an unclear process, a skill gap or a strained working relationship. Quiet preparation now saves stress later. Your steadiness will be noticed.
reversed.money: Calmly go over the weak spots in your budget while nothing is urgent. Check recurring costs, emergency savings and any commitments that feel fragile. Small adjustments now can prevent bigger stress later. Keep it practical and free of panic.
reversed.health: You may be coming through a stressful stretch and still feeling the effects. Rebuild your energy slowly, and avoid jumping straight back to full speed. Gentle routines, rest and support from people you trust all help. Recovery counts even when it's quiet.
reversed.family: Tension at home may be smaller than it feels, but avoiding it won't make it go away. Bring it up gently, at a calm moment, instead of letting it simmer. A short, honest conversation can stop a bigger rift. Patience on all sides will help.
reversed.general: Change is either delayed or softened. Avoiding it won't remove it, but you do have time to prepare and choose how it happens. Repair what you can and let go of what can't be saved. Rebuilding carefully is a strength.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed, leaning no. Go carefully and fix any weak spots first. If the foundations look sound after an honest check, the answer may soften over time. For now, prepare before you commit.
reversed.timing: Change comes slower and softer than you expected. Recovery happens in small, steady stages rather than one big turn. You may notice progress more when you look back. Give it a patient season.
reversed.advice: Rebuild slowly on firmer ground. Deal with the small cracks now, gently and honestly, before they grow. Don't put off a change you already know is needed. Steady repair is quieter than collapse and lasts much longer.
reversed.thread: a gentler shake-up and a chance to rebuild carefully

cards.name: The Star
cards.image_prompt: A kneeling figure pouring water into a pool and onto land, one large champagne-gold star and seven small ones above, peaceful midnight night.

upright.summary: Hope is coming back after a hard stretch. It's quiet, more like a clear evening sky after rain than fireworks. Healing is happening at its own pace, and you can trust it. Let yourself believe things can get better, because they're already starting to.
upright.love: Gentle optimism brings people closer. Trust feels possible again, whether that's in a new connection or with someone you've known a long time. Be open and sincere, and let the other person see the real you. Small honest moments matter more than grand gestures right now.
upright.career: Ideas and inspiration are flowing. Share them with quiet confidence, maybe in a meeting, a proposal or a side project you care about. Keep a steady, sustainable pace instead of burning out from excitement. Real progress builds from consistent effort.
upright.money: Things look brighter, even if the change is modest. Stick with a simple, steady plan instead of chasing quick wins or trends. Regular small habits add up over time. Let hope keep you consistent, not careless.
upright.health: Rest and renewal are working. Gentle routines, enough water, regular sleep and time outdoors, like a walk in the park or along the reservoir, can support how you feel. Don't push to make up for lost time. Let your energy come back on its own schedule.
upright.family: A calmer, kinder mood is settling at home. Small acts of care, like a shared meal, a check-in message or a kind word, help everyone feel more hopeful. Old tensions may ease with this lighter feeling. Enjoy the quiet goodwill while it grows.
upright.general: You're coming through something difficult with a fresh heart. You don't have to have everything figured out to feel hopeful. Trust the slow, steady renewal happening in you and around you. There's a quiet sense of direction now, and you can follow it.
upright.yes_no: This card leans yes. The outlook is hopeful, especially if you stay patient and sincere. Things may not happen instantly, but the direction is good. Go ahead with an open heart and realistic steps.
upright.timing: Change here is gradual and gentle. Improvement comes steadily over weeks and seasons rather than all at once. You may only see how far you've come when you look back. Keep tending it and trust the pace.
upright.advice: Keep hoping and keep going, one calm step at a time. Do small things that refill you, like rest, nature and honest conversations. Share your hopes with people who support you. Steady faith in yourself is enough for now.
upright.thread: renewed hope, healing and a quiet sense of direction

reversed.summary: Hope feels dim right now, but it hasn't gone. You may just be tired, stretched thin or disconnected from what usually lifts you. That isn't failure. It's a sign you need rest and support. The light comes back more easily once you've recovered a little.
reversed.love: When you feel low, it's tempting to pull away or expect the worst. Try not to give up on kindness. Small warm gestures, like a message, a shared drink or a moment of listening, can rekindle connection. Let someone close know you're having a hard time.
reversed.career: Your motivation may have dropped, and work may feel flat or pointless for a while. Think back to why you started and look for one part you still care about. Ease the pressure where you can and set smaller goals. Your drive usually returns once you're less drained.
reversed.money: Avoid making money decisions while you're in a gloomy mood, since pessimism and impulse can both lead you astray. Stick to essentials and keep things simple for now. Wait until you feel clearer before making changes. Things may look different once you've rested.
reversed.health: Fatigue and low spirits are telling you that you need rest and support. Be gentle with yourself and lower your expectations for a while. Talk to someone you trust, and if the heaviness lasts, reaching out to a professional is a caring step. Small comforts count.
reversed.family: Everyone at home may feel a bit flat or tired. Nobody needs to fix it in a big way. Simple shared moments, like a meal together, an evening walk or a favourite show, can lift the mood. Be patient with one another's low energy.
reversed.general: Discouragement is clouding your view right now. The hope is still there, just hard to see from where you're standing. Rest, reconnect with what matters to you, and look up again when you're less tired. This is a pause, not an ending.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed, leaning yes later. The basic outlook isn't bad, but now may not be the time to decide. Wait until you feel steadier and clearer. A yes made from a rested place will feel much more solid.
reversed.timing: Things are slow to lift. Renewal comes after you've rested, not before. Expect a gradual return over a season, with brighter days starting to show up more often. Don't force the pace.
reversed.advice: Rest first, then let a little light back in. Do one small thing each day that comforts or nourishes you. Reach out to someone instead of carrying it alone. Hope often comes back quietly once you stop demanding it.
reversed.thread: flagging hope that needs rest before it can return

cards.name: The Moon
cards.image_prompt: A full champagne-gold moon above a winding path between two towers, a dog and wolf howling, crayfish in a pool, misty midnight landscape.

upright.summary: Part of the picture is still hidden, and your mind may be filling the gaps with guesses that feel like facts. That's natural, but it can make small things look bigger or stranger than they are. Move slowly and notice which thoughts feel steady and which ones only show up when you're tired or anxious. Let things become clear in their own time instead of forcing an answer.
upright.love: Feelings may be hard to read right now, whether they're yours or the other person's. A late reply or a quiet evening can easily turn into a story you tell yourself, so be careful about reading meaning into silence. Ask gentle, open questions and give the other person room to answer honestly. If you're unsure what you feel yourself, it's fine to say so instead of pretending to be certain.
upright.career: Some information at work seems to be missing, delayed or unclear. Office talk and half-finished updates may be filling the gaps. Where you can, hold off on big commitments until you have the whole picture, and ask for things in writing when it matters. Trust your sense that something is off, but check it before you act on it.
upright.money: Be careful with any offer, deal or arrangement that feels vague or rushed. If the terms are hard to follow, that's a reason to slow down and ask more questions. Read the fine print, keep records of what was agreed, and don't let pressure or excitement replace clear details. A calm pause now can save you confusion later.
upright.health: Worry and broken sleep may be clouding your mood and energy. Late-night scrolling and going over the same thoughts again and again can make everything feel heavier than it is. Keep your daily routines steady and give yourself a real wind-down before bed, such as dimmer lights, a quiet drink or a short walk. If unease lasts, talking it through with someone you trust can help.
upright.family: There may be tension at home that nobody is naming. Moods can shift without a clear reason, and it's easy to guess wrongly about what someone else is thinking. Listen for what isn't being said, and give people a soft way to open up before you react. Keeping things calm and patient will do more good than pushing for answers.
upright.general: This is a time of fog, dreams and mixed signals. Not everything is what it first seems, and that includes your fears. Your intuition is active, so it's worth listening to, but it works best as a clue rather than a verdict. Give yourself permission not to have everything figured out yet.
upright.yes_no: Maybe. The answer isn't clear yet, and deciding now would mean relying on guesses. Wait for more facts, watch how things develop, and see whether your instinct still holds once you know more. A firmer answer is likely to come once the details are visible.
upright.timing: Slow and uncertain, a bit like waiting for morning mist to clear. Clarity tends to come after a few more nights of rest and some patient watching, not from pushing. Expect things to unfold bit by bit rather than all at once. Let the situation show itself before you try to set its pace.
upright.advice: Move slowly, check your facts, and treat your instincts as clues to look into rather than proof. Write down what you actually know and keep it separate from what you fear might be true. Look after your sleep and calm so your judgement stays clear. When the fog lifts, you'll be ready to act well.
upright.thread: a situation that is still foggy and asks for your patience

reversed.summary: The fog is starting to lift. Now that more of the truth is visible, what worried you looks smaller and easier to manage. Some of the fears you carried came from not knowing, not from anything actually going wrong. Let this relief settle in, while still paying attention to the details.
reversed.love: A misunderstanding may be about to clear up. A calm, honest conversation can bring real relief and show that the gap between you was smaller than it felt. Say plainly what you meant and listen to what they meant too. Things can feel lighter once nobody is guessing anymore.
reversed.career: Details that were confusing at work are starting to make sense. Instructions get clearer, the real priorities show up, and you can plan with more confidence. Go ahead with the work, but still double-check anything important before you sign off. Clarity is a good base to build on, not a reason to skip care.
reversed.money: Clarity is returning around figures, bills or paperwork. This is a good time to sort your records, confirm amounts and tidy up anything that was left vague. You may find things are more manageable than you feared. Keep your notes organised so this clearer picture stays clear.
reversed.health: Anxious thoughts may be easing, and sleep may start to feel more restful. Enjoy the lighter feeling, but don't assume the worry is gone for good. Keep up the habits that calm you, like steady routines, time outdoors and good rest. Small, regular care helps this calm last.
reversed.family: Something that was unsaid at home may finally come out. It may be uncomfortable for a moment, but it can clear the air. Take what's shared with kindness instead of defensiveness, so people feel safe being honest again. Over time, the house can feel easier to live in.
reversed.general: Illusions are fading and hidden matters are coming to the surface. You'll likely find that some of your worry was fear rather than fact. Things you couldn't see clearly before now have shape and edges you can work with. Use this clarity to make grounded choices.
reversed.yes_no: Leaning yes. Clarity is improving and the situation is becoming easier to judge. Before you commit, confirm the key facts so you're acting on what's true and not just on relief. Once that's done, moving forward looks reasonable.
reversed.timing: Gradual, like dawn rather than a switch. Things should brighten over the coming days and weeks as more information comes in. Each conversation or update adds a bit more light. Steady attention will serve you better than rushing.
reversed.advice: Let facts take the place of worry, and gently drop fears that no longer have anything feeding them. Write down what's now clear and act on it one step at a time. Stay honest in your conversations so nothing new gets murky. Allow yourself to feel the relief.
reversed.thread: confusion lifting and a truth becoming easier to see

cards.name: The Sun
cards.image_prompt: A radiant champagne-gold sun with a gentle face over a garden wall of sunflowers, a joyful child on a white horse, midnight edges fading into warm light.

upright.summary: Warmth, clarity and good energy are with you now. Things feel more open and honest, and your efforts are more likely to be noticed. This is a time to actually enjoy what's going well instead of waiting for the next worry. Share the good mood, because it tends to grow when it's shared.
upright.love: Affection comes easily and honestly. Whether you're single or attached, being openly glad and warm makes you easy to be close to. Plan something simple and fun together, or let yourself enjoy someone's company without overthinking it. Honest happiness is a gift you can give each other.
upright.career: Your work is visible and valued. Colleagues or managers may notice what you've delivered, so don't hide it out of modesty. Share your results clearly and with quiet pride, and give credit to the people who helped. Confidence now can open doors to the next step.
upright.money: A hopeful outlook supports sound choices right now. You may feel more settled and able to see real progress. Enjoy that, while keeping your simple, steady habits, like tracking what comes in and what goes out. Good times last longer when they rest on a clear routine.
upright.health: Energy and mood are lifting. Time outdoors, such as a morning walk by the park connector or an evening by the sea, can top up that brightness. Keep your rest regular and make room for play, laughter and movement you enjoy. Small habits of joy help hold this good spell in place.
upright.family: Home feels lighter, with more laughter and ease. It's a good time for a shared meal, a weekend outing or simply sitting together without rushing. Small celebrations, even ordinary ones, help everyone feel connected. Let the warmth reach the quieter family members too.
upright.general: Things are open, honest and bright. What you've been working on has room to grow, and people respond well to your openness. You don't have to make yourself smaller or hold back your happiness. Enjoy this season and let it remind you what's possible.
upright.yes_no: Yes. The signs are clearly positive and the situation supports you. Go ahead with an open heart and steady effort. Good outcomes look likely when you act with honesty and confidence.
upright.timing: Soon and steady. Good momentum is available now rather than somewhere far off. Things may move with a natural ease, like a clear morning after rain. Use this bright stretch while it's here.
upright.advice: Let yourself be seen and enjoy it. Share your warmth, your results and your thanks with the people around you. Spend time in daylight and in good company. Joy is worth taking seriously.
upright.thread: joy, clear success and warmth that you can openly enjoy

reversed.summary: A cloud is covering the light for now, but the sun is still there. Your mood, energy or results may lag behind what you hoped for. This is a short dip, not a lasting shadow. Be patient with yourself and keep doing the simple things that work.
reversed.love: A flat patch or a small dip in mood may be passing between you. Try not to read too much into a quiet week or a distracted moment. Keep things light, kind and easy, and make room for a little fun together. Warmth usually comes back when nobody forces it.
reversed.career: Recognition or success may arrive later than you hoped. Keep working steadily and let your results speak for you instead of overselling. Watch that confidence doesn't slide into skipping checks or promising too much. Patience now protects the success that's still on its way.
reversed.money: Optimism can make it easy to skip the details. Before you commit to anything, look at the numbers, terms and timelines with a calm eye. A positive outlook is helpful, but it works best alongside clear facts. Steady habits will carry you through this cloudy spell.
reversed.health: Energy may feel low or flat. Rest, daylight, water and small pleasures can gently bring it back. Don't push yourself to feel cheerful. Simply look after the basics. If low mood lingers, it's worth sharing with someone you trust.
reversed.family: Home may feel a bit dull or strained right now. Everyone may be tired or busy, and the usual warmth feels further away. A simple shared moment, like a meal, a show or a short walk, can warm things up again. Small gestures matter more than big plans.
reversed.general: Good things are delayed, not denied. Watch out for two extremes: being overconfident, or being gloomier than the facts call for. Keep a balanced view and do what you can each day. The brighter side of this situation is still within reach.
reversed.yes_no: Leaning yes, but with some delay. The outcome looks positive overall, though it may need more time or care than expected. Check the details and keep your expectations realistic. Patience is likely to pay off.
reversed.timing: A little slower than you'd like. Expect brighter days after a short wait rather than right away. Small signs of progress may show up before the bigger result. Keep a steady pace and let things ripen.
reversed.advice: Find one small joy today and let it count. Keep your expectations realistic and your effort steady. Don't let a cloudy patch convince you the sun has gone. Ground yourself in simple routines until the light returns.
reversed.thread: a temporary cloud, delayed success or a need to stay grounded

cards.name: Judgement
cards.image_prompt: An angel blowing a champagne-gold trumpet from the clouds, figures rising with open arms below, midnight sky with streaming light.

upright.summary: Judgement brings a clear inner call to look honestly at your past and step into a new chapter. You may suddenly see a pattern or truth that was hidden from you before. This is not about being judged harshly, but about understanding yourself more fully. With that clarity, you can make choices that fit who you are now.
upright.love: Fresh understanding can renew a bond that has felt stuck. Forgiveness, whether you give it or receive it, may open a real path forward. You might see an old relationship pattern clearly and decide to do things differently this time. Honest conversation now can lead to a deeper, more grown-up connection.
upright.career: A sense of calling may become sharper, showing you what kind of work truly matters to you. Review your path honestly: what has fulfilled you, and what has only kept you busy? You do not need to change everything at once. Answering the call with even one clear step can bring fresh energy and direction.
upright.money: Look back at your past money choices with honest eyes, but without shame. Notice what worked, what did not, and what you have learned along the way. Then make a fresh, realistic plan from where you stand today. This card favours a clean start built on lessons rather than regret.
upright.health: You may feel ready to change a habit for good, because you finally understand why it matters to you. Reflect on what your body and mind have been signalling, such as tiredness, tension or restlessness. Small, sustainable changes tend to last the longest. This is a good moment to begin.
upright.family: Old family matters may be revisited, this time with more maturity on all sides. A conversation that once felt impossible may now be calmer and more honest. Listening to each other's side of the story can bring real healing. Even partial understanding is a meaningful step forward.
upright.general: This is a moment of awakening and renewal. You see your own story more clearly and realise you are free to choose differently. The past becomes something to learn from rather than something to carry. Answering this call can feel both humbling and freeing.
upright.yes_no: Yes. This card leans towards answering the call and moving ahead. You likely already know, deep down, what you need to do. Trust that inner clarity and take the step, even if it feels big. The answer favours renewal over staying where you are.
upright.timing: A turning point is close. The decision you make matters more than the exact date it happens. When you feel that moment of clarity, act on it rather than waiting for perfect conditions. Things can move quickly once you commit.
upright.advice: Reflect honestly on where you have been, and forgive what you can, including yourself. Notice the step you keep hearing about in quiet moments. Then take it, even if it is a small one. Renewal begins with one honest choice.
upright.thread: an inner call to reflect, forgive and start a new chapter

reversed.summary: Self-criticism or doubt may be drowning out your inner call. You might be replaying old mistakes or waiting until you feel completely sure before you move. The call has not disappeared, but harshness towards yourself makes it hard to hear. Take the lesson from the past and let the rest go.
reversed.love: Old blame may be keeping hearts closed, whether it is aimed at a partner, an ex or yourself. Holding on to every past mistake makes it hard to move forward together. Kindness, including towards yourself, softens things on both sides. You do not have to forget, but you can choose to stop keeping score.
reversed.career: You may be ignoring what you really want from work because it feels risky or unfamiliar. Waiting for total certainty can keep you stuck for a long time. Instead, take one small step, such as a short course, a conversation or a side project. Action tends to quiet doubt far better than more thinking does.
reversed.money: Do not keep punishing yourself for past money mistakes. Regret uses up energy that could go into better choices now. Look at where you are today, accept it as your starting point, and plan from there. Steady progress is possible from any position.
reversed.health: Harsh self-talk can quietly drain your energy and make healthy changes feel heavier than they are. Notice how you speak to yourself when you slip up. Try treating yourself as you would a friend who is doing their best. Gentleness often makes good habits easier to keep.
reversed.family: Old grievances may still linger at home, colouring how people respond to one another. Bringing up the same history again rarely changes the outcome. Try to let it rest and focus on how you want things to go from here. A small act of goodwill can soften even a long-standing tension.
reversed.general: Hesitation is holding you back right now. The call to change has not gone away, but doubt keeps muting it. You may be asking for more proof than you really need. Recognising this pattern is already the first step out of it.
reversed.yes_no: Leaning yes, but first you need to quiet the doubt. The opportunity is still there and still right for you. What stands in the way is mainly hesitation and self-judgement. Once you settle that, you can move forward with a clearer heart.
reversed.timing: Slower for now, mostly because of second-guessing. Progress comes once you stop circling the decision and act on it. There is no need to wait for a perfect sign. The pace picks up as soon as you take the first real step.
reversed.advice: Be kind to your past self, who did their best with what they knew at the time. Take the lesson and leave the blame behind. Then choose one small, concrete step towards what you know you want. Let action, not doubt, have the final word.
reversed.thread: self-doubt muting a call you still need to answer

cards.name: The World
cards.image_prompt: A dancing figure within a champagne-gold laurel wreath, four symbolic creatures in the corners, star-filled midnight sky, sense of completion.

upright.summary: A long chapter is coming to a proper, satisfying close. When you look back, you can see how much ground you have covered and how much you have grown along the way. This is not luck; it is the sum of many ordinary days of effort. Let yourself feel the finish before rushing to the next thing.
upright.love: There is a growing sense of belonging, of being at home with someone. If you are together, the relationship may feel settled and whole, with less to prove and more to enjoy. If you are single, you may feel complete in yourself, which makes any future bond healthier. Savour the ease and say out loud what you appreciate.
upright.career: A major goal at work is reached or very close to it, whether that is a finished project, a qualification or a role you worked toward. Pause and acknowledge it properly instead of moving straight to the next target. Write down what made it succeed so you can carry those habits forward. The next chapter will start on firmer ground because of this one.
upright.money: Years or months of steady effort begin to show in your finances. You may feel more secure, or simply see that your habits have quietly worked. Enjoy the reward in a measured way that does not undo the progress. Take note of what helped, so the pattern can continue.
upright.health: Body and mind feel more in step with each other than they have in a while. Sleep, meals and movement may have settled into a rhythm that suits you. Keep the routines that brought you here rather than dropping them now that you feel better. Wholeness is maintained gently, day by day.
upright.family: Home feels connected and complete, with people more at ease with one another. A milestone such as a graduation, anniversary or reunion may be worth marking, even simply over a shared meal. These moments remind everyone what holds the family together. Take photos, tell stories and let the gathering be unhurried.
upright.general: Things are coming together in a way that feels earned. You have finished something real, and that completion opens a wider horizon than before. It is a natural time to look outward, travel in mind or body, and consider what larger circle you want to join. Closing well is what makes a good beginning possible.
upright.yes_no: Yes. This is one of the clearest positive signs, pointing to completion and things falling into place. The outcome you are asking about looks well supported, especially if you have already put in the work. Move forward with confidence while keeping your feet on the ground.
upright.timing: This marks the end of a long phase rather than a sudden turn. Results arrive as the natural fruit of steady effort over a season or more. Expect a feeling of arrival, then a short pause before the next cycle begins. Do not rush that pause.
upright.advice: Celebrate the finish and thank the people who helped you get here. Take time to reflect on what you learned, both the wins and the hard parts. Then, when you feel rested, begin again with that wisdom in hand. Every ending well done is quietly a new start.
upright.thread: a cycle reaching a full and satisfying completion

reversed.summary: You are close to the finish line, but a few loose ends are keeping the chapter open. It can feel frustrating to be so near and not quite done. The remaining tasks may be small, yet they matter for a real sense of closure. A little more steady effort will let you rest properly.
reversed.love: Something unresolved sits quietly between you and another person, or between you and the past. Before things can deepen or move on, it may need a gentle, honest conversation. Avoid pretending it is finished when it is not. Clearing the air kindly can make room for real closeness.
reversed.career: Finish what you started before taking on something new. It may be tempting to cut corners or hand over half-done work, but that tends to come back later. Look at the final details, documentation or follow-ups that still need attention. Completing them well protects your reputation and your peace of mind.
reversed.money: Small outstanding tasks may be weighing on you, such as forms, reminders or tidying up records. None may be urgent alone, but together they keep you feeling unsettled. Set aside a quiet hour to work through them one by one. You will likely feel lighter once the list is cleared.
reversed.health: You may feel tired just before the end of a demanding stretch. This is common, and it is a sign to pace yourself rather than push harder. Rest, eat properly and give yourself small breaks before the last push. If tiredness lingers, it is wise to check in with a professional.
reversed.family: A family matter may remain unsettled, perhaps an old disagreement or a plan never quite agreed. It could keep resurfacing until it is talked through. Choose a calm moment, listen first and aim for one clear agreement. Patience now helps the matter finally close.
reversed.general: Delays and unfinished business are holding a chapter open longer than you hoped. The ending is near, but not complete. Shortcuts may look attractive, yet they risk leaving you with more to redo. Slow, careful completion is the faster route in the end.
reversed.yes_no: Leaning yes, but not just yet. The outcome looks possible, yet a few steps still need finishing first. Tie up the remaining details and the answer becomes clearer and firmer. Rushing now could turn a yes into a delay.
reversed.timing: Slightly delayed rather than blocked. Completion arrives once the last details are dealt with, not before. Think in terms of a closing stretch that takes a little longer than planned. Steady attention shortens it.
reversed.advice: Close the loop on what is still open, even the tedious parts. Resist the shortcut that promises a quick finish but leaves gaps. Once it is truly done, allow yourself real rest. You will start the next thing lighter.
reversed.thread: loose ends that need tying up before a true finish

cards.name: Ace of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A single glowing wand sprouting gold leaves, held by a hand from midnight clouds, champagne-gold flame accents.

upright.summary: A fresh spark of energy and inspiration is arriving, and it feels lively. You may have an idea you cannot stop thinking about, or a sudden urge to try something new. This is a good moment to begin, because the enthusiasm itself is useful fuel. Give it a simple first step so it becomes something real instead of staying a pleasant thought.
upright.love: New attraction or renewed warmth may brighten your days. If you are with someone, a small change such as a new activity together can bring back some playfulness. If you are single, you may feel more open, confident and willing to say hello. Be warm and curious without rushing to decide what it all means.
upright.career: A new idea, project or direction feels ready to start. You may have more drive than usual and a clearer sense of what you want to build. Turn that energy into one practical first step, such as a short proposal, a draft or a conversation with the right person. Momentum grows best from action, even small action.
upright.money: A new opportunity may come into view, perhaps linked to a skill, an idea or a side interest. It is worth looking at, calmly and with your eyes open. Read the details, ask questions and check that it fits your situation before you commit to anything. Enthusiasm is a good starting point, but it does not replace clear information.
upright.health: Your motivation and energy are rising, so this is a good time to start a healthy habit. Choose something you can actually keep up, like a short daily walk, an earlier bedtime or regular stretch breaks at your desk. Starting gently helps the spark last instead of burning out after a week. Let enjoyment guide you as much as discipline.
upright.family: New energy or a fresh plan may liven up the home. It could be a weekend outing, a small project like reorganising a room, or a new family tradition. Invite others to share ideas so it feels like something you do together rather than your project alone. Enthusiasm spreads easily when people feel included.
upright.general: A creative or personal beginning is open to you now. The energy is real, but it needs a direction before it can turn into something lasting. Ask yourself what excites you most and what one step you could take this week. Acting early and small keeps the spark alive. Even a rough start teaches you more than waiting.
upright.yes_no: Yes. The energy here clearly favours starting and saying yes to something new. You have momentum behind you, and too much hesitation is likely to waste it. Move forward, keeping your first steps sensible and manageable. The enthusiasm you feel is a good sign that this is worth beginning.
upright.timing: Quick to begin. The spark is here now, and you can start soon if you act on it. Lasting results will come from steady effort over the following weeks and months. Think of this as the first light of a season, not the full harvest.
upright.advice: Act on the idea that makes you feel most alive, and start small. One clear step taken today is worth more than a perfect plan that stays in your head. Protect your enthusiasm by not loading it with too many goals at once. Let your first success build confidence for the next.
upright.thread: a fresh spark of energy and a chance to begin

reversed.summary: The spark is there, but it is hard to light. You may feel drawn to begin something yet find your energy flat or your timing off. That does not mean the idea is wrong. It may simply need more rest, preparation or clarity first. Treat this as a pause to gather fuel, not a closed door.
reversed.love: Interest may feel uneven, slow to start or hard to read. One person may be keener than the other, or both may be holding back out of caution. Give things room to grow without pushing for quick answers. At this stage, gentle consistency often does more than grand gestures.
reversed.career: A project may stall, start awkwardly or lose momentum after an exciting beginning. Rather than forcing it, step back and rest so you can see it more clearly. Review the plan, check what resources and support you actually need, and scale it down if necessary. A slower, better-prepared restart is often stronger than the first attempt.
reversed.money: This is not a time for rushed starts or quick decisions. If an idea or opportunity feels exciting but unclear, wait until the plan and the numbers make sense. Ask questions, read the fine print and give yourself time to think it over. Patience here protects both your peace of mind and your resources.
reversed.health: Your motivation may be lower than usual, and pushing hard could leave you more drained. Allow yourself proper rest, and notice what is quietly using up your energy. When you feel ready, ease back in with something very light and achievable. Being kind to yourself tends to rebuild energy faster than pressure does.
reversed.family: A plan at home may be slow to get going, perhaps because people are busy, tired or not fully on board. Pushing ahead alone could cause friction. Take time to agree on what everyone actually wants and what each person can contribute. With clearer agreement, the plan is more likely to take off.
reversed.general: A false start or a dip in motivation is holding things back for now. The idea is not wasted. It is only early or not yet well prepared. Use this pause to rest, reflect and sharpen the plan. When the spark returns, you will be in a better position to use it well, and the second start may feel much easier.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, but leaning yes in time. The energy behind this is good, but the moment is not quite right. Rest, clarify your plan and try again once you feel steadier. A second attempt has a better chance than forcing the first one. Treat this as a 'not yet' rather than a 'no'.
reversed.timing: Delayed, not cancelled. Expect a restart once you have rested and prepared more carefully. The energy may come back gradually, like a slow warm-up rather than a sudden burst. Watch for the point when the idea feels exciting again instead of heavy.
reversed.advice: Rest first, then try again with a clearer plan and a smaller first step. Notice what drained your energy last time and adjust for it. There is no prize for starting fastest. A well-timed beginning will take you further, so let yourself wait until the idea feels light again.
reversed.thread: a spark that needs rest, patience or a clearer plan

cards.name: Two of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A figure on a midnight castle wall holding a small golden globe, two wands beside them, gold-lit sea beyond.

upright.summary: You are looking ahead and weighing what comes next. Something good is already in your hands, and the question is how far you want to take it. A lot is open to you, but this calls for thought rather than impulse. It is a time for vision, research and honest reflection on what you really want.
upright.love: You may be thinking about where a relationship is heading, or what kind of partnership you want in the future. These thoughts are worth sharing rather than keeping to yourself. Talk openly about your hopes, your timelines and the life you each picture. Getting clear now helps both of you make choices that fit.
upright.career: Plan your next move with care. A bigger path, such as a new role, further study or more responsibility, may be possible if you prepare well. Look at the skills you have, the gaps you could fill and the people who could advise you. Right now, strategy matters more than speed.
upright.money: Think long term rather than reacting to the moment. A simple written plan, even a rough one, can guide your everyday choices and cut down on second-guessing. Consider what you want your money to support over the next few years. If decisions feel complex, it is sensible to seek qualified guidance.
upright.health: Set a realistic, longer-term goal for your wellbeing instead of chasing quick results. Think about how you want to feel a few months from now and which habits would support that. Steady planning tends to beat sudden bursts that fade. Choose one area to focus on first and build from there.
upright.family: Family plans may need careful thought, such as a move, care arrangements or a change in how the household runs. Different family members may hope for different things, so talk through the options together. Gather information before anyone commits. A shared plan tends to last longer than one made in a hurry.
upright.general: You have a solid base and are deciding where to go from here. Vision matters now, and it works best when tied to practical steps. Look at the bigger picture, then narrow it down to what matters most. The options are real, and the real work is choosing well.
upright.yes_no: Maybe. The path looks open, but it is not yet a firm yes. You need more planning, information or reflection before you can commit with confidence. Once the plan is clearer, the answer may well tip in your favour. For now, keep the question open while you prepare.
upright.timing: Medium term. This is a planning phase that comes before action. Expect things to take shape over weeks or months rather than days. Use the time to prepare, so you are ready when the moment to move arrives.
upright.advice: Map out the path before you set off, and be honest about what you want. Gather the information you need, then commit to the first real step. Do not wait for every detail to be perfect. A clear direction plus one concrete action is enough to begin.
upright.thread: planning ahead and weighing a wider path before you move

reversed.summary: Uncertainty may be keeping you somewhere familiar, even though part of you wants more. Fear of change or unclear plans can make staying put feel safer than it really is. It is fine to move slowly, but it helps to keep moving. A small, deliberate step can break the feeling of being stuck.
reversed.love: Mixed feelings or worry about change may be clouding your view. Before you talk with a partner or someone you like, be honest with yourself about what you want. Once you are clearer, a calm conversation can ease the uncertainty. Avoid making big promises or demands while you still feel torn.
reversed.career: A plan may feel unclear, or so big that you don't know where to start. Break it into small, clear steps you can manage alongside your daily work. You may also be playing it safer than your abilities call for. Notice where caution is wise and where it is just habit.
reversed.money: Worry can keep you frozen, avoiding decisions that would actually help. Review your options calmly, perhaps by writing them down side by side. Choose a modest, sensible next step instead of waiting for a perfect answer. If things feel complicated, qualified advice can bring clarity.
reversed.health: Fear of change, or of not being able to keep it up, may be blocking a healthy habit. Begin with something so small it feels almost too easy, such as five minutes of stretching or one extra glass of water. Small wins help you trust yourself. Let progress be quiet and gradual.
reversed.family: Different views may be stalling a decision at home. Everyone may be waiting for someone else to choose, or holding tightly to their own preference. Listen first so each person feels heard. Then look for one small step everyone can agree on, even if the larger decision takes longer.
reversed.general: Indecision or playing small may be holding you back. The options you were considering have not disappeared. They are simply waiting for you. Ask yourself what is really making you hesitate, because naming the fear often makes it easier to get past. Even a tentative choice is better than standing still for too long.
reversed.yes_no: Maybe, leaning towards 'not yet'. The outcome is still uncertain because the plan itself is unclear. Work out what you want and what the first step would be before you decide. With more clarity, the answer could change. For now, hold off on committing until the direction feels firmer.
reversed.timing: Slow for now. Progress tends to come once you stop circling and choose a direction. The delay is mostly about your readiness, not outside obstacles. Once you make a clear choice, things can start to move, often faster than you expect.
reversed.advice: Choose one small step and take it, even if the whole plan is not yet clear. Waiting for complete certainty may keep you in the same place. Give yourself permission to adjust as you go. Moving forward teaches you things that thinking alone cannot.
reversed.thread: indecision or fear of change that keeps a plan on hold

cards.name: Three of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A figure watching golden ships sail across a midnight sea, three wands planted on a cliff, stars above.

upright.summary: The effort you put in earlier is starting to pay off, and your plans now reach further than they did at the start. You can see the general direction things are heading, even if the details are still filling in. This is a good moment to look ahead with confidence while staying involved in the day-to-day work. Momentum is building, and your job is to keep it moving steadily.
upright.love: A relationship may be growing with a hopeful, forward-looking feeling. You might be making plans together, managing distance, or talking about what a shared future could look like. If you are single, someone from a wider circle, perhaps from abroad or met through travel or work, could catch your interest. Keep the conversations open and enjoy the sense of looking ahead together.
upright.career: The groundwork you laid is beginning to show results, and people may be noticing. This is a sensible time to consider a wider reach, such as a new client group, another team, a regional role or a project that builds on what already works. Base your next step on evidence from what has gone well so far. Keep track of your progress so you can explain it clearly when opportunities come up.
upright.money: Steady effort and patience may bring returns over time rather than all at once. Think in seasons instead of weeks, and give your plans room to mature. It helps to review what is working and keep doing it consistently. Avoid getting distracted by others' quick wins; your slower, careful approach suits this card.
upright.health: Your energy feels outward-moving and hopeful, and you may want to take on more. To sustain this, keep a steady routine for sleep, meals and movement, especially when your schedule fills up. A walk outdoors, perhaps along a park connector or the waterfront, can help you clear your head and plan. Pace yourself so enthusiasm does not turn into tiredness.
upright.family: Family matters may stretch across distance, such as relatives overseas, a child studying away, or plans for a move. Regular contact and clear sharing of intentions will help everyone feel included. A video call or a shared group chat update can do more than you expect. Talk early about plans so nobody feels surprised later.
upright.general: You have set things in motion and can now watch them travel further. The view ahead is wider than it was, and new possibilities are starting to appear. Stay steady and observant rather than rushing to the next big leap. Small, sensible follow-through will carry this momentum a long way.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. Progress is already underway, and the conditions look favourable for continuing. It still depends on your steady follow-through rather than luck alone. Keep doing the practical next step and the answer is likely to keep moving in your favour.
upright.timing: Results tend to build gradually after a good start. Expect noticeable movement over a few months rather than overnight. Think of this as a season of growth, where patience and consistency matter more than speed. Signs of progress may arrive in stages.
upright.advice: Keep your eyes on the bigger picture while handling the next sensible task in front of you. Check in on what is working and build on it instead of starting over. Stay open to options further away than you first imagined. Trust the progress you have made, and keep tending it.
upright.thread: early effort starting to travel further than you expected

reversed.summary: Plans are moving more slowly than you hoped, and it may be hard to see the wider picture right now. Pushing harder is unlikely to speed things up and may only add frustration. This is a pause that invites you to check your assumptions and fix any gaps. The goal is still there; the route or timeline may need adjusting.
reversed.love: Expectations about timing, distance or the future may not quite match between you. One person may be ready to plan ahead while the other needs more time. Talk openly and calmly about what each of you actually wants rather than guessing. Clear, kind conversation can turn a frustrating wait into better understanding.
reversed.career: A delay or setback may be giving you time to spot what was missed. Before moving forward, review the plan, the resources and the people involved. Small corrections now can prevent bigger problems later. Treat this as a chance to strengthen your foundation rather than proof that the idea was wrong.
reversed.money: Returns may be slower than you expected, which can be disappointing. Resist the urge to chase quick wins to make up for it. Instead, review your plan calmly and see whether expectations need resetting. Patience and careful record-keeping will serve you better than rushed decisions.
reversed.health: Frustration from waiting may be wearing on your energy and mood. Rest, gentle routines and small daily wins can help more than forcing the pace. Notice if stress is affecting your sleep or appetite, and make room to recover. Speak to someone you trust if the waiting feels heavy.
reversed.family: Plans involving family or distance may stall, such as a trip, a visit or a move. Be patient and clear about what each person can realistically do. Avoid blaming anyone for delays that may be outside their control. Keeping communication warm will help everyone get through the wait.
reversed.general: Waiting has narrowed your outlook, and it may feel like nothing is moving. The goal has not disappeared, only the timeline has changed. Step back and look again at the bigger picture. A refreshed view may show options you overlooked.
reversed.yes_no: This leans mixed to no for now. The outcome may still happen, but later than you hoped or in a different form. Use the delay to adjust your approach. Asking again after some changes may bring a clearer answer.
reversed.timing: Expect slower progress and a longer wait than planned. This is a season for refining rather than racing ahead. Movement is likely to return once gaps are addressed. Give it time, and use that time well.
reversed.advice: Adjust the plan instead of abandoning it. Look at what was missed, ask for input, and widen your view again. Small corrections now can restore momentum later. Be patient with yourself while you do this work.
reversed.thread: a delay asking you to refine plans rather than force them

cards.name: Four of Wands
cards.image_prompt: Four wands forming a garland arch of gold flowers, figures celebrating under a midnight sky with lanterns.

upright.summary: A milestone has arrived, and it deserves a proper pause to appreciate it. Home and community feel steady, warm and supportive. This card invites you to recognise what has been built and share the moment with others. Stability here gives you a good base for whatever comes next.
upright.love: This is a happy phase for relationships, whether that means deepening commitment, meeting each other's families or simply enjoying time together. Gatherings and shared celebrations may bring you closer. If you are single, social events and friends' occasions could bring pleasant connections. Let yourself enjoy the warmth without overthinking it.
upright.career: A stage of work has been completed, and it is worth marking. Thank the people who helped, and take a moment with your team to recognise the effort. A good working atmosphere is a strength you can build on. Note what made this stage succeed so you can repeat it.
upright.money: Your situation may feel more stable and secure for now. Enjoy this with gratitude, and celebrate in ways that fit your means. A simple meal with loved ones can mean as much as something lavish. Keeping things modest helps the stability last.
upright.health: You may feel more settled and supported, which helps your energy. Time with people you like, shared meals and relaxed evenings can lift your mood. Let yourself rest after effort rather than moving straight on. A sense of belonging is good for your wellbeing now.
upright.family: This is a good time for a family meal, a festive gathering or marking a home milestone. Warmth and belonging are strong, and people may be glad to come together. Festivals like Hari Raya, Deepavali or Chinese New Year can feel especially meaningful. Include those who are often left out, and enjoy the shared moment.
upright.general: Something has landed safely, and you can stop to enjoy it. The foundation feels firm and the people around you are supportive. This is a natural point for appreciation before the next chapter. Let the good feeling sink in.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. The ground is stable and the people around you are supportive. Conditions favour a positive outcome. Go ahead with a grateful and steady attitude.
upright.timing: This points to a natural resting point, often around a gathering, festival or the end of a stage. Things feel settled for a while. It is a time to pause and enjoy rather than rush ahead. The next phase can begin once you have marked this one.
upright.advice: Pause and celebrate how far you have come. Include the people who helped you get here, and thank them sincerely. Enjoy the stability without needing to fill it straight away. Let this moment give you strength for what follows.
upright.thread: a milestone worth celebrating with people who matter

reversed.summary: Home or group life may feel slightly unsettled, with plans shifting or tension sitting just beneath the surface. Nothing may be seriously wrong, but things feel less comfortable than usual. Small acts of kindness and patience can help ease the atmosphere. This is a period of transition rather than a breakdown.
reversed.love: Shared plans may change or be postponed, which can feel disappointing. Try not to read too much meaning into it. Stay gentle and keep talking about what each of you needs. Quiet moments together may matter more than big occasions right now.
reversed.career: Team morale may feel uneven, or a celebration may be delayed. Some colleagues might feel overlooked or tired. Reconnecting with people one by one can help more than a big group event. Acknowledge effort even when the formal recognition is late.
reversed.money: Keep spending on celebrations and home improvements modest for now. Plans may shift, and flexibility will help. Focus on what genuinely brings comfort rather than appearances. Review commitments calmly before adding new ones.
reversed.health: An unsettled home atmosphere may leave you more tired than usual. Make one part of your day calm, such as a quiet morning tea or an evening walk. Protect your rest even if things around you feel busy. Small routines can restore a sense of steadiness.
reversed.family: Tension or change at home, such as a move, renovation or a gathering that falls through, may unsettle people. Listen before reacting, and allow everyone to share how they feel. Avoid making big decisions in the heat of the moment. Patience and small kindnesses can rebuild warmth.
reversed.general: Your foundation is in transition, and it may feel less secure than before. This does not mean it is lost; it can be rebuilt with care. Pay attention to what needs mending. Steady effort will bring back a sense of home.
reversed.yes_no: This leans mixed. The outcome is possible, but the setting needs to settle first. Address any tension or uncertainty before moving ahead. A clearer answer is likely once things calm down.
reversed.timing: Things may take longer while arrangements shift. Allow time for people and plans to settle. Rushing may only add stress. The celebration or milestone can still come, just later.
reversed.advice: Focus on creating calm at home before anything else. Listen, be kind and keep plans flexible. Small steps toward stability will help more than grand gestures. Once things settle, you can celebrate properly.
reversed.thread: a need to settle your home or group before celebrating

cards.name: Five of Wands
cards.image_prompt: Five figures crossing golden wands in playful sparring under midnight blue, gold sparks flying.

upright.summary: Many viewpoints are competing for attention, and tempers may be shorter than usual. The situation is more noisy than dangerous. Handled well, this friction can sharpen ideas and bring out better solutions. Staying calm and fair will help you come through it well.
upright.love: Small disagreements may come up more often, often over minor things. Listen more than you argue, and avoid turning conversations into contests. Playful energy can be fun if both of you keep it light. Remember you are on the same side even when you disagree.
upright.career: Competition, crowded meetings or many voices pushing ideas may make work feel lively. Stay fair, keep your focus on your own contributions and avoid getting pulled into office politics. Healthy debate can improve a project if people stay respectful. Use clear facts to support your points.
upright.money: Many people may have opinions about how you should handle money. Listen politely but keep your own plan steady. Comparing yourself with others can create needless pressure. Make choices based on your own situation, not the loudest voice.
upright.health: You may feel restless or wired, with energy that needs an outlet. Physical movement, like a brisk walk, a swim or a game with friends, can help work it off. Watch for tension building up through the day. Make time to wind down before sleep.
upright.family: Household opinions may clash over small matters such as chores, plans or schedules. Let everyone speak before deciding anything. A fair process often matters more than the final outcome. Keep humour close and remember these clashes usually pass.
upright.general: Things feel scrappy and busy, with everyone pushing to be heard. It is more competitive than harmful. Approach it with patience and a sense of perspective. The challenge can make you stronger and clearer.
upright.yes_no: This is mixed. The outcome is possible, but expect some jostling, competition or debate along the way. There is no clear, easy run. Persistence and fairness will improve your chances.
upright.timing: This points to a busy, messy stretch that usually passes once views have been aired. Things may feel chaotic for a while. Progress returns as people find common ground. Ride it out calmly.
upright.advice: Treat the challenge as practice rather than a battle. Stay respectful, listen well and keep your focus. Use friction to improve ideas rather than win arguments. Calm confidence will serve you best.
upright.thread: lively friction that can sharpen ideas if handled calmly

reversed.summary: Tension may be easing, or it may simply be pushed out of sight. Either way, there is less open conflict than before. Calm, honest conversation can help things settle properly. Notice whether real peace is forming or issues are just being avoided.
reversed.love: A disagreement may be cooling down. Make peace kindly, but do not bury things that still matter to you. A gentle conversation about what happened can prevent it from returning. Real closeness comes from understanding, not silence.
reversed.career: Look for common ground with colleagues rather than staying in separate camps. Avoid letting silent resentment build within the team. A short, honest check-in can clear the air. Cooperation will move work forward more than quiet tension.
reversed.money: Step back from stressful comparisons with friends or colleagues. Focus on your own situation and what truly matters to you. Avoid making choices just to keep up. Quiet clarity will bring more peace than competition.
reversed.health: Held-in tension may show up as tight shoulders, headaches or restless sleep. Find a safe way to release it, such as gentle exercise, journaling or talking with someone you trust. Notice what you have been holding back. Letting it out can ease your energy.
reversed.family: Someone at home may be avoiding a topic. A gentle, private conversation may help more than a group discussion. Choose a calm moment and listen without judging. Small steps toward honesty can restore trust.
reversed.general: The conflict is either resolving or going underground. Pay attention to which one is happening. If it is resolving, support it with kindness. If it is hidden, find a gentle way to bring it into the open.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed, leaning toward yes if people are willing to talk honestly. The outcome depends on whether tension is resolved or avoided. Open communication will improve your chances. Silence may keep things stuck.
reversed.timing: Things tend to calm in the near term if the issue is faced directly. Avoidance may stretch the tension longer. A simple conversation can speed up resolution. Peace follows honesty.
reversed.advice: Seek agreement rather than victory. Be honest but kind, and invite others to share their side. Look for small points of common ground. A lasting truce is built through understanding.
reversed.thread: a truce that needs honest talk to hold

cards.name: Six of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A rider on a white horse with a golden laurel wreath on a wand, crowd under midnight sky, gold banners.

upright.summary: The work you have been doing, often without anyone watching, is starting to show. People around you are noticing, and a win or a moment of real recognition may be close. You are allowed to enjoy this without brushing it off or making it smaller than it is. Let the good feeling settle in, because it is fuel for whatever comes next.
upright.love: You may feel appreciated, attractive and more sure of yourself in matters of the heart. If you are with someone, they may tell you plainly that they value you, or show it in small, everyday ways. If you are single, your confidence makes you easier to approach. Let yourself be seen as you are, without trying to put on a show.
upright.career: A compliment from a manager, a successful presentation, a good appraisal or a promotion-type moment may be on its way. Accept it graciously instead of deflecting it with jokes or modesty. Name the teammates who helped, because sharing credit builds trust that lasts longer than any single win. This is also a good time to note what worked so you can repeat it.
upright.money: Steady, careful effort may start to bring visible results, such as a bonus, a finished goal or simply a healthier balance than before. Enjoy the progress and mark it in a way that feels right to you. There is no need to prove anything to anyone with how you spend. Quiet satisfaction is usually worth more than a flashy gesture.
