upright.health: Your mood and confidence are lifting, and that can give you more energy for the routines that support you. Use the momentum to keep steady habits, like regular meals, a walk after dinner or a sensible bedtime. Feeling good is easier to keep than to rebuild. Notice what helped you get here and protect it.
upright.family: Someone at home may be proud of you, or a relative may have news that deserves a proper celebration. A family meal or a simple message of congratulations can mean a lot. Share the good mood generously, including with the quieter members of the family. Recognition passed around the dinner table tends to bring people closer.
upright.general: A stretch of effort is turning into results and a real boost in confidence. Others are beginning to see what you have built, and you can see it more clearly too. This is a moment to stand a little taller without becoming boastful. Let it remind you that steady work does pay off.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. The signs point towards a good outcome, especially where you have already put in honest effort. Others are likely to respond well to what you bring. Go ahead with reasonable confidence while staying gracious.
upright.timing: Recognition usually arrives after a period of steady work, and that period may be ending now. Things are likely to come together fairly soon rather than in the distant future. Watch for a turning point after a long stretch of effort. When it comes, it may feel like the season has quietly changed.
upright.advice: Let yourself enjoy this win fully instead of rushing on to the next goal. Thank the people who supported you, by name if you can. Stay humble, but do not shrink. Your confidence is earned and useful.
upright.thread: recognition arriving for effort you have steadily and quietly put in

reversed.summary: Recognition may be slow to come, or you may be doubting yourself even when things are going reasonably well. It can sting to work hard and hear nothing back. Still, your value does not rise and fall with other people's applause. The progress you have made is real whether or not anyone says so.
reversed.love: You may be craving reassurance and wondering whether you are truly valued. Rather than testing your partner or waiting for them to guess, ask honestly for what would help you feel secure. Notice too whether you are comparing your relationship with what others post online. Plain, kind words usually work better than hints.
reversed.career: Your contribution may go unmentioned, or credit may land with someone else for now. Keep doing careful work and keep a simple record of what you have delivered, with dates and outcomes. This makes appraisal conversations easier and calmer. Be wary of letting frustration turn into self-promotion that puts colleagues off.
reversed.money: Be careful of spending to impress people or to prove that you are doing well. Upgrades, treats for show or keeping pace with friends can quietly drain your savings. Ask yourself who a purchase is really for. Progress you can actually feel matters more than progress others can see.
reversed.health: Self-doubt can wear you down more than you expect, affecting sleep and mood. Try noticing what you have done each day, not only what is unfinished. A short list of small wins can steady you. If low feelings linger, talking to someone you trust can help.
reversed.family: You may feel taken for granted at home, as if your efforts go unnoticed. Instead of keeping score silently, say plainly and kindly what you need, perhaps a thank-you or more shared help. Family members are often unaware rather than uncaring. One honest conversation can shift a lot.
reversed.general: The win may be quieter than you hoped, or pride and comparison may be getting in the way of enjoying it. Either way, progress still counts. This is a time for inner steadiness rather than outer proof. Building a sense of worth that does not need an audience will serve you for years.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed. Real progress is happening, but it may not be recognised or rewarded just yet. The answer may be yes in substance and slower in visible results. Keep going and do not judge the outcome too early.
reversed.timing: Recognition is moving more slowly than you would like. It may arrive later, or in a smaller form than expected. Try not to measure your progress by when others notice it. This season is for quiet building.
reversed.advice: Value your own progress before looking for anyone else to confirm it. Keep a record of your efforts and look at it when doubt creeps in. Drop comparisons that only make you feel small. Steady self-respect lasts longer than praise.
reversed.thread: quiet progress that does not yet need anyone's applause

cards.name: Seven of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A figure on a midnight hilltop holding one golden wand against six rising below, determined pose, gold rim light.

upright.summary: You may find yourself needing to defend something that matters to you, such as a decision, a boundary or a belief. Others might question it or push against it. Calm confidence will serve you better than raising your voice. You hold the ground you have earned, and you can hold it steadily.
upright.love: Healthy boundaries in a relationship may be tested, whether by a partner, family or outside opinions. Protect them kindly but clearly, explaining what you need without blaming. Standing firm is not the same as being cold. A partner who respects you will usually respect a clear and gentle no.
upright.career: Your ideas or position at work may be challenged by colleagues or competitors. Hold steady on the points that genuinely matter and back them up with facts. You do not need to win every argument to be respected. Quiet conviction often earns more trust than forceful debate.
upright.money: Others may pressure you to spend, lend or join something that does not fit your plans. Stick with the budget and decisions you made when you were thinking clearly. A polite, firm no is enough explanation. Protecting your plan now saves stress later.
upright.health: Your rest and routines may be crowded out by work, social plans or other people's needs. Treat your sleep, meals and quiet time as worth defending. Saying no to one late night can protect a whole week. Your energy is a limited resource, so guard it calmly.
upright.family: You may need to turn down a family expectation, such as a plan, a role or an opinion about your life. Be firm and respectful, acknowledging that they likely mean well. You can honour your family and still make your own choices. Keep your tone gentle and your answer clear.
upright.general: You are holding a position and others are testing it. This is uncomfortable but not a crisis. Stay grounded, know your reasons and avoid getting drawn into every challenge. Holding steady now builds confidence you will draw on later.
upright.yes_no: This is mixed, leaning towards yes if you are willing to hold your ground. The outcome depends on your persistence when challenged. If the matter truly matters to you, it may be worth the effort. If you are unsure, decide first how much you are prepared to defend.
upright.timing: This is a testing phase that tends to last as long as the pressure does. Things may not settle immediately, but they will ease once your position is clear. Steady effort shortens the season. Expect some back and forth before calm returns.
upright.advice: Stand firm on what matters, and stay kind while you do it. Know your reasons so you do not need to argue loudly. Let small challenges pass. Keep your energy for the stands that count.
upright.thread: a position worth defending calmly and without hostility

reversed.summary: You may be worn out from defending too much for too long. Not every challenge needs a response, and not every point is worth the fight. Alternatively, you might feel like giving up on everything at once. The healthier path lies in between: choose the stands that truly matter.
reversed.love: You may be holding on tightly to being right, which can leave both of you tired and guarded. Try softening a little, listening more and letting minor disagreements go. Defensiveness often hides hurt, so it may help to name what is really bothering you. Connection grows when both people feel safe.
reversed.career: You might be carrying too much, or defending every decision as if it were under attack. Ask for help, share the load and let some points go. Being stretched thin can make you sharper with colleagues than you intend. Protecting your energy is part of doing good work.
reversed.money: Commitments that once made sense may now be draining you. Look at what you can simplify, and avoid overextending just to keep up with others. Pulling back is not failure. A lighter set of obligations can bring real relief.
reversed.health: Exhaustion and constant defensiveness are signs that you need rest. Try not to wait until you are completely depleted before slowing down. Small breaks, earlier nights and less arguing online can make a difference. If tiredness persists, it is worth checking in with someone you trust.
reversed.family: Ongoing family debates may be leaving you drained. Pick the one issue that genuinely matters and let the others rest for now. Peace at home sometimes means agreeing to disagree. You do not have to win every conversation over dinner.
reversed.general: You are overwhelmed, or tempted to give in on everything just to make the pressure stop. Neither extreme is necessary. Step back, recover a little and then decide what is still worth holding. Clarity comes more easily once you have rested.
reversed.yes_no: This leans no for now. You may be too stretched to see this through well at the moment. Rest and refocus before committing to more. The answer may change once your energy returns.
reversed.timing: Things are likely to slow down until you recover your strength. Pushing through now may only prolong the struggle. Give yourself a quieter season first. Progress resumes more easily after rest.
reversed.advice: Rest, and keep only the stands that truly matter. Let go of battles that cost more than they are worth. Ask for support where you can. You do not need to defend everything alone.
reversed.thread: exhaustion from over-defending, and a need to choose battles

cards.name: Eight of Wands
cards.image_prompt: Eight golden wands flying in parallel across a midnight sky, trailing champagne-gold light streaks.

upright.summary: Things are moving quickly now. News, replies or progress may arrive faster than you expected. What felt stuck is starting to flow, and several pieces may fall into place at once. Stay alert, keep your communication clear and be ready to act when the opening comes.
upright.love: Messages and feelings may flow easily right now, and a connection could develop quickly. Conversations feel lively and things may pick up pace. Enjoy the energy, but check that the other person is moving at the same speed as you. Clear, honest messages help the momentum feel good for both of you.
upright.career: Momentum at work is strong, with emails, approvals or opportunities arriving in quick succession. Act while things are moving, and respond promptly to keep projects going. Fast-moving situations can lead to misunderstandings, so keep updates short and clear. Staying organised helps you make the most of this burst.
upright.money: Money matters, such as paperwork, applications or arrangements, may move faster than usual. That can be welcome, but speed is no reason to skip the details. Read everything properly before you agree to anything. Being quick and careful together is the best approach here.
upright.health: Your energy may feel high and your days busy, with lots going on. It's easy to run on adrenaline and forget the basics. Remember to pause, drink enough water, eat proper meals and get enough sleep. Short breaks help you keep up the pace without burning out.
upright.family: Quick news, sudden plans or last-minute arrangements may involve your family. Things like visits, gatherings or changes to the schedule might come up with little warning. Keep everyone in the loop, perhaps through a family chat, so nobody feels left out. A little flexibility makes the busy patch easier for everyone.
upright.general: After a period of being stuck, a burst of movement clears the way. Things line up and start moving fast. This is a good time to act decisively, follow up on messages and push projects forward. Stay focused so the speed works for you rather than scattering you.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. Things are moving in your favour, and an answer or result may come quickly. The way is clearer than it has been. Act promptly and keep your communication clear to make the most of it.
upright.timing: The pace here is fast. Things that have been waiting may move quickly, often sooner than you'd expect. This is a short, active stretch rather than a slow season. Be ready to respond, since openings may not stay open for long.
upright.advice: Move with the flow and stay alert to new messages and openings. Respond promptly and keep things simple. Don't let speed push you into skipping the important details. Use the momentum while it's here.
upright.thread: fast-moving news and momentum that favour quick, clear action

reversed.summary: Things may feel slow, scattered or tangled right now. Messages might be delayed, plans may cross, or you may be juggling too much at once. This isn't a dead end, just a pause. Use it to get organised, clear up misunderstandings and get ready for when things pick up again.
reversed.love: Mixed signals, late replies or messages that get misread may cause some confusion. Instead of guessing what the other person meant, ask clearly and kindly. Try not to read too much into silence, as people are sometimes simply busy. Slowing down can help you both get back on the same page.
reversed.career: Approvals, replies or projects may be taking longer than planned. Waiting can still be useful time. Tidy up loose ends, update your documents and prepare for the next push. Following up politely in writing can prevent crossed wires.
reversed.money: Matters may be delayed, or the details may not be clear yet. Avoid rushing into decisions just to end the waiting. Ask questions, check what's still missing and give yourself time to understand the situation. Patience now can save you trouble later.
reversed.health: Scattered energy and too many tasks at once can leave you feeling tired and unsettled. Try focusing on one thing at a time, and take breaks before you feel worn out. Simple routines can bring back a sense of steadiness. Notice where your energy is leaking and protect it.
reversed.family: Miscommunication may cause small mix-ups at home, such as wrong times, missed messages or plans that clash. Confirm arrangements in writing, maybe in the family group chat, so everyone has the same details. Stay patient when things get muddled. A calm check-in clears up most confusion.
reversed.general: Momentum has stalled for now, or too many things are going on at once to make real progress. This is a cue to slow down and sort out your priorities. Clear up any unclear messages and finish what you can. Once things are untangled, movement usually comes back.
reversed.yes_no: This leans no for now. Timing and communication need some work before things can move forward smoothly. It's more a 'not yet' than a firm no. Clear up the details and ask again once things settle.
reversed.timing: Things are slower than expected, so allow extra time. Delays may come from waiting on others or from crossed communication. Use the slower pace to prepare. When things do pick up, you'll be ready to move.
reversed.advice: Slow down and focus on one thing at a time. Clear up any unclear messages before you assume the worst. Use the pause to organise and prepare. Momentum tends to return once you've cleared the clutter.
reversed.thread: a pause to sort out scattered energy and unclear messages

cards.name: Nine of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A weary figure leaning on a golden wand before eight others, bandaged but upright, midnight dusk glow.

upright.summary: You're tired, but you're still on your feet, and the end of this stretch is nearer than it feels from the inside. You've kept going through setbacks, and that already shows what you're made of. This card doesn't ask you to be fearless. It asks you to stay steady a bit longer. Think of the effort so far as proof you can finish, not a reason to doubt yourself.
upright.love: Old disappointments have taught you useful things about what you'll accept and what you won't. Hold on to those lessons, but don't let them turn into a wall that keeps everyone out. Being careful and being open can go together. If someone is showing up consistently, let them come a little closer, at a pace you can manage.
upright.career: A project, deadline, or demanding season at work is close to done. One more steady push, paced well rather than rushed, may get it over the line. Keep track of what's left so the final tasks feel finite rather than endless. Your persistence has probably been noticed more than you think, even if nobody has said so yet.
upright.money: The careful habits you built during a tighter period are protecting you now. This isn't the time to relax them just because things feel slightly easier. Keep tracking spending and sticking to the limits you set for yourself. Steady routines give you a cushion when surprises come, and they let you think clearly instead of anxiously.
upright.health: Your stamina is real, but it isn't endless, and this card is a gentle reminder of that. While you finish this demanding stretch, protect the basics: regular meals, enough water, decent sleep and a little movement. Small breaks during the day matter more than one big rest you keep putting off. Notice early signs of strain and respond to them kindly.
upright.family: You may be the one holding the household together right now, juggling schedules, moods and chores while others lean on you. That effort counts, even if it isn't always acknowledged out loud. This demanding patch won't last forever. Let one or two family members know how things stand for you, so they can support you through the last part.
upright.general: You're near the finish after a long run, and your energy may feel thin. At this point, courage is mostly about not stopping short and not letting tiredness talk you out of what you've already built. Guard your time and attention carefully. A calm, steady finish is enough. You don't need a dramatic one.
upright.yes_no: The answer here is mixed, leaning hopeful. It can work out if you're willing to see it through a little longer and keep your effort steady. The obstacles in front of you look manageable rather than final. Ask yourself honestly whether you still have the energy, and if you do, keep going.
upright.timing: You're late in this cycle, close to the end rather than the beginning. The final stretch often feels slow and tiring, almost as if nothing is moving. Even so, the finish is in sight and things should ease once this phase wraps up. Patience and steady pacing will serve you better than a last-minute sprint.
upright.advice: Pace yourself so you reach the end with some energy to spare. Protect what matters most, whether that's your time, your health or the people close to you, and let lesser things wait. Finish what you started before taking on anything new. You've come this far for good reasons.
upright.thread: staying power for the last stretch of a long effort

reversed.summary: Weariness and guardedness may be taking over, so that every new demand feels like a threat. Pushing on without rest may now cost more than it gains. This isn't failure. It's a sign that your reserves need refilling. Recovery is the most useful thing you can do right now, and the work will still be there afterwards.
reversed.love: Old hurts may have you holding people at arm's length or expecting disappointment before it arrives. That habit makes sense, but it can block the closeness you actually want. Go gently with yourself and with the people around you. Instead of bracing for the worst, try saying clearly what you need and see how they respond.
reversed.career: Burnout is a real risk under this card. If you've been working through lunch, answering messages late at night or covering for others, it may be catching up with you. Take real breaks, the kind where you aren't checking your phone. If the workload is more than one person can carry, raise it calmly with your supervisor or team.
reversed.money: Money worries may feel heavier than they are simply because you're drained. Exhaustion makes every bill look bigger and every choice feel urgent. Simplify one thing, such as reviewing a single recurring expense, and leave the rest until you've rested. Clearer decisions usually come after sleep, not at midnight.
reversed.health: Your body and mind seem to be asking for rest, perhaps through tiredness, irritability or trouble focusing. Treat those signals as useful information, not a weakness to push past. Make room for proper sleep, quiet time and gentle activities that restore you. If you feel persistently unwell or low, a check-in with a doctor or counsellor is a sensible step.
reversed.family: You may feel you have to defend your space and energy at home, which can make everyday interactions tense. Rather than carrying that alone, think about asking a relative to take on a specific task or give you some quiet time. People often help more than you expect when you're clear about it. Easing your own load will also soften the atmosphere for everyone.
reversed.general: You've been on guard for too long, and the strain is showing. The next step isn't more effort but recovery, even if that feels uncomfortable for someone used to pushing on. Let yourself step back from at least one battle. Rested, you'll be able to tell which challenges are really worth your energy.
reversed.yes_no: This leans no for now. Not because the goal is impossible, but because you're running low on the energy it would need. Rest first, then look at the question again with fresh eyes. A decision made from exhaustion is rarely the one you'd choose when you feel well.
reversed.timing: A pause is needed before things can move forward. Pushing ahead right now is likely to slow you down rather than speed you up. Progress should pick up once you've recovered some energy and perspective. Think of this as a resting season, not a stalled one.
reversed.advice: Rest is part of resilience, not the opposite of it. Put the shield down for a while and let someone you trust share the watch. Choose one restorative thing to do this week and protect it. You'll come back stronger and clearer.
reversed.thread: fatigue, guardedness, and a real need to rest

cards.name: Ten of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A figure carrying a bundle of ten golden wands toward a distant midnight town, warm gold windows ahead.

upright.summary: You're carrying a heavy load, and much of it was taken on out of duty or a wish not to let anyone down. The goal may be close, but the weight is wearing you down. This card asks you to look honestly at what you're holding. Not every responsibility on your shoulders has to stay there.
upright.love: One of you may be doing most of the carrying in the relationship, whether that's planning, chores or emotional support. Over time, that imbalance can turn closeness into a list of tasks. Talk openly and without blame about how responsibilities are shared. Leave room for time together that has nothing to do with logistics.
upright.career: Too many responsibilities may have piled up on you, perhaps because you're reliable and people keep handing you more. Write down everything you're currently holding and mark what truly needs you. Some tasks could be shared, delayed or clarified with your manager. Doing fewer things well usually beats doing everything while exhausted.
upright.money: Commitments and obligations may feel heavy right now, from regular payments to promises you made to support others. Review them calmly, one by one, to see which still fit your life and priorities. For bigger decisions, a qualified adviser can help. Just knowing exactly what you carry often brings some relief.
upright.health: Overload tends to show up in the body as tight shoulders, tiredness, poor sleep or a shorter temper than usual. Pay attention to those signs rather than pushing through them. Lighten your schedule wherever you reasonably can, even by one commitment. Rest and simple routines will help you carry what remains.
upright.family: You may be the person everyone relies on at home, whether for ageing parents, children, finances or daily chores. That reliability is admirable, but it shouldn't mean you carry everything alone. Ask siblings, a partner or older children to take a fair share. Being specific about tasks makes it easier for others to say yes.
upright.general: You've said yes to a lot, and the effort you've put in is real. Still, not all of it has to be yours. Some of it may be habit, guilt or other people's expectations. Sorting what is truly your responsibility from what you simply absorbed is the first step towards relief.
upright.yes_no: This leans no, at least not on top of everything you're already carrying. Adding something new now could stretch you past what's sustainable. If the answer matters to you, think about what you could set down first. A clearer plate may change the answer later.
upright.timing: This is a heavy season, and waiting alone may not lighten it. Relief tends to come when the load is shared or reduced, not just when time passes. Expect things to feel slow while you carry this much. Every task you hand off speeds up the easing.
upright.advice: Put down what isn't yours to carry. Choose one responsibility you can delegate, postpone or decline, and act on it this week. Asking for help is a practical choice, not a failure. You'll have more to give to what really matters.
upright.thread: a heavy load taken on out of duty

reversed.summary: The weight is starting to lift as you hand things over or drop what no longer fits. You may be realising that you don't have to prove your worth by carrying everything. Delegating is sensible, not lazy. With more room to breathe, you can give real attention to what matters most.
reversed.love: Sharing the load can bring you closer. When responsibilities are spread more fairly, there's more energy left for warmth and fun. Be honest about what you can manage, and let your partner step in without redoing their efforts. Trusting each other this way builds a sturdier bond.
reversed.career: This is a good time to hand off tasks, set clearer limits and say no where it's reasonable. Talk with your team or manager about priorities so expectations are realistic. Quality often improves once your plate is lighter, because you can focus properly. People may respect your boundaries more than you expect.
reversed.money: Trimming obligations you no longer need can ease the pressure, even if each change seems small. Look for recurring commitments that have quietly stopped serving you. A modest cut can still bring real peace of mind. Take it step by step rather than overhauling everything at once.
reversed.health: Your body is likely to welcome the rest as you set burdens down. You may notice better sleep, looser shoulders or a calmer mood as the pressure eases. Protect that new space instead of filling it straight away with fresh obligations. Gentle, regular routines will help the relief last.
reversed.family: Family duties can now be shared more fairly. Have the conversation before resentment builds, and be clear about which tasks you'd like others to take on. Relatives may simply not have realised how much you were carrying. A fairer split can make home feel warmer for everyone.
reversed.general: Relief is possible, and it's already starting. You're learning what to keep and what to release, which is a skill that will serve you for a long time. Letting go might feel strange at first if you're used to carrying a lot. Give yourself time to get used to the lighter feeling.
reversed.yes_no: This leans yes, provided you let go of something to make room. The answer opens up once your load is more manageable. Think about what you're ready to release before you commit. Making space first gives the new thing a fair chance.
reversed.timing: Things should ease soon, but the change follows your actions rather than the calendar. It begins with one task handed off or one commitment declined. Each release makes the next one easier. Expect relief to build gradually and steadily.
reversed.advice: Let go of one task today and notice how it feels. Pick something small and concrete so the step is easy to take. Thank whoever takes it on, and resist the urge to take it back. Small releases add up to real change.
reversed.thread: relief through delegating and releasing what is too heavy

cards.name: Page of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A young figure gazing at a sprouting golden wand in a midnight desert, salamander motifs on tunic.

upright.summary: Curiosity and fresh enthusiasm are opening a new door for you. A spark of an idea, an invitation or some good news may arrive. This card favours exploring before you commit, so you learn as you go. Let yourself feel the excitement without needing every answer worked out yet.
upright.love: Playfulness and light flirtation can lift the mood, whether you're single or in a relationship. Be curious about the other person, ask questions and enjoy discovering each other without rushing to define things. Try something new together, perhaps a different hawker centre or a weekend walk somewhere unfamiliar. Warmth grows easily when things feel light.
upright.career: A new skill, idea or small project may be inviting you in. You don't need to overhaul your career to explore it. A short course, a side task or a conversation with someone in the field is enough to start. Treat it as an experiment and pay attention to what you learn.
upright.money: Curiosity about better money habits can pay off over time. You might read about budgeting, compare options or learn how something works before you rely on it. Do your research and take your time before committing to anything. Learning is a low-risk way to put this energy to use.
upright.health: You may feel a lift in energy and motivation. Use it for movement or an activity you'll actually enjoy, such as dance, swimming or a new walking route, rather than forcing a routine you dislike. Starting small helps the habit stick. Enjoyment is a good sign you've found something sustainable.
upright.family: There's a lively, curious mood at home. A new hobby, a shared project or an outing could bring everyone together, especially younger family members. Listen to the ideas people bring, even the unusual ones. Small adventures can create warm shared memories.
upright.general: Something new is stirring, and it feels exciting. You don't need a full plan yet, just a willingness to explore with an open mind. Pay attention to what keeps catching your interest. Early sparks like this often point towards something worth developing.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. The energy around your question is fresh and encouraging. Start small, try it out and see how it goes before committing fully. Early results will show you whether to take the next step.
upright.timing: Things are quick to begin under this card. Early signs, messages or openings may come soon, giving you something to act on. The full picture usually takes longer to develop. Enjoy the start and let things grow at their own pace.
upright.advice: Follow your curiosity and see where it leads. Take one small step this week towards the idea that excites you. Stay open to learning rather than expecting to get it perfect. Enthusiasm grows when you act on it.
upright.thread: fresh curiosity and an exciting spark of something new

reversed.summary: Ideas are plentiful, but your focus keeps slipping from one to the next. Without follow-through, early excitement tends to fade before anything takes shape. This isn't a lack of talent, just energy that needs direction. Choosing fewer things to pursue will help you actually see results.
reversed.love: Early excitement may cool if neither of you puts in steady effort. Restlessness can make it tempting to chase the next spark instead of building something real. Be honest with yourself and the other person about what you actually want. Consistency matters more right now than thrills.
reversed.career: You may have too many half-started ideas, projects or applications. Spreading yourself thin makes it hard for any of them to succeed. Finish one before taking on the next, even if it feels less exciting. Completed work builds more credibility than a long list of beginnings.
reversed.money: Impulse buys or sudden new projects could drain your funds. When something catches your eye, wait a few days before deciding. Often the urge passes, and you'll be glad you waited. Keep spending tied to plans you've already thought through.
reversed.health: Restlessness and scattered energy can make it hard to settle, rest or stick with healthy habits. A simple daily routine, such as regular sleep times or a short walk, can help steady you. Try not to start several new regimes at once. One small habit, kept up, will do more good.
reversed.family: Plans at home may start and then stall, leaving things half done and people frustrated. Agree as a household on one thing to focus on and do it properly. Shared follow-through builds trust and a sense of progress. New ideas can wait until this one is finished.
reversed.general: The enthusiasm is there, but direction is missing. Without a clear focus, energy leaks away into false starts. Narrow your attention to what matters most to you. A smaller, steadier effort will take you further than many scattered ones.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed, leaning no for now. The idea may have promise, but it hasn't been tested or thought through yet. Wait until your interest has held steady for a while before committing. If it still appeals later, the answer may change.
reversed.timing: Things may start fast and stall easily under this card. Early momentum is no guarantee of lasting progress. Give the idea time to prove itself before investing heavily. Steadier progress comes once your focus settles.
reversed.advice: Pick one idea and nurture it properly. Write down the next concrete step and do it before considering anything new. Keep a list of other ideas for later so they don't distract you. Focus turns sparks into something lasting.
reversed.thread: scattered enthusiasm that needs focus to take root

cards.name: Knight of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A knight on a rearing horse holding a golden wand, flame-pattern cloak, midnight desert, gold sparks.

upright.summary: This card brings a burst of drive and a real appetite for movement. Something that felt stuck is ready to get going, and you have the nerve to push it along. Use this momentum while it's here, but keep enough of a plan that the energy goes somewhere useful. A little adventure, like a new route, a new skill or a bold first step, can do you good right now.
upright.love: Chemistry and enthusiasm run high, whether you're dating or in a long relationship. You may want to plan something spontaneous, say what you feel, or bring back some of the fun. Enjoy that spark, and check that the other person is enjoying it at the same speed. Passion lands best when it leaves room for both of you.
upright.career: This is a good moment to act on a goal you've been circling, such as pitching the idea, sending the application or starting the project. Momentum favours people who move, especially when they've already sketched out the next few steps. Others may notice your energy and want to join in. Keep a short list of priorities so the excitement doesn't spread you too thin.
upright.money: You may feel ready to finally deal with a financial goal you've been putting off. That drive is useful, so turn it into a simple, written plan before you make any move. Ask yourself what you're trying to achieve and what a sensible first step looks like. Moving with energy and a clear head tends to work better than moving on adrenaline alone.
upright.health: Your energy is likely up, and it wants an outlet. Active pursuits like a brisk walk at East Coast, a swim, a dance class or a new sport can turn restlessness into something that feels good. Warm up properly and build up gradually instead of going all out on the first day. Moving your body may also help clear a busy mind.
upright.family: Home life may feel lively, with outings, visitors, travel plans or talk of change. Your enthusiasm can lift the mood and get people moving. Just make sure everyone hears about plans early, especially older relatives or anyone who prefers a slower pace. Bringing others along, rather than pulling them, keeps the household happy.
upright.general: Things are speeding up, and you're more ready for it than you might think. This is a time to say yes to movement, try something new and trust your courage. Keep one eye on the practical details so small things don't trip you up. Bold, with a bit of care, is the right setting.
upright.yes_no: This leans clearly towards yes. The energy around your question supports action rather than waiting. Go ahead with confidence, but double-check the details: the timing, the logistics and who else is affected. A quick review before you leap keeps a good yes from turning messy.
upright.timing: Expect a quick pace. Things that have been slow may suddenly start moving, and decisions may need to be made faster than you're used to. This is a season of momentum more than patience. Stay ready so you can respond when an opening appears.
upright.advice: Go for it, and bring some care with you. Take the bold step you've been thinking about, but decide your direction before you start. Tell the people who need to know, and check the key details once. Courage and a bit of planning will take you much further than either one alone.
upright.thread: bold momentum and a real readiness to take action

reversed.summary: The drive is still there, but it's turning into haste. You may be rushing, starting several things at once, or getting frustrated when they don't move as fast as you'd like. That impatience can lead to avoidable mistakes. Slowing down a little now is a way to protect your progress, not to lose it.
reversed.love: Things may be moving too fast, or feelings may run hot one week and cool the next. That can leave both of you unsure where you stand. Slow the pace and say plainly what you want and what you're ready for. Being steady will build more trust than a grand gesture.
reversed.career: Frustration at work may tempt you to fire off the email, push the launch or make a quick call you haven't thought through. Take a breath before you act. Look at the plan again and ask what really needs doing today. A short pause now can save you a lot of cleaning up later.
reversed.money: A rushed purchase or a quick money decision could cost more than it seems to. If something feels urgent, treat that as a reason to wait rather than to act. Sleep on it, compare options and talk it over with someone level-headed if that helps. You'll rarely regret taking a calm second look.
reversed.health: You may feel wired and tired at once, busy but not getting much done. Scattered energy wears you out faster than steady effort does. Try to pace your days, protect your sleep and pick one form of movement you can keep up. Rest is part of getting your energy back, not a break from it.
reversed.family: Tempers at home may be shorter than usual, and small things can flare up quickly. If you feel the heat rising, step away before you answer. A walk around the block or a glass of water can change how a conversation goes. Cooler replies will help everyone settle.
reversed.general: There's plenty of fire but no clear aim. Starting too many things, or charging ahead without a map, leaves you drained and frustrated. Choose one direction and give it your attention for a while. Focused energy gets much further than energy pointed everywhere.
reversed.yes_no: For now, this leans towards no. The urge to act fast may be stronger than the case for acting. Slow down, review your reasons and look at what you might be missing. With a calmer approach, the answer may change later.
reversed.timing: The pace feels uneven, with sudden rushes followed by stalls. Pushing harder will probably cause more delay, not less. A measured, steady approach is likely to get you there sooner. Let things settle before you move again.
reversed.advice: Channel your fire instead of letting it scatter. Choose one priority and finish it before you start the next. Wait before you make big or emotional decisions. Your energy is valuable, so give it a direction.
reversed.thread: haste and frustration that need a clear direction

cards.name: Queen of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A queen on a lion throne holding a golden wand and sunflower, black cat at her feet, midnight backdrop.

upright.summary: Warmth and quiet self-assurance are at the centre of this card. You're at your best when you stop editing yourself and let your natural energy show. People are drawn to that kind of ease. Trust what you bring and let your confidence guide your choices.
upright.love: Your warmth and openness are appealing right now. You don't need to perform or chase, because being relaxed and generous does more. If you're attached, bring some playfulness and affection back into daily life. If you're single, trust that you're enough exactly as you are.
upright.career: You can lead well here, whether or not you have the title. Combine clarity with kindness and people will respond. Speak up in meetings, share your ideas and take ownership of work you care about. Your energy can set the tone for the people around you.
upright.money: You're in a good place to make organised, confident money choices. Trust your own sense of what you need instead of following what others are doing. A tidy budget or a clear savings goal can feel empowering instead of restrictive. Choices made from self-respect tend to be sound ones.
upright.health: Your energy rises when you make time for things you truly enjoy. Joy is fuel, so plan for it, whether that's cooking, dancing, gardening or meeting friends. Movement you like is easier to keep up than movement you dread. Look after your warmth and it will look after you.
upright.family: You may be the warm heart of the household right now, the one who gathers people and lifts the mood. That's a lovely role to play. Make sure quieter family members also get space to shine and be heard. Shared warmth lasts longer than warmth held by one person.
upright.general: Confidence and independence are your strengths now, so let them show. You don't need permission to take up space or pursue what excites you. Stay generous and grounded at the same time. This is a time to stand fully in your own life.
upright.yes_no: This leans towards yes. Your instincts are trustworthy here, and the conditions support moving ahead. Go forward with confidence and openness. If it feels right in a calm, settled way, that's a good sign.
upright.timing: The pace is steady and bright. Things warm up as your confidence grows, and momentum builds from your own presence. You don't have to force a quick result. Showing up consistently will move things along.
upright.advice: Own your light without dimming anyone else's. Be confident, be warm and let your real self be seen. Encourage others while you shine. There's room for more than one bright person in the room.
upright.thread: warm confidence and the strength of being yourself

reversed.summary: Your usual glow feels dimmer. Self-doubt, comparison or plain tiredness may be making you question yourself. This isn't a lasting change. It's a sign that your energy needs refilling. Gentleness will help more than pressure right now.
reversed.love: Insecurity or jealousy may be creeping in, perhaps without a clear reason. Keeping those feelings to yourself usually makes them bigger. Talk about them calmly and honestly, without accusing anyone. Reassurance often comes more easily once the worry is out in the open.
reversed.career: You may be overextended at work and starting to doubt your worth. Remind yourself of what you've already handled well, and write it down if that helps. Cut back where you can, and rest before you take on more. Confidence comes back faster when you aren't running on empty.
reversed.money: Watch out for spending to lift your mood or to keep up with friends and social media. A treat is fine, but a pattern of it may leave you feeling worse. Take a moment to work out what you actually need. Being clear about that is a quiet kind of confidence.
reversed.health: Your energy and confidence may both feel low. Gentle, steady routines like regular meals, enough sleep and short walks can help you rebuild. Go back to small things you enjoy, even for ten minutes a day. If the low mood lingers, talking to someone you trust is worthwhile.
reversed.family: You may be giving a lot at home and feeling unseen for it. Resentment builds quietly when needs go unspoken. Ask clearly for help or appreciation instead of hoping someone notices. The people around you may simply not realise how much you carry.
reversed.general: Your confidence needs rebuilding, not forcing. Start with small, doable steps that remind you what you're capable of. Step back from comparisons that drain you. Your warmth hasn't gone. It's resting.
reversed.yes_no: The answer is mixed and leans towards no for now. You may not feel sure enough of yourself to commit fully. Give yourself time to steady and rest first. Once your footing feels firmer, the question may look quite different.
reversed.timing: Things move more slowly for now, and that's alright. Your confidence returns as you rest and reconnect with what you enjoy. This is a season for recovering, not racing. Momentum will come back when your energy does.
reversed.advice: Be as kind to yourself as you are to others. Notice your inner critic and answer it the way a good friend would. Rest, ask for support and do one small thing that makes you feel like yourself. Self-respect is how confidence starts again.
reversed.thread: shaky confidence that needs kindness and rest

cards.name: King of Wands
cards.image_prompt: A king on a throne carved with lions and salamanders, holding a golden wand, midnight sky with gold stars.

upright.summary: You have a clear sense of where things should go, and the confidence to lead the way there. This card is about vision that turns into action. People follow someone who can show them a direction and explain why it matters. Use your strength to lift others as well as yourself.
upright.love: You bring steadiness, generosity and a sense of shared purpose to your relationship. You may be the one who suggests plans or a direction for the future. Lead by example and through warmth, not pressure. A partner feels secure when your strength includes them.
upright.career: This is a good time to step up, whether by proposing a big idea, taking charge of a project or giving a team direction. Clarity is persuasive, so be ready to explain the goal simply. Delegate generously and trust others with real responsibility. Leadership that gives people credit builds loyalty.
upright.money: Think long term and plan strategically. A clear plan you can stick to will usually do better than quick, reactive moves. Set goals that reflect what you actually want your life to look like. If a decision is complex, get qualified guidance before you act.
upright.health: Your drive is strong and can help you work towards real wellbeing goals. Set a direction, but build in rest so your pace is one you can keep up. Leaders burn out when they forget their own limits. Steady habits will carry you further than heroic bursts.
upright.family: You may be the one setting the tone at home, making decisions or guiding plans. Be decisive and warm at the same time. Explain your reasons and invite people's views before you settle things. A household follows a steady, kind lead quite naturally.
upright.general: You have both vision and the will to act on it, which is a powerful combination. Use it to build something that helps others along with you. Stay open to ideas that sharpen your own. This is a time to lead your own life with purpose.
upright.yes_no: This leans towards yes. Your vision looks sound, and you have what you need to carry it out. Go ahead with care and keep other people's needs in mind. A thoughtful yes here is likely to hold up.
upright.timing: Expect steady, building progress rather than overnight change. Results grow as you lead consistently and follow through. This is a season for showing up reliably. The momentum you create now will keep going.
upright.advice: Lead with vision and lift others up. Be clear about where you're heading and generous with the people who help you get there. Make decisions with confidence, and stay open to feedback. The best leaders make others feel capable too.
upright.thread: clear vision and confident, generous leadership

reversed.summary: Strength of will is starting to slip into impatience or control. You may be setting expectations too high, for others or for yourself, and getting frustrated when they aren't met. Pushing harder usually makes this worse. Easing your grip and listening more will restore the balance.
reversed.love: Demanding or controlling behaviour, even when it's well meant, can create distance. Notice whether you're making decisions for both of you without asking. Share the choices and listen properly to what your partner says. Closeness grows when both people feel they have a say.
reversed.career: You may be aiming too high, too fast, and your team or colleagues may be struggling to keep up. Frustration on all sides is a signal to adjust. Ask for input, reset deadlines where you can and set realistic milestones. Good leaders adapt the plan when it isn't working.
reversed.money: A bold financial move may be rasher than it looks. Check the numbers carefully and get a second opinion from someone you trust, or a qualified adviser, before you commit. Confidence isn't the same as certainty. Waiting a little costs less than a hasty mistake.
reversed.health: Pushing hard and expecting too much of yourself may be building tension in your body and mind. Notice where you're overdoing things. Ease off, rest properly and let your goals be kinder for a while. Your drive will return stronger once you've had a break.
reversed.family: Insisting on your own way may be straining things at home. Family members may feel unheard or overruled, even if your intentions are good. Ask questions before you give answers. Making space for other views brings people back towards you.
reversed.general: Power without patience tends to backfire. If things feel like a struggle, the answer is probably to slow down and listen, not to push harder. Look again at whether your expectations are realistic. Flexibility is a strength here.
reversed.yes_no: For now, this leans towards no. The plan may need rethinking before you commit. Look closely at whether you're rushing or overreaching. A revised approach could change the answer later.
reversed.timing: Delays here are likely to come from rushing. Forcing things may stall them further. A measured, patient pace will probably get better results. Let the plan settle before you push forward again.
reversed.advice: Lead by listening as well as speaking. Loosen your grip on how things must go and invite other ideas in. Set expectations that are fair to others and to yourself. Patience will make your strength far more effective.
reversed.thread: strong will that needs patience and more listening

cards.name: Ace of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A golden chalice overflowing with five streams of light, hand from midnight cloud, white dove above.

upright.summary: Something tender is starting to move in you, and there is real room in your heart to let it in. It might be a new affection, a renewed sense of compassion, or simply the relief of feeling things fully again. This card suggests warmth and sincere connection are close at hand. You do not need to force anything; staying open is most of the work.
upright.love: A new attraction may be stirring, or an existing bond may soften into a more honest kind of closeness. Let your affection show in simple ways, like a message sent without overthinking or a moment of real attention over dinner. Try not to script how it should unfold. Feelings that are allowed to breathe tend to grow more naturally than ones managed too tightly.
upright.career: You may find fresh energy in work that feels meaningful, especially where you can see the people your effort helps. Caring about the purpose behind a task, rather than just ticking it off, will show in the quality of what you produce. This is a good time to bring kindness into team dynamics or client relationships. Small acts of goodwill at work can open doors you did not expect.
upright.money: A grateful mood can change how you see what you already have, often showing that there is more than you thought. You may feel drawn to share or give, whether through a treat for someone, a contribution, or simply your time. Let that generosity stay within what feels comfortable for your budget. Giving from a steady place feels better than giving from pressure.
upright.health: Your mood is likely to lift when you let emotions move rather than holding them in. A good laugh, a quiet cry, or an unhurried evening of rest can all help reset your energy. Notice how much lighter your body feels when your heart is at ease. Gentle routines that nourish you emotionally are worth protecting this season.
upright.family: A kind word or a small gesture, like bringing home someone's favourite kuih, could warm the mood at home noticeably. Someone in the family may be more ready than usual to open up and share what they feel. Listen without rushing to fix or advise. These soft moments can quietly strengthen the bonds between you.
upright.general: A new emotional chapter is beginning, and it wants to flow rather than be held back. You may notice yourself feeling more moved by ordinary things, such as music, kindness from strangers, or a friend's good news. Stay receptive instead of bracing for disappointment. Openness now lays the ground for deeper connection later.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. The feeling behind the question appears genuine, and the way forward looks open to you. Still, a beginning like this needs tending, so keep showing up with care and honesty. Treat it as a warm invitation rather than a finished outcome.
upright.timing: This energy tends to arrive gently, like the first rain after a dry spell. It may start quietly and build over the coming weeks as you give it attention. There is no need to hurry it along. Let it unfold at a soft, natural pace.
upright.advice: Say yes to openness, even if part of you wants to stay guarded. Let yourself receive kindness, compliments and help as easily as you give them. Notice when you deflect warmth out of habit, and try accepting it instead. Your heart has more capacity than you may realise.
upright.thread: a fresh wave of feeling and a heart open to love

reversed.summary: Your feelings may be tucked away, muted, or simply running low right now. This is not a failure; it often happens after a period of giving too much or carrying too much. The card asks you to refill your own cup before pouring more for others. Inner care comes first, and connection can follow once you feel steadier.
reversed.love: You may feel guarded, numb, or unsure what you actually want from someone. Rather than pushing for answers from a partner or a new interest, sit with your own heart for a while. Journalling or a quiet walk can help you sort through what is really there. Clarity about yourself will make any relationship conversation more honest.
reversed.career: Work might feel flat, repetitive, or quietly draining at the moment. Look for small pockets of satisfaction, such as a task you enjoy or a colleague you like talking to. Protect your energy by setting gentle limits on overtime and after-hours messages where you reasonably can. Motivation often returns once you stop running on empty.
reversed.money: When your mood feels hollow, it can be tempting to fill the gap with online shopping or little indulgences. Pause before buying and ask what you are really hoping to feel. Often the need is for rest, company, or comfort that costs nothing. Noticing this pattern helps you spend in ways that truly serve you.
reversed.health: Emotional tiredness may be showing up as low energy, restless sleep, or a short temper. Slow, kind routines can help, like an early night, a warm meal, or time away from screens. Talking to someone you trust can lighten what you are carrying. If the heaviness lingers, reaching out to a qualified professional is a caring step.
reversed.family: You may be giving a great deal at home and receiving little in return. It is fair to make space for your own needs, even within a busy household. Let others know, gently, when you need help or quiet time. Looking after yourself makes you a steadier presence for the people you love.
reversed.general: The feeling is present, but it is blocked, unspoken, or hidden beneath fatigue. This is a season for inner work rather than outward reaching. Give yourself permission to slow down and notice what you have been avoiding. Once your inner well begins to refill, connection will feel easier again.
reversed.yes_no: This leans mixed to no for now. Your heart does not seem quite ready, and acting too soon could leave you feeling more drained. Wait until you feel steadier and clearer about what you want. The answer may shift once you have taken care of yourself.
reversed.timing: Things move slowly here, and that is part of the healing. Feelings need time to settle before a clear opening can appear. Rushing will likely only add pressure. Allow a quieter season and trust that warmth will return.
reversed.advice: Do one small, kind thing for yourself today, without guilt or explanation. It might be a quiet coffee alone, an early night, or saying no to an extra obligation. Treat your own needs as worth meeting. Refilling yourself is not selfish; it is how you keep caring for others.
reversed.thread: feelings held back and a need to gently refill yourself

cards.name: Two of Cups
cards.image_prompt: Two figures exchanging golden cups beneath a winged lion caduceus, midnight blue sky, soft gold glow.

upright.summary: Two people are meeting with genuine respect and real interest in each other. This card describes a bond where giving and receiving feel balanced and fair. It may be romantic, professional, or a close friendship. What makes it work is that both sides are truly showing up.
upright.love: Mutual attraction and honest regard are strong here. You may sense that the other person sees you clearly and likes what they see. A relationship can deepen naturally when both of you put in a similar effort and speak openly. Enjoy the ease of a connection that does not require chasing.
upright.career: A collaboration or dependable working partner is favoured now. Shared goals make heavy projects feel lighter, and each person's strengths can cover the other's gaps. This is a good time to propose working together or to strengthen ties with a trusted colleague. Respectful communication will keep the partnership productive.
upright.money: Joint plans, such as shared household costs or a group arrangement, tend to go smoothly when everyone understands the terms. Talk openly about who covers what and how decisions will be made. Clear agreement protects goodwill as well as resources. Fairness is the foundation here.
upright.health: Support from a friend or partner can make a real difference to your wellbeing. Healthy habits may feel easier to keep when you share them, like evening walks at the park connector or cooking together. Being encouraged, and encouraging in return, keeps energy up. Lean into that mutual support.
upright.family: Understanding is growing between you and a relative or partner. Small compromises, offered willingly by both sides, are bringing calm into the home. You may find old tensions easing as you listen more closely to each other. Meeting halfway is proving worth the effort.
upright.general: Connection is working because both sides contribute. Harmony here is not luck; it comes from reciprocity, honesty and respect. Notice the relationships where you feel equally valued. These are worth nurturing and celebrating.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. The interest and goodwill appear to be mutual. As long as both sides stay honest and keep showing up, the outlook is good. Trust the balance you are sensing.
upright.timing: This moves at a steady, shared pace. Progress comes from both people stepping forward together rather than one rushing ahead. Expect things to build as trust grows. Let it unfold at a rhythm you can both sustain.
upright.advice: Be fair, be direct, and meet the other person halfway. Say what you appreciate as well as what you need. Small acts of consistency build more trust than grand gestures. Treat the connection as something you both look after.
upright.thread: a balanced bond built on mutual respect and care

reversed.summary: A connection feels uneven or strained at the moment. Signals may have been misread, and small assumptions could be creating distance. The attraction or goodwill has not disappeared, but the balance is off. Honest, calm conversation can do a lot to repair it.
reversed.love: One of you may be giving more than the other, or unspoken expectations may be piling up. Rather than waiting for the other person to guess, name your needs plainly and kindly. Ask how they are feeling, too, and listen without defending yourself. Openness can restore closeness that silence has worn down.
reversed.career: Roles within a partnership or team may have become blurry. If you feel you are carrying more than your share, raise it early and constructively. Agreeing on who does what can prevent resentment from building. Clarity now protects the working relationship.
reversed.money: Shared arrangements may be vague or based on assumptions. Writing down expectations, even informally in a shared note, can prevent misunderstandings later. Revisit any agreement that no longer feels fair. Clear terms keep money from becoming a source of tension.
reversed.health: Strain in a close relationship may be affecting your sleep, appetite or mood. Notice how much of your energy is going into worrying about the other person. Give yourself time to rest and do things that settle you. Your own balance matters too.
reversed.family: Words may be landing badly at home, even when no harm is meant. Slow down and check what the other person actually meant before reacting. A calm moment over a meal may be better than discussing things in the heat of the moment. Patience can soften a tense atmosphere.
reversed.general: The pull between you is real, but the give and take has slipped out of balance. Adjustment is needed rather than abandonment. Look at where communication has broken down. Small corrections now can prevent bigger rifts later.
reversed.yes_no: This leans mixed. The connection has potential, but it can only work well once the imbalance is honestly addressed. If both sides are willing to talk and adjust, the answer may turn more positive. For now, hold off on assuming a clear yes.
reversed.timing: Things are moving more slowly than you might hope. Resolution is more likely to follow an open conversation than patient waiting. The sooner the air is cleared, the sooner progress resumes. Expect a period of adjustment first.
reversed.advice: Listen as much as you speak, and ask before you assume. Check your interpretation of the other person's words or silence. Share your own needs without blame. Balance returns when both people feel heard.
reversed.thread: a bond out of balance that needs honest, kind talk

cards.name: Three of Cups
cards.image_prompt: Three dancers raising golden cups in a midnight orchard, gold fruit and garlands around them.

upright.summary: Friendship, community and shared celebration are in the spotlight. Joy grows when you spend time with people who genuinely lift you. This may be a reunion, a festive gathering, or simply a good evening with close friends. Let yourself enjoy the warmth of good company.
upright.love: Social settings may bring warmth and new sparks, and friends could play a part in introductions or support. Happiness feels easier when it is shared with people who care about you both. If you are in a relationship, time spent with mutual friends may bring you closer. Lightness and fun are good for the heart now.
upright.career: Teamwork is strong and morale looks good. This is a fine time to acknowledge wins together, even small ones, perhaps over a team lunch. Celebrating shared progress builds trust and motivation. Collaboration is likely to feel smooth and encouraging.
upright.money: You can enjoy good times without overreaching. A simple hawker meal or potluck with friends can be just as joyful as an expensive night out. Choose celebrations that feel generous in spirit rather than in price. Shared joy does not need a big bill.
upright.health: Time with supportive people restores your energy and lifts your mood. Laughter, conversation and a sense of belonging all do you good. Consider joining a group activity you enjoy, such as a walking club or a hobby class. Connection is a quiet but powerful source of wellbeing.
upright.family: A gathering or shared meal could bring relatives closer, especially around festive seasons. Try to include everyone you can, even those who are often left out. Simple traditions can rekindle warmth between generations. Enjoy the noise and closeness while it lasts.
upright.general: Community and good company bring cheer right now. Take time to celebrate what is going well, rather than rushing on to the next task. Recognising shared happiness strengthens your bonds. Joy grows when it is spread around.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. Support and goodwill seem to surround the matter. People around you are likely to help or cheer you on. Move forward with a light and open heart.
upright.timing: This tends to arrive soon, often around a gathering, festival or shared occasion. Things may come together when people meet. Look for momentum in social moments. It is a lively, sociable season.
upright.advice: Make time for the people who lift you, and let yourself fully enjoy it. Reach out to a friend you have been meaning to see. Celebrate small victories together. Joy is worth making room for.
upright.thread: friendship, shared celebration and the lift of good company

reversed.summary: Your social life may be tipping out of balance, whether through too much activity, too little contact, or too much talk behind backs. The card is a reminder that a few real connections matter more than a crowded calendar. It is a good time to check which ties truly nourish you. Favour depth over noise.
reversed.love: Outside opinions or a busy social schedule may be crowding the space between you and someone special. Friends meaning well can still add pressure or confusion. Protect time that belongs just to the two of you. Your own sense of the relationship matters more than group commentary.
reversed.career: Office chatter, cliques or group chats may be distracting or dividing the team. Keep your words neutral and avoid being pulled into sides. Focus on your work and on respectful, direct communication. Staying out of drama protects your reputation and your peace.
reversed.money: Outings, treats and group celebrations can add up quickly. Check how much you are spending just to keep up socially. It is fine to suggest simpler plans or sit some events out. Your real friends will understand.
reversed.health: Late nights or overindulgence may be leaving you drained. Alternatively, you may be feeling lonely and in need of genuine contact. Either way, look for balance: rest when you need it, and seek out company that feels nourishing. Your energy will thank you.
reversed.family: Gossip or side-taking in the family may be causing friction. Try not to pass on stories or join in on criticising others. If asked to choose sides, gently step back. Staying neutral can help calm the wider family atmosphere.
reversed.general: The group energy feels off, and the quality of connection matters more than the number of people involved. Notice where you feel drained rather than supported. It may be time to pull back from some circles and invest in others. Balance will return with a little discernment.
reversed.yes_no: This leans mixed to no. Consider whether the people involved are truly helping or simply adding distraction. If the crowd is clouding your judgement, step back before deciding. A clearer answer may come once things quieten down.
reversed.timing: The pace feels uneven and a little scattered. Things are likely to settle once you cut back on noise and distractions. Give yourself a quieter stretch before expecting progress. Calm brings clarity.
reversed.advice: Nurture a few close friendships and step away from gossip. Choose gatherings that feel meaningful rather than obligatory. Rest when your social energy runs low. Real connection grows best in calmer spaces.
reversed.thread: social excess, gossip or isolation that asks for balance

cards.name: Four of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A figure under a tree with arms crossed, three golden cups before them, a hand offering a fourth from midnight cloud.

upright.summary: You may be feeling flat, bored or quietly turned inward, as if nothing on offer really moves you. That mood is worth listening to, since it often means something needs rethinking. Still, a dull patch can make good things look grey. Before you write everything off, take a slower second look, because something worthwhile may already be within reach.
upright.love: You may be so caught up in your own thoughts that you miss the care already coming your way, like a message checking in or a small effort made for you. Ask yourself honestly whether you are tired and withdrawn, or truly not interested. Those two feel alike but call for different responses. If you are single, a kind person may be nearer than you think, so keep at least one door open.
upright.career: Work may feel like the same routine every day, and nothing seems exciting enough to chase. Use this quiet stretch to think about what you actually want from your working life, not just what would get you out of the slump. Be careful not to turn down an offer, project or conversation just because your mood is low. Make a note of it and come back to it when you feel clearer.
upright.money: There may be options you brushed aside too quickly, such as a better arrangement, a small adjustment or advice you never followed up on. A calm review now could show you something useful you missed. You don't have to act straight away. Just look again with fresh eyes before deciding something isn't worth it.
upright.health: Low motivation can be a sign of tiredness, overload or simply needing rest, rather than a lack of willpower. Go gently and notice what drains you and what gives you a little lift. Small things help, like a short walk, an early night or less time on your phone. If the heaviness hangs on, it is sensible to talk to someone you trust or a professional.
upright.family: At home you might feel a little distant, going through the motions while your mind is elsewhere. Small kindnesses, like food kept aside for you or a parent asking how your day went, can start to feel like background noise. Try to look up and notice who is making an effort. Even a simple thank-you can warm things up again.
upright.general: Reflection is useful, and stepping back from noise can show you what matters. But staying closed off for too long can cost you a chance you would actually have liked. Treat this as a pause and not a wall. Stay a little curious, even if you aren't excited yet.
upright.yes_no: This leans maybe. Something is being offered, but you haven't really engaged with it yet, so the answer depends on you. If you take a proper look and still feel nothing, a no is fair. If you notice even a spark of interest, it could become a yes.
upright.timing: The pace is slow and reflective, a bit like the lull of a long, humid afternoon. Take the time you need to sort out your feelings, since rushing won't help. Just don't let the pause drag on until the chance has passed. Give yourself a gentle point at which to decide.
upright.advice: Lift your eyes and notice what is actually in front of you before deciding it isn't enough. Write down what is being offered, even the small things. Ask what would make you feel more engaged rather than waiting for the mood to change by itself. One honest look may change your answer.
upright.thread: a reflective pause and an offer you may be overlooking

reversed.summary: Interest is quietly coming back, and you feel more ready to take part in life again. The fog of a flat patch is lifting, and your outlook is fresher. You can see possibilities you couldn't see before. Let that new energy guide you toward something real, one step at a time.
reversed.love: You may feel open to connection again after a period of numbness or holding back. Curiosity returns, and you might reply more warmly, say yes to plans or notice someone in a new way. Couples may find small pleasures together again. Take it at an easy pace and enjoy the returning warmth.
reversed.career: Your motivation is picking up, and work feels less like a grind. You may be ready to say yes to a new task, a course or a conversation about your next step. Ideas come more easily now that the heaviness has eased. Act on one of them while the interest is fresh.
reversed.money: Your options look clearer, and you can weigh them with a calmer mind than before. Things that felt confusing or tiresome now seem easier to manage. This is a good time to review your plans steadily, without pressure. Clear thinking, not speed, is your strength here.
reversed.health: Your energy and mood are starting to lift, perhaps slowly but noticeably. Build on this with steady routines like regular meals, movement you enjoy and decent sleep. Don't rush to make up for lost time all at once. Consistency will help the good feeling last.
reversed.family: You reconnect with the people at home and start to notice the efforts they make. Conversations over dinner feel lighter, and you may want to join in again. Warmth comes back as you show up more fully. A small gesture from you will likely be welcomed.
reversed.general: The fog is clearing, and you are moving from withdrawal back into taking part. What felt pointless now has some meaning again. Accept that you needed the pause, and let it go without guilt. A new perspective is ready for you to use.
reversed.yes_no: This leans yes. You are in a better place to recognise a good chance and accept it. Your renewed interest makes it more likely that things will move forward. Trust the spark you feel.
reversed.timing: Things are picking up soon. Momentum builds as your mood lifts, often faster than you expect once you start. Early steps may feel small, but they add up. Keep moving while the energy is there.
reversed.advice: Accept the new opportunity gently, without needing it to be perfect. Say yes to one thing that genuinely interests you. Let your curiosity lead rather than your old doubts. You can adjust as you go.
reversed.thread: renewed interest and a fresh view after a flat patch

cards.name: Five of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A cloaked figure facing three spilled cups, two golden cups standing behind, a bridge to a gold-lit house at midnight.

upright.summary: A loss or disappointment is taking up most of your attention right now, and that hurt is real. It makes sense to feel it rather than brush it aside. Even so, grief can narrow your view until it seems nothing good is left. Something meaningful is still standing behind you, waiting until you are ready to turn around.
upright.love: Hurt, regret or a sense of what might have been may feel loud right now. Let yourself feel it honestly instead of pretending you are fine. In time, notice the connection, care or friendship that is still there. Healthy closeness is not completely gone, even if it looks different from what you hoped.
upright.career: A setback at work may sting, like a rejection, a plan that fell through or feedback that hurt. Treat it as information and a lesson, not a final verdict on your worth. Give yourself some time to process it before deciding anything big. Your skills and experience are still yours.
upright.money: A past choice or an unexpected loss may be weighing on you. Dwelling on it won't change it, but learning from it can. Make small, calm next steps instead of drastic moves driven by regret. If you feel unsure, speaking with a trusted, qualified person may help you think more clearly.
upright.health: Grief and regret can drain your energy and affect your sleep and appetite. Be patient with yourself and keep basic care going, even if it is simple. Lean on people you trust instead of carrying it alone. If the heaviness feels too much, reaching out for professional support is a sign of strength.
upright.family: Old hurts, a family loss or unmet expectations may be colouring life at home. Acknowledge these feelings kindly, both your own and other people's. Not everyone grieves in the same way or at the same speed. Notice who is still close by and willing to sit with you.
upright.general: You are focused on what was lost, and grieving is fair. Still, it isn't the whole picture of your life. When you feel ready, look around for what remains, such as people, strengths and possibilities. Both things can be true at once.
upright.yes_no: This leans no. Disappointment is likely in the short term, and things may not go the way you hoped. That doesn't mean everything is lost. What remains may open a different path later.
upright.timing: The pace is slow. Grief and disappointment work on their own timetable, and they can't be rushed. Perspective comes gradually, often when you least expect it. Allow the process its season.
upright.advice: Honour what you feel instead of hurrying past it. Then, gently, turn around and take stock of what is still here. Talk to someone who cares about you. Small steps forward count.
upright.thread: disappointment and grief, with something still standing behind you

reversed.summary: Healing is beginning as you slowly accept what happened. The loss still matters, but it no longer takes up all your attention. You are ready to look forward without carrying the whole weight with you. This is a quiet turning point.
reversed.love: Forgiveness, whether toward someone else or yourself, may bring real peace now. This doesn't mean pretending the hurt didn't happen, only that you choose not to keep living in it. Space opens up for renewed closeness or something new. Let your heart soften at its own pace.
reversed.career: You find the lesson in a recent setback and move on with more clarity. What went wrong becomes useful experience rather than a sore point. You may feel ready to try again or change your approach. Confidence returns as you take practical steps.
