reversed.money: Recovery comes step by step instead of all at once. Small, steady choices help rebuild your sense of security and confidence. Keep things simple and realistic. Each careful decision adds to your footing.
reversed.health: Your mood is gradually steadying, and the heaviness is easing. Keep up gentle routines that support you, like rest, movement and time with people you care about. Some days will still be harder than others, and that is normal. Overall, the direction is toward feeling better.
reversed.family: Tension at home is starting to ease, and old hurts are losing their grip. A sincere conversation or a small gesture could open the way to reconciliation. Not everything needs to be resolved at once. Warmth can return gradually.
reversed.general: You are turning away from loss and toward what is still here. Acceptance is doing its quiet work, even if you can't feel all of it yet. Let yourself enjoy small good moments without guilt. Moving forward doesn't erase what you lost.
reversed.yes_no: This leans mixed to yes. Things improve as you let go of what you can't change, though not instantly. The answer becomes more positive the more you focus on what is possible now. Patience helps here.
reversed.timing: Change is gradual. Improvement comes in small steps over a period of weeks rather than overnight. You will notice it more looking back than day to day. Keep going steadily.
reversed.advice: Let go of what you can't change, and turn toward what remains. Forgive where you can, including yourself. Take one small, hopeful step today. Healing grows from there.
reversed.thread: healing, acceptance and a first step toward moving forward

cards.name: Six of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A child handing a golden cup of white flowers to another in a midnight courtyard, gold lantern light.

upright.summary: Sweet memories and simple kindness are close at hand right now. The past offers gentle comfort and may even spark a useful idea. You might reconnect with an old friend, revisit a familiar place or think warmly about childhood. Let this softness steady you.
upright.love: Familiar warmth fills your relationships, and trust comes easily. Someone from your past may get back in touch, or you and your partner may enjoy remembering how things began. Simple dates and shared jokes mean a lot now. Sweetness is more important than grand gestures.
upright.career: Early interests or skills you set aside may inspire fresh ideas at work. Think about what you enjoyed before titles and targets took over. Mentoring, teaching or helping a newer colleague suits you now. Kindness at work builds lasting goodwill.
upright.money: Simple pleasures may be more than enough for now. Familiar, low-cost joys, like a favourite hawker meal or an evening with old friends, can satisfy more than new purchases. Value what you already have. Contentment is a quiet strength.
upright.health: Comforting routines and time with loved ones help you settle. Gentle, familiar activities, like an old hobby, a walk in a place you love or a home-cooked dish, can lift your mood. Let yourself rest in what feels safe. Small comforts restore energy.
upright.family: Shared memories and small acts of kindness bring everyone closer. Looking through old photos, cooking a family recipe or sharing stories over a meal may bring real warmth. Children or older relatives may especially enjoy this. Home feels more like home.
upright.general: Nostalgia and goodwill surround you. Let them comfort you and remind you of what you value, without letting them rule your choices. Simple kindness, given and received, is the heart of this time. Innocence and trust are easier to find.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. The mood is kind and familiar, so trust and agreement come easily. Things linked to people or places you know are especially favoured. Go ahead with an open heart.
upright.timing: The pace is unhurried and comfortable. Developments may be linked to something or someone from your past coming back into view. There is no need to rush. Let things unfold naturally.
upright.advice: Offer a small kindness today, perhaps to someone you haven't spoken to in a while. Enjoy what is familiar without guilt. Let good memories remind you of who you are. Simplicity serves you well now.
upright.thread: gentle nostalgia, simple kindness and comfort from the past

reversed.summary: Holding on too tightly to the past may be keeping you from enjoying today. Old memories have turned from comfort into a kind of anchor. It is time to keep what mattered and look ahead. Growing up doesn't mean forgetting.
reversed.love: You may be idealising a past relationship or repeating an old pattern without noticing. Comparing the present to a polished memory isn't fair to anyone. Try to see the person in front of you clearly, as they are now. Real connection lives in the present.
reversed.career: Old methods or past successes may no longer fit how things work today. Hanging on to how it used to be can hold your progress back. Be willing to update your skills and your approach. Moving with the times keeps you relevant.
reversed.money: Spend in a way that suits your life now, not on what recalls an earlier time or feeling. Nostalgic purchases can add up quietly. Check whether your habits still match your current priorities. Let your choices grow up with you.
reversed.health: Longing for an earlier time may be weighing on your mood. Comparing your energy or life now to the past can be discouraging. Build new routines that suit who you are today. Present-focused care is more helpful.
reversed.family: Family roles may need to grow along with the people in them. Adult children, ageing parents and siblings all change over time. Let relationships adjust instead of expecting old patterns to stay the same. Respecting who people are now helps everyone.
reversed.general: Nostalgia has turned into something that holds you back. You may be revisiting the past for answers it can't give. Moving forward doesn't erase what mattered to you. It simply makes room for what comes next.
reversed.yes_no: This leans mixed to no. Looking back too much clouds the decision right now. If the choice relies on recreating something old, it may not work. Ground the question in the present first.
reversed.timing: Things move slowly until you loosen your grip on the past. Movement starts once you focus on what is in front of you now. The sooner you shift your attention, the sooner things pick up. Let the season change.
reversed.advice: Keep the memory, but let go of the longing. Thank the past for what it gave you and step into today. Try one new thing that belongs to your present life. Growth is a kindness to yourself.
reversed.thread: a past that is holding you back and a need to move on

cards.name: Seven of Cups
cards.image_prompt: Seven golden cups floating in midnight clouds, each holding a symbol: jewels, castle, wreath, dragon, veiled figure.

upright.summary: There are many options in front of you right now, and they are not all equally solid. Some are real chances. Others are mostly hope and imagination. Enjoy the daydreaming, because it shows you what you long for. Then sort the dreams from the plans you can actually carry out.
upright.love: You may be falling for who someone could become rather than who they are today. That is easy to do when the hope feels sweet. For a while, watch what they actually do: whether they turn up, keep small promises and treat you kindly when nothing is at stake. Let those plain facts count for more than the picture in your head.
upright.career: Too many ideas can spread your energy so thin that nothing moves. That might be a side project, a course, a new role or a business you keep sketching. Pick the one that excites you and also fits your current time and skills. Test it properly for a few weeks before chasing the next shiny thing.
upright.money: An offer or plan that sounds almost too good is worth a slow second look. Ask plain questions, read the fine print, and notice whether you feel rushed or flattered. If something only makes sense when you picture the best case, think it over more. Wait until you have the full picture before you decide.
upright.health: A busy mind full of plans can tire you as much as a long day of work. Holding too many possibilities at once keeps your thoughts loud and your sleep light. A simple, repeatable routine can give your mind somewhere to rest. Regular meals, a short walk and a fixed time to switch off screens are good places to start.
upright.family: Everyone at home may have a different idea about what to do next. That could be a holiday plan, a move, who hosts Chinese New Year or how to care for an older relative. When all the options stay open, people talk past each other. Sit down together, write the choices out, and narrow the list until a few real ones remain.
upright.general: Your imagination is strong right now, and so is the pull of wishful thinking. Both can be useful if you know which one you are using. Some of what appeals to you is workable and some is just pleasant to picture. Your task is to tell them apart gently, without judging yourself for dreaming.
upright.yes_no: Maybe. Several answers look possible from where you stand, and some may be wishful thinking. Before you commit, check which outcome is real and well supported. Once you know that, the answer will be easier to see.
upright.timing: This is a time for browsing, comparing and weighing things up. That has its uses, but it can stretch on if you let it. Things start moving once you stop collecting options and start crossing some off. Expect the pace to pick up soon after you narrow things down.
upright.advice: Write every option on one page, then mark the ones that are realistic with the time, money and energy you have now. Cross out the ones that only work in a perfect world. Choose one of the remaining options and take one small, practical step toward it this week.
upright.thread: many tempting options, and the work of finding the real one

reversed.summary: The fog is lifting, and your options look plainer and more honest than before. Some dreams fade, and that can feel like a small relief rather than a loss. You are closer to a decision than it felt even recently. Trust what you now see clearly.
reversed.love: You have a clearer sense of what you want from closeness and what you no longer want. That clarity is worth acting on. You can stop guessing and say what you need plainly and kindly. Let your actions follow what you now know, rather than old fantasies.
reversed.career: Focusing on one direction will start to show results. Dropping or pausing side ideas may feel like giving something up. In practice it frees time and energy for work that can actually grow. Commit to the main path for a set period, then review how it is going honestly.
reversed.money: Wishful thinking is giving way to a more realistic view of your money. Looking at the real numbers may feel sobering at first. It usually brings calm, because you are no longer planning around guesses. Decisions based on what you actually have tend to feel steadier.
reversed.health: Cutting back on distractions and overcommitment can bring real relief. With fewer things pulling at you, your energy can gather again. Notice which commitments drain you most and which you could politely drop. Quiet evenings and fewer open tabs, in every sense, may help more than you expect.
reversed.family: A muddled family question gets easier once people say plainly what they want. They can stop hinting or going along to keep the peace. One honest conversation can clear up weeks of confusion. Encourage everyone, yourself included, to name their real preference.
reversed.general: A reality check is arriving, and it feels more like relief than disappointment. Seeing things as they are lets you stop circling and start committing. Not every dream has to go. It just needs to stand on solid ground before you build on it.
reversed.yes_no: Leans yes, as long as you choose the clear, grounded option rather than the dreamy one. If the answer still looks good in practical terms, you can move ahead. If it only shines in imagination, wait.
reversed.timing: Clarity comes fairly soon, once you stop going round the same options. You may notice one choice quietly standing out. After you decide, things move faster than they have for a while. Momentum follows commitment here.
reversed.advice: Choose the option you would still stand behind on an ordinary, tired Tuesday, not only on a hopeful night. Tell someone you trust what you have decided so it feels real. Then take the first concrete step without reopening every other door.
reversed.thread: clearer sight, sharper focus and a decision ready to be made

cards.name: Eight of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A cloaked figure walking away from eight stacked golden cups toward mountains under a crescent moon.

upright.summary: Something in your life may look perfectly fine from the outside but no longer satisfies you on the inside. This card describes a quiet inner turning, a sense that you've taken what you can from a situation and are looking for something more meaningful. It isn't about drama or blame, just honesty about what fulfils you now. The path ahead may not be fully visible yet, and that's okay.
upright.love: Ask yourself honestly whether this connection still nourishes you, or whether you're both mostly going through the motions. That question doesn't call for a dramatic decision, only for reflection and an open conversation. A little breathing space, like time with friends or a few quiet evenings alone, may help you see things more clearly. What matters is understanding your own needs before deciding anything.
upright.career: Work may feel hollow even when the results look good on paper. You might be doing well, getting decent feedback, and still wondering what the point is. That restlessness deserves careful thought rather than an impulsive move. Consider what kind of purpose you're missing, and whether it could come from new responsibilities, learning, or interests outside the office.
upright.money: Think about what you keep paying for, in money, time or energy, that no longer gives much back. It might be a subscription you never use, a commitment you keep out of habit, or an expensive routine that's lost its joy. Spotting these quietly can free up resources for things that matter more to you now. This is about awareness, not any specific financial move.
upright.health: Emotional tiredness may be asking you to slow down. When something has stopped feeling meaningful, carrying on as usual can be draining in ways that are hard to explain. Some time alone, a slower weekend, or a walk somewhere green like the Botanic Gardens can help you recover. Give yourself permission to rest without needing a reason.
upright.family: You may need a bit more space, or a slightly different role, within your family's expectations. Perhaps you've been the one who always organises, mediates or gives way, and it's wearing thin. You can shift that gently, by explaining what you need clearly and kindly rather than simply pulling away. Loved ones usually adjust better when they understand why.
upright.general: A chapter feels like it's closing, and you're the one choosing to turn the page. You don't have all the answers about what comes next, but staying exactly where you are no longer feels right. That uncertainty is a normal part of growth. Trust the quiet sense that you're looking for something truer.
upright.yes_no: This leans no, especially if you're asking whether to keep things exactly as they are. The card suggests that a familiar arrangement has run its course in some way. The better answer is likely to involve change, a new direction, or a different way of approaching the situation, taken thoughtfully and at your own pace.
upright.timing: This is a slow, considered transition, not a sudden leap. Expect a quieter period between what you're leaving behind and whatever comes next. That in-between stretch can feel empty, but it's where your direction gradually takes shape. Don't rush it, because clarity comes with time.
upright.advice: Let go with care rather than in a hurry. Take the lessons, friendships and good memories with you, and leave behind only what genuinely no longer fits. Talk things through with someone you trust before making any big decisions. Then walk, one steady step at a time, toward what feels more honest and meaningful.
upright.thread: a quiet choice to move beyond what no longer fulfils

reversed.summary: You're caught between going and staying, and you can't quite decide. Fear of change, comfort with routine, or nagging second thoughts may be keeping you where you are. Part of you knows something needs to shift, while another part wants to hold on. This is a time for honest reflection rather than forcing a decision.
reversed.love: You may be holding on to something because it feels safe, or because you're afraid of being alone, rather than because it truly makes you happy. Or you might be pulling away and then coming back, unsure what you want. Be honest with yourself, and where appropriate with the other person, about what you really need. Clarity about your own feelings comes before any decision.
reversed.career: You may be drifting in a role that doesn't quite fit, not committing to it and not deciding anything else either. That limbo can quietly sap your motivation. Before considering any big move, spend some time reflecting on what's actually bothering you and what you'd want instead. Sometimes small adjustments or honest conversations help more than you expect.
reversed.money: Watch for spending or commitments that carry on purely out of habit. You might keep paying for something because cancelling feels like admitting a mistake, or because changing it seems like too much effort. A calm review of your regular outgoings can show what's still worthwhile. Treat it as housekeeping, not a judgement on past choices.
reversed.health: Restlessness and indecision can be surprisingly draining. Going over the same question again and again may leave you tired, irritable or unable to switch off. Gentle routines, like regular sleep, light exercise and time away from screens, can give your mind some ground to stand on. Journaling may help you see what you're really feeling.
reversed.family: Old patterns or a strong sense of loyalty may keep you in a family role that feels too small for who you are now. You may stay quiet to keep the peace, even when it costs you. For now, simply notice where this happens and how it feels. Understanding the pattern clearly is the first step before changing anything.
reversed.general: You know something feels off, but you aren't ready to act on it yet. That hesitation isn't failure, it's information about what you value and what scares you. Staying a bit longer while you work things out is fine. Just be careful that pausing doesn't quietly turn into avoiding the question altogether.
reversed.yes_no: This leans no for now. You don't seem settled enough within yourself to act with confidence. Rather than pushing for a yes, give yourself more time to understand what's holding you back, and come back to the question when you feel steadier.
reversed.timing: The pace is slow and a little uncertain. Things are unlikely to move much until you face whatever is keeping you in place, whether that's fear, habit or unspoken doubts. Once you understand that, movement tends to follow fairly naturally. Be patient with yourself in the meantime.
reversed.advice: Write down what you're afraid of losing if things change, and what you're afraid of missing if they don't. Seeing both lists side by side often makes the real question clearer. Talk it over with someone who'll listen without pushing you either way. Then make the decision that you can live with calmly, not the one driven by panic.
reversed.thread: hesitation, habit, and mixed feelings about leaving or staying

cards.name: Nine of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A smiling figure seated before an arc of nine golden cups on midnight drapery, warm gold light.

upright.summary: Contentment is close, and a wish you've been quietly holding may well come true. This card is about the simple pleasure of things going right, whether that's comfort, recognition or a long-awaited result. You're allowed to enjoy it without guilt or waiting for the catch. Let yourself feel satisfied for a while.
upright.love: There's warmth and ease in your love life right now. If you're in a relationship, enjoy the comfortable moments together without searching for problems that aren't there. If you're single, you may feel content in your own company, which makes connecting with others feel lighter. Either way, appreciate what feels good and say so out loud.
upright.career: You may feel genuinely satisfied with your work and what it has earned you. Recognition, a good review or a finished project could confirm that your effort was worthwhile. Take a moment to acknowledge this rather than jumping straight to the next goal. Feeling proud of good work is healthy, and it gives you energy for later.
upright.money: There's a sense of comfort and having enough. Even if not everything is perfect, the basics feel steady, and that's worth appreciating. Gratitude for this stability can help you keep sensible habits going. Enjoy small treats within your means, and remember this feeling of security when making future plans.
upright.health: You may feel more at ease in both body and mind. Good food, decent rest and pleasant company are all supporting your wellbeing. This is a good time to notice which habits help you feel this way, so you can come back to them when life gets busier. Simply enjoying a slow meal or a relaxed evening can be restorative.
upright.family: Shared meals, relaxed conversations and easy time together bring real pleasure at home. It might be a weekend dinner at the kopitiam or a quiet evening watching something together. These ordinary moments are worth treasuring, even if they don't seem special. Let people know you're glad to have them around.
upright.general: Things are going well, and it's fine to admit it. You don't need to push harder or immediately raise the bar. This is a time to enjoy what you have and the progress you've made. Contentment, when you let yourself feel it, tends to make you kinder and more generous too.
upright.yes_no: Yes. This card leans clearly toward a satisfying outcome. What you're hoping for looks likely to work out, or may already be falling into place. Keep your expectations reasonable and enjoy the good result when it comes.
upright.timing: The good result is near, or may already be here without you fully noticing. There's no need to rush on to the next thing straight away. Give yourself time to enjoy the moment and let it sink in. This is a season of reaping rather than striving.
upright.advice: Take stock of what's going well and say thank you, to others and to yourself. Share your good news with people who'll be happy for you. Resist the urge to immediately look for what's missing. Letting yourself fully enjoy this moment is the most useful thing you can do.
upright.thread: contentment, gratitude, and a wish close to coming true

reversed.summary: Something feels missing, even though things look fine on paper. You may have got what you wanted and found it less satisfying than expected, or a wish may be taking longer than hoped. This card gently suggests that lasting contentment comes more from inside than from outside achievements. It's a time to look at what really fulfils you.
reversed.love: Surface wishes, like a grand gesture, a particular milestone or a certain type of partner, may be hiding a deeper need for closeness or reassurance. Ask yourself what would actually make you feel loved and connected. Then share that honestly, in simple words. Small, sincere moments often matter more than the big picture you imagined.
reversed.career: Success may not feel as rewarding as you thought it would. A promotion, title or achievement might leave you strangely flat. This doesn't mean it wasn't worth it, only that you may need to rethink what you really want from your work. Meaning, growth or balance might matter more to you now than the next milestone.
reversed.money: Buying or collecting more may not fill the gap you're feeling. Shopping for comfort can give a quick lift that fades just as quickly. Try to notice when spending is about mood rather than need. Keeping your wants and your means in balance will feel better in the long run.
reversed.health: Overindulging to feel better, whether in food, screens, drinks or late nights, may only work for a short while. If you notice yourself reaching for comfort often, ask what you're really craving: rest, connection, or simply a break. Small, kind changes can help more than strict rules. Be gentle with yourself while you work it out.
reversed.family: Comfort at home may feel flat or taken for granted. Everyone might be going through the motions without really noticing each other. Small gestures of appreciation, like a thank you, a shared snack or asking how someone's day really went, can change the mood. Warmth often returns when it's acknowledged.
reversed.general: A wish may be delayed, or it may come true but feel less satisfying than you hoped. Either way, the lesson is about where satisfaction really comes from. Chasing the next thing won't fill a gap that's really about meaning or connection. Looking inward first will help you choose what's truly worth wanting.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed, leaning no. You might get what you're asking about, but it may not bring the satisfaction you expect. Before pushing for it, consider whether it's what you truly need or just what you think you should want.
reversed.timing: Things move slowly here, with a need to reflect before going further. Satisfaction tends to grow once your expectations settle and you're clearer about what matters. Don't rush to fill the gap with the next goal. Give yourself time to adjust.
reversed.advice: Look closely at what's already good in your life and give it some credit. Then ask yourself honestly what you need, as opposed to what you simply want. Small, meaningful changes may bring more contentment than big new goals. Let inner satisfaction lead and outward wishes follow.
reversed.thread: a gap between what you have and how it feels

cards.name: Ten of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A family beneath a rainbow of ten golden cups across a midnight sky, a cosy home with gold windows.

upright.summary: This card is about the quiet happiness of belonging somewhere and to someone. The people around you feel close, and the relationships that matter most feel settled rather than fragile. It's less about a big event and more about a steady warmth that runs through ordinary days. Notice it and enjoy it, because this kind of contentment is easy to take for granted.
upright.love: A loving bond built on shared values is favoured here. You may feel that being with this person is like coming home, safe and understood, with no need to perform. If you're single, think about what kind of everyday life you want to share, not only the spark. For couples, small rituals like a weekly makan or an evening walk strengthen what is already good.
upright.career: Work and home are in better balance, and each one supports the other. A kind team, a reasonable manager or a workplace that respects your time can make a real difference now. You might feel proud of work that benefits more than just yourself. Protect this balance by keeping clear limits on after-hours messages where you can.
upright.money: Money feels more secure, and it feels shared rather than something you carry alone. The household may agree on priorities more easily, whether that's a family trip, a comfortable home or simply less worry. This is a good time to talk openly about common goals while everyone is in a cooperative mood. The steadiness comes from agreement, not from any big windfall.
upright.health: Connection is doing your wellbeing real good. Time with people who accept you can lift your mood, ease stress and help you rest more deeply. Shared meals, laughter and unhurried conversation all count as care. Keep making room for them, even when your schedule fills up.
upright.family: Home feels warm and united. Gatherings, festive visits and simple dinners are likely to go smoothly, with room for both old jokes and new news. Different generations may find common ground more easily than usual. Take photos, tell stories and let everyone feel included.
upright.general: There's a strong sense of emotional fulfilment here, the feeling that what matters most is close by. You may notice gratitude coming more easily. This harmony isn't perfection. It's people choosing each other again and again. Let that be enough, and let it steady you.
upright.yes_no: Yes. This card leans clearly towards a happy and harmonious outcome, especially where relationships, home or shared plans are involved. The result looks likely to bring comfort to more than one person. Go ahead with care and generosity, and include the people it affects.
upright.timing: Good things here build steadily and last, rather than arriving all at once. Think of a season of slow growth, where trust and comfort deepen with each shared experience. Patience pays off because the foundations are sound. What grows now is likely to hold.
upright.advice: Spend real, unhurried time with the people who feel like home, and tell them plainly what they mean to you. Put your phone away during meals and really listen. Keep small traditions going, because they are what holds a family or friendship together. Gratitude said out loud strengthens bonds more than you might expect.
upright.thread: warm belonging, shared values, and happiness that lasts with family

reversed.summary: Home or close relationships feel a little out of tune. Nothing may be badly wrong, but expectations, values or routines have drifted apart. The picture you hoped for and the life you're living don't quite match. That gap is worth noticing gently, without blame, so it can start to close.
reversed.love: You and your partner may be picturing different futures, or simply getting less from each other than before. Talk about values and hopes calmly, using 'I' statements rather than accusations. Listen for what your partner needs, not just what they're doing wrong. Reconnection often starts with one honest, kind conversation.
reversed.career: Work may be taking time and energy that home life needs. Long hours, late chats or constant tiredness can leave loved ones feeling second. Look at where small changes are possible, such as protecting one evening a week or a proper weekend morning. Even modest shifts in balance can ease the tension at home.
reversed.money: Money may be causing friction in the household, perhaps because people have different priorities or don't feel heard. Avoiding the topic usually makes it heavier. Sit down together, list what matters to each person and look for shared ground. Keeping the conversation regular and calm matters more than getting it perfect in one go.
reversed.health: Ongoing tension at home can leave you drained, restless or on edge. Notice how your body reacts after difficult conversations. Calming habits like a short walk, earlier nights or quiet time alone can help you reset. If the strain feels heavy, talking with a trusted friend or counsellor can also help.
reversed.family: There may be distance, misunderstanding or quiet resentment in the family. Some relatives may feel left out, or old disagreements may come back up. Simple shared time, without heavy topics, can reopen the door. Not every issue needs solving at once. Warmth comes first.
reversed.general: Your ideal and your reality don't line up right now, and that can feel disappointing. Real families and relationships are always a bit messy. Instead of chasing a perfect picture, look for one or two things that would make things feel more connected. The gap can close gradually with honest effort.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, leaning no for now. The harmony you want isn't fully in place yet, and pushing ahead may stir up more friction. It needs more effort, patience and honest conversation first. Once people feel heard, the answer may change.
reversed.timing: Progress is slow and uneven, with good days and awkward ones. Repair happens through small gestures repeated over weeks rather than one grand fix. Expect a gradual thaw, not a sudden turnaround. Steady kindness is what moves things forward.
reversed.advice: Share a meal, listen without trying to fix anything and let people finish their thoughts. Drop the need for a picture-perfect family and aim for real connection instead. Apologise where it's fair, and appreciate small efforts from others. Little moments of warmth add up.
reversed.thread: family distance and the gap between ideal and real home life

cards.name: Page of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A youth holding a golden cup with a small fish peeking out, midnight shoreline, gold wave patterns.

upright.summary: A gentle message, a creative spark or a small pleasant surprise may come your way. The energy is light, curious and open-hearted. You don't need to analyse everything right now. Simply notice what delights or moves you. Small feelings can point somewhere meaningful.
upright.love: A sweet text, a thoughtful gesture or the start of a tender feeling could brighten your days. It may be shy or playful rather than dramatic. Respond with openness and some courage, even if you feel a bit awkward. For couples, a small surprise or a funny note can bring the softness back.
upright.career: Creative ideas come easily now, sometimes at odd moments like on the MRT or in the shower. Write them down before they fade, even if they seem half-formed. A fresh, curious approach may help you solve a problem others have been stuck on. Junior roles, new projects or creative side work are especially well supported.
upright.money: Your instinct may give a useful nudge about a purchase or plan. Treat it as a starting point, not a final answer. Check the facts, compare options and give yourself time before acting. Curiosity about learning money basics could also serve you well.
upright.health: Play and lightness are good for your mood and energy. Make room for something you simply enjoy, like drawing, music, a swim or a silly film with friends. These moments refill you more than you might think. Let yourself be a beginner at something without pressure.
upright.family: A child or young relative may bring joy, news or a funny moment that lightens the home. Gentle humour can smooth over small tensions. Be open to hearing someone's feelings or dreams, even if they seem young or unusual. Encouragement now goes a long way.
upright.general: This is a soft, imaginative moment that asks you to listen to your feelings without overthinking them. Something small, like a song, a conversation or an idea, may carry more meaning than it seems. Stay curious. You're allowed to be tender and hopeful.
upright.yes_no: Yes. This card leans positive, especially for creative, emotional or relationship questions. The start may be small, but it's sincere. Say yes with an open heart and let it grow naturally.
upright.timing: News or inspiration is likely to arrive soon and lightly, often without warning. It starts small, like a seed or a first message. Whether it grows depends on how you nurture it over the following weeks. Pay attention to early signs.
upright.advice: Follow your curiosity and let yourself play. Give one small idea or feeling a chance to develop instead of judging it too quickly. Keep a notebook or voice memo handy. Openness and a little courage will take you further than perfection.
upright.thread: a gentle message, creative spark, and open-hearted curiosity

reversed.summary: Moods may swing more than usual, or your creativity may feel stuck. Small things can feel bigger than they are. Go easy on yourself and try not to react straight away. This is about inner work, learning to hold feelings without letting them steer every decision.
reversed.love: You might be reading too much into a short reply, a delay or a passing look. Guessing tends to feed worry. Ask plainly and kindly instead of building stories in your head. If you feel insecure, say so honestly rather than testing the other person.
reversed.career: A creative block is frustrating, but forcing ideas usually makes it worse. Step back, rest and take in something inspiring that has nothing to do with work. Do routine tasks in the meantime so you keep moving. Ideas often come back once the pressure eases.
reversed.money: Spending driven by mood is a real risk, such as a late-night online cart or a treat to cheer yourself up. Give yourself a 24-hour pause before buying anything non-essential. Notice which feelings make you want to spend. Small comforts are fine, but keep them within your plan.
reversed.health: Emotions may feel big and tiring, leaving you flat or restless. Rest, journaling or a talk with a friend can help you process them. Try not to escape too much into scrolling or distraction. If heavy feelings stay with you, consider speaking with a counsellor.
reversed.family: Someone at home may be sensitive, sulky or easily hurt, and it might be you. Patience and a calm tone go a long way. Avoid teasing or bringing up old issues while feelings are raw. A quiet check-in later often works better than confronting it in the moment.
reversed.general: Your feelings are running ahead of your ability to make sense of them. That's human, not a failure. Slow down and name what's going on, whether that's hurt, boredom or longing. Once you name it, it usually loosens its grip.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, leaning no for now. Your current mood may be colouring how you see things. Wait until you feel steadier before deciding. A clearer answer will come when you're calmer.
reversed.timing: Things feel uneven and changeable for now. Progress may stop and start along with your moods. Once your feelings settle, things tend to steady as well. Give it a little time and don't rush.
reversed.advice: Name your feelings kindly and without judgement, and give yourself proper rest. Put off big choices until you feel calm. Choose gentle comforts over escape. Be as patient with yourself as you would be with a young friend.
reversed.thread: shifting moods and a creative spark that needs gentler handling

cards.name: Knight of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A knight on a calm white horse offering a golden cup, winged helmet, river under a midnight sky.

upright.summary: A heartfelt invitation, offer or romantic gesture may arrive. It comes from a sincere place and can feel lovely to receive. Respond with warmth, and keep your judgement switched on too. The best path combines feeling with good sense.
upright.love: Charm, romance and thoughtful gestures are in the air, such as a surprise date, a heartfelt message or an open declaration. Enjoy it fully while still paying attention to who this person is day to day. For couples, it's a good time to bring back romance with intention. Let the feeling be real, and let trust build at its own pace.
upright.career: A creative or meaningful proposal may appeal to you, perhaps a project that matches your values or a role that feels inspiring. Consider whether it works in practice, including workload, pay structure and the people involved. Passion is a strength here, but it needs a plan behind it. Ask questions before you commit.
upright.money: You may be drawn to a choice that feels good emotionally, like a dream purchase or a heartfelt cause. Look at the numbers as well as the dream. Check costs, timelines and what you might be giving up. A short pause won't spoil a good idea.
upright.health: Following what feels nourishing can help, such as gentle movement, time in nature at the Botanic Gardens or creative rest. Choose habits you'll actually enjoy, so they last. Avoid all-or-nothing enthusiasm that fades in a week. Steady, pleasant routines work best.
upright.family: A kind gesture or invitation could soften things at home. You might be the one who reaches out with a visit, a meal or a thoughtful message. Offer it sincerely, without expecting a particular response. Warmth given freely tends to come back over time.
upright.general: Idealism and sincerity are strong, and an offer in front of you is probably genuine. It still needs a grounded response. Ask how it fits your real life, not only your hopes. When heart and head agree, you can move forward with confidence.
upright.yes_no: Maybe, leaning yes. The offer is appealing and sincere, but check that it works in practice before you agree. Look at the details, the commitment and the follow-through. If those hold up, it's a good yes.
upright.timing: Things move smoothly rather than quickly. Offers and invitations arrive, then need time to show what they're really worth. Expect a graceful unfolding over weeks rather than overnight results. Enjoy the courtship phase, whatever the area of life.
upright.advice: Lead with your heart, but read the details before you say yes. Ask the practical questions that romance tends to skip. Stay generous and open, and let consistency confirm what your feelings suggest. Sincerity and sense can work together.
upright.thread: a heartfelt offer that needs both feeling and sense

reversed.summary: Promises may sound better than they turn out to be. Charm, big words or dreamy plans may not be backed by steady action. Look at what people do, not just what they say, and apply the same standard to yourself. Seeing clearly now protects your heart and your time.
reversed.love: Charm without consistency is a warning sign. Notice whether affection shows up reliably or only when it suits the other person. Watch your own jealousy or moodiness too, because it can cloud what's really happening. Honest, calm conversations help more than grand gestures.
reversed.career: An exciting offer or pitch may hide gaps. Ask for specifics in writing, such as scope, pay, timelines and who is responsible for what. If answers stay vague, be cautious. Make sure there's real substance behind the enthusiasm.
reversed.money: A dreamy plan without clear numbers is risky. Before committing, ask for details, costs and realistic outcomes. Be wary of anything that leans on emotion or urgency to persuade you. A calm, factual review will show you whether it holds up.
reversed.health: Mood swings and wishful thinking may pull you away from routines that support you. You may start ambitious plans and then drop them. Simple, steady habits like regular sleep, meals and a short walk help you stay balanced. Consistency matters more than intensity.
reversed.family: Someone may promise more than they can deliver, and it might be you. Be honest about what's realistic with your time and energy. Small promises kept build more trust than big ones broken. Clear, kind expectations reduce disappointment at home.
reversed.general: Your ideal and your reality are some distance apart right now. That isn't a disaster. It's information. Seeing the gap clearly helps you avoid hurt and make wiser choices. Let your hopes stay, and ground them in facts.
reversed.yes_no: Leans no for now. Words and actions don't yet match, so it's wise to wait. Watch whether there's real follow-through before committing. If consistency appears, you can think again.
reversed.timing: This will be slow to prove itself. Time is the real test, and it will show who follows through and who only talks. Give it several weeks of watching behaviour before deciding. Patience protects you here.
reversed.advice: Balance feeling with facts. Judge people and offers by how consistent they are over weeks, not by one lovely moment. Ask direct questions and notice your own tendency to idealise. Keep your heart open, and keep your eyes open too.
reversed.thread: fine words, uneven follow-through, and a need for realism

cards.name: Queen of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A queen on a shore throne gazing into an ornate golden lidded cup, midnight sea, gold shell carvings.

upright.summary: This card shows someone who stays steady and kind while noticing what people feel, including you. You can sense the mood in a room without getting swept away by it. Others tend to relax around you because you listen properly instead of rushing to fix things. Right now that quiet warmth is one of your best resources, so trust it.
upright.love: Closeness grows through patient, gentle attention more than grand gestures. Say how you feel in plain words, then leave real room for your partner's answer, even if it is slow or messy. If you are single, notice who feels easy to be honest with, because that is worth more than quick sparks. Small acts of care, like remembering what someone said last week, mean a lot here.
upright.career: You read people well, so you often notice tension or worry before anyone says it. That is useful in teamwork, client work and any role where trust matters. Don't treat it as a soft extra. Let it show, for example by checking in with a struggling colleague or calming a meeting that is getting heated. People will remember how you made the work feel.
upright.money: Your instincts about money tend to be calm rather than panicky, which helps. Still, a good feeling is not the same as good figures. Before any decision, write down the actual amounts, dates and commitments and see whether they match your gut. When heart and numbers agree, you can move forward with more confidence.
upright.health: Your energy follows your mood closely, so looking after your emotions is part of looking after yourself. Gentle routines like a regular bedtime, a quiet cup of tea or a slow walk in a park or by the water can help you settle. Notice what drains you and what restores you, and plan around that. If you feel low for a long time, talking to someone you trust can help.
upright.family: At home you may be the one who calms things down when tempers rise. Your patience can soften a tense talk between relatives or help a younger family member feel heard. Use it with care, and let others do their share of the listening too. A calm meal together or an unhurried chat may do more than a big discussion.
upright.general: Compassion and intuition are your best guides right now. This is a time to respond with care, not to force an outcome or win an argument. Pay attention to the quiet sense you have about people and situations, then check it gently against the facts. Kindness that is also clear-eyed will get you further than pressure.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. The answer seems to fit with what your heart already senses, and the emotional ground looks supportive. Before you commit, quickly check that the practical side agrees: time, effort and any costs. If it does, you can say yes with a settled mind.
upright.timing: Things are moving at a gentle, natural pace, not a sprint. Like water finding its level, the situation will settle as it unfolds. Pushing for quick results may only stir things up. Give it the time it needs and keep showing up steadily.
upright.advice: Trust the quiet instincts you already have, even if they are hard to explain. Be as kind to yourself as you are to others, and rest when you need to. Listen first, then speak simply. A gentle response is often the strongest one you have.
upright.thread: calm compassion and trusting what your heart already quietly senses

reversed.summary: You may be giving more care than you can spare and taking on everyone else's feelings as your own. Somewhere along the way your own needs dropped to the bottom of the list. This isn't a failure of kindness, just a sign your reserves are low. The work now is to turn some of that care back towards yourself.
reversed.love: Care may have turned into constantly fitting yourself around your partner, or worrying about how they feel. That can leave you quietly resentful or unsure of where you stand. Gently say what you need, even something small, and let your partner meet you halfway. A healthy bond has room for both people's feelings, not just theirs.
reversed.career: You may be carrying your colleagues' stress, deadlines or moods as though they were your job to fix. That wears you down and can blur your own priorities. Keep offering support, but set limits on your time and attention. It is fine to say, "I can help with this part, not all of it."
reversed.money: Spending to cheer yourself up, or helping others beyond what you can afford, may be creeping in. The urge comes from a good place, but it can strain your budget. Pause before buying or lending anything, and check your actual figures first. Supporting people in ways that don't cost money can be just as meaningful.
reversed.health: Emotional tiredness is likely, the kind that sleep alone doesn't fully fix. Protect quiet time, cut back on draining conversations and practise saying no a little more often. Notice whose problems you keep taking home with you. If the heaviness hangs on, consider speaking with someone you trust or a qualified professional.
reversed.family: Family members may be leaning on you heavily, maybe because you have always been the dependable one. It is fair to share the load and ask siblings or others to step up. You can still care without being on call all the time. Clear, kind boundaries usually help the whole household in the long run.
reversed.general: Your sensitivity has tipped into overwhelm, and other people's feelings are crowding out your own. The inner work is to protect your energy without closing your heart. Notice where you are overgiving out of guilt or insecurity. Pulling back a little isn't selfish, and it lets you care more steadily.
reversed.yes_no: This one is mixed and leans no for now. You may not be in the best place to judge clearly while you are this stretched. Look after yourself first: rest, step back, settle your feelings. Then ask the question again and see if the answer has changed.
reversed.timing: Progress slows until you have had a proper chance to recover. This is a season for refilling, not for pushing ahead. Rushing now may drain you further. Once your energy comes back, things can start moving again.
reversed.advice: Fill your own cup before you pour for anyone else. Pick one thing this week that is just for you and protect it. Say no to one request you would usually take on without thinking. Your care lasts longer when you look after its source.
reversed.thread: giving past your limits and needing to protect your own energy

cards.name: King of Cups
cards.image_prompt: A king on a stone throne floating on a midnight sea, holding a golden cup, fish and ship in gold detail.

upright.summary: This card shows someone who feels deeply but still thinks clearly. You can stay calm when others are rattled, and that makes you a steady presence. Fair, level-headed leadership is open to you now, whether at work, at home or among friends. Your strength is staying composed without shutting your feelings off.
upright.love: Maturity and dependable care strengthen the relationship. You can talk openly about feelings without turning it into drama or a contest. Being consistent, doing what you say and showing up when it counts builds deep trust. If you are single, you may be drawn to someone emotionally grounded, and you will bring that quality yourself.
upright.career: Your diplomacy is valuable, especially when meetings get tense or teams disagree. People trust you because you listen first and judge fairly. You may be asked to mediate, mentor or lead a sensitive project. Steady communication and a calm tone will earn you more respect than force.
upright.money: Measured, unhurried decisions suit you right now. Instead of reacting to news, trends or how you feel today, think about the long term. Review your plans calmly and stick to what you already understand. Patience and consistency will serve you better than bold moves.
upright.health: Emotional steadiness supports your overall wellbeing. Regular routines such as set mealtimes, steady sleep and a dependable way to unwind after work help keep you balanced. Make some space to decompress before stress builds up. A calm evening walk or quiet reading can be enough.
upright.family: You can be the calm anchor at home, the one people come to when things feel unsettled. Listen first, then offer gentle guidance without taking over or lecturing. Your even temper can help older and younger relatives understand each other. Use your influence to make room for everyone's voice.
upright.general: Your heart and head are working well together. You can feel what is happening and still respond with good judgement. Staying composed under pressure is your strength, and others will notice it. Lead quietly by example.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. A calm, well-considered choice is likely to hold up over time. Make sure you have weighed both the feelings and the facts. If you have, go ahead with quiet confidence.
upright.timing: The pace is steady and measured, not rushed. Good outcomes come through patience and consistent effort. Expect gradual progress you can rely on, not sudden leaps. Keep a calm rhythm and let it build.
upright.advice: Stay composed, listen well and act with kindness. Before you respond, take a breath and consider how the other person feels. Be firm where you need to be, but never cold. Steady fairness is your best tool.
upright.thread: emotional balance and calm, fair-minded judgement under pressure

reversed.summary: Your feelings may be bottled up, or they may be leaking out as irritability and sudden moods. Either way, emotions that don't get proper attention tend to come out sideways. You may be trying hard to look in control while feeling unsettled underneath. What you need is an honest, healthy outlet.
reversed.love: Feelings you haven't said out loud can create distance, even when nothing is obviously wrong. Sulking, hinting or going quiet can leave your partner guessing. Try saying plainly what you feel, even if it feels awkward. Also notice whether either of you is using guilt or silence to get your way.
reversed.career: Pause before you react, especially in tense meetings or over stressful messages. A sharp reply sent in frustration can be hard to take back. Watch for passive-aggressive habits in yourself or others, such as pointed silence or subtle digs. Talking directly and calmly will clear more than hidden tension can.
reversed.money: Decisions made while upset or restless usually cost more later. Avoid big commitments right after an argument or a stressful day. Wait until you feel level, then look at the figures again. Being clear about your feelings first protects your budget.
reversed.health: Stress you hold in may show up as tension, restlessness or poor sleep. Your body often carries what you won't say. Talking to someone, walking it off or writing your thoughts down can release some of the pressure. If it keeps going, consider getting support from someone qualified.
reversed.family: Moods may be setting the tone at home, whether they are yours or someone else's. Own your part honestly and avoid using silence, guilt or a cold shoulder to steer people. A simple, calm apology or a plain explanation can reset the atmosphere. Encourage everyone to say things directly.
reversed.general: Your emotional control has become either too rigid or too shaky. The inner work is to let yourself feel things without being ruled by them. Pretending everything is fine won't help, and neither will blowing up. Look for the middle ground, where feelings are named and then handled.
reversed.yes_no: This leans no for now. Emotions seem to be clouding the question, and a choice made in this state may not last. Wait until things settle and you feel steadier. Then look at it again with a clearer head.
reversed.timing: Expect some turbulence before things calm down. The way forward clears once you have processed what you feel. Rushing now may stir up more trouble. Give yourself time to steady first.
reversed.advice: Breathe, name the feeling, then respond. Even saying "I feel frustrated" to yourself can loosen its grip. Choose one trusted outlet, like a friend, a journal or a walk. Respond from calm, not from the heat of the moment.
reversed.thread: feelings held in or spilling over that need a healthy outlet

cards.name: Ace of Swords
cards.image_prompt: A single upright sword rising from soft midnight clouds, its blade glowing champagne gold, a fine crown floating at the tip.

upright.summary: A clear insight arrives and the fog starts to lift. You can see what is true in a situation and say it simply. It may come as a sudden realisation, a fresh idea or a decision that finally makes sense. Use this clarity well, because it is a real opening.
upright.love: Honest, kind words can clear the air between you. If something has been left unsaid, this is a good time to say it calmly and directly. Clarity helps both people know where they stand. Choose words that are truthful without being harsh.
upright.career: A fresh idea or a clear plan is taking shape. Write it down while it is still sharp, then share it with the right person. You may finally understand how to solve a problem that has been stuck. Clear, simple communication will help others back you.
upright.money: Your numbers look clearer, and a simple plan now feels possible. Lay out what comes in, what goes out and what matters most. Keep the plan plain enough to check easily. Clarity about the facts is the foundation for any sensible next step.
upright.health: Clear thinking helps you see what your body and daily routine actually need. An honest look at sleep, meals, movement and screen time may bring relief. Pick one simple change rather than a complicated overhaul. Seeing things clearly is the first step to feeling better.
upright.family: A direct but gentle conversation could finally sort out an old misunderstanding at home. Stick to facts and keep your tone kind, especially with elders. Saying clearly what you mean can save months of guessing. Listen just as clearly to what others say back.
upright.general: A breakthrough in understanding opens up a path forward. You may suddenly see what was hidden or confusing before. Clarity is the gift here, so use it with care and not as a weapon. The truth, said kindly, can set things moving.
upright.yes_no: This leans yes. The facts seem to support it, and your thinking is clear. Act on what you know rather than waiting for perfect certainty. A clean, honest decision is favoured.
upright.timing: Things move quickly, with a sudden sense of clarity. Insights like this fade if you don't act on them. Follow up soon while the idea is still fresh. Momentum is on your side for now.
upright.advice: Trust the clear thought when it comes, and act on it gently. Write down what you now understand. Say it simply and kindly to whoever needs to hear it. Clarity works best when it is paired with care.
upright.thread: a clear insight that cuts through confusion and names what is true

reversed.summary: Your thinking feels blurry, scattered or rushed right now. You may be jumping to conclusions or getting stuck between too many options. This is temporary, but it isn't a good moment for big decisions. Let the picture settle before you choose.
reversed.love: Messages may be misread, or mixed signals may be passing both ways. A text taken the wrong way can grow into a bigger issue. Ask before you assume, and avoid sharp or sarcastic words. Patience and a clarifying question can prevent a lot of hurt.
reversed.career: Too many ideas may be competing for attention, or you may be judging situations too fast. Pick one idea and test it on a small scale before committing. Double-check emails and instructions for misunderstandings. Slower, clearer thinking will save time later.
reversed.money: The details aren't clear enough yet to act on. Go back to basics: check statements, terms and figures carefully. Avoid deciding on assumptions or half-read information. When the picture is clear, the choice will be easier.
reversed.health: A busy, overthinking mind may be wearing you out. Too much noise, news and screen time can make it harder to think straight. Try short breaks, quieter evenings or writing your thoughts down before bed. Giving your mind some rest helps clarity return.
reversed.family: Misunderstandings may be building up at home. Someone may have heard something different from what was meant. Slow down and confirm what each person actually means before reacting. A calm, clarifying talk can untangle a lot.
reversed.general: Clarity is close but hasn't arrived yet. Gather the missing facts and avoid conclusions based on guesses or rumours. Questioning your own first impressions is part of the work here. Clear understanding will come if you are patient.
reversed.yes_no: This is mixed and leans no for now. Too much is still unclear to give a reliable answer. Wait until you have the facts and your mind has settled. Then the answer is likely to be easier to see.
reversed.timing: Things are slower than you would like. Confusion needs time to clear before you can move forward. Don't force a decision just to end the uncertainty. Wait until your thinking feels steady again.
reversed.advice: Slow down and ask one more question before you decide. Check the facts and your assumptions. Avoid sending anything sharp in a hurry. Clarity will come if you give it room.
reversed.thread: confusion and hasty conclusions that need time to settle

cards.name: Two of Swords
cards.image_prompt: A calm blindfolded figure on a stone bench holding two crossed gold swords, a crescent moon over a still midnight sea.

upright.summary: Two paths sit evenly in front of you, and you have chosen to stand still between them for now. That stillness can be sensible, because it gives you time to steady yourself before committing. Still, a pause only helps if it ends at some point. Use this quiet stretch to gather what you need, and remember that not choosing is a choice too.
upright.love: You may be keeping your real feelings folded away, maybe to protect yourself or to keep the peace. The tension you feel often comes from what is going unsaid, not from the relationship itself. A calm, unhurried talk, perhaps over a simple meal or a walk, could ease a lot. You do not need every answer before you speak. Being honest about where you stand is enough to begin.
upright.career: A work decision is waiting, and you may have been circling it for a while. Try writing the facts for each side on one page: workload, people, growth, and how each option fits the next year or two. Seeing it in plain ink often shows that one side quietly outweighs the other. If you are still unsure, ask one trusted colleague for their view rather than polling everyone.
upright.money: Two options may look almost the same at first, whether that is a plan, a purchase, or a commitment. Line them up side by side and include the less obvious parts like fees, lock-in periods, and how much effort each one takes. A plain comparison usually breaks the tie. If it does not, it is fine to hold off until you understand both clearly.
upright.health: Holding yourself braced against a decision can show up as stiff shoulders, a tight jaw, or shallow breathing. Give yourself a few minutes of slow breathing, or a quiet moment away from your screen. When the body loosens, it becomes easier to hear what you actually need. Rest here is about steadying yourself, not avoiding the question.
upright.family: You may feel caught between two relatives, or between what the family expects and what you want. Staying neutral for a while can protect everyone while feelings settle. But keeping the peace forever can turn into quiet resentment. When the time feels right, gently say where you stand, even if it is only to one person first.
upright.general: This is a standoff, and it asks for both patience and honesty. You need the facts, but you also need the courage to act on them once you have them. Notice whether you are waiting for clarity or waiting for the problem to go away on its own. The first is wise, and the second rarely works.
upright.yes_no: Mixed, for now. The matter is still in the balance and has not tipped either way. More clarity is needed, and some of it has to come from you being honest about what you want. Ask again once you have looked at both sides properly.
upright.timing: This is a holding season, and things feel suspended. Movement usually returns once the avoided choice is finally faced. The pace is up to you more than it seems. Things can start moving as soon as you make up your mind.
upright.advice: Accept the pause, because it can be useful time. Use it to collect the facts and listen to your own instincts. Then set a point where you will decide, and keep to it. A choice made with care is better than a choice that drifts for months.
upright.thread: a quiet standoff where an important choice is still waiting

reversed.summary: The waiting has started to feel heavy, and you may be stuck under too many opinions, articles, and what-ifs. Information helps up to a point, but past that point it only blurs the picture. The good news is that the blindfold is slipping. You already know more than you think, and the way forward is becoming easier to see.
reversed.love: Topics that were tucked away are coming up, sometimes all at once. That can be uncomfortable, especially if you both preferred not to look at them. Yet there is often relief in finally saying the thing aloud. Go slowly, listen as much as you speak, and treat this as a chance to understand each other better.
reversed.career: Colleagues, family, and online advice may all be pulling you in different directions. Step back from the noise and go back to what you have seen for yourself in your own work. Your direct experience counts for more than secondhand views. Trust your own reading of the situation, and check only the facts that really matter.
reversed.money: Endless comparing, with more tabs, more reviews, and more spreadsheets, can wear you down without helping. If two choices are close enough, either may serve you reasonably well. Give yourself a simple deadline and decide with the information you already have. If the matter is complex, a qualified professional can help you sort out the important points.
reversed.health: Overthinking may be costing you sleep or leaving you foggy during the day. Try to stop the late-night research and give your mind a proper break before bed. A short walk, a warm shower, or writing your worries down can help. If restlessness continues, it is reasonable to talk it through with someone you trust or a professional.
reversed.family: Tension at home has become hard to ignore, and everyone may be feeling it. Carrying it in silence tends to be more tiring than speaking up. Opening the conversation gently, at a calm moment, may bring more relief than you expect. You do not have to fix everything in one talk.
reversed.general: You are starting to see the situation as it is, not as you feared or hoped. That can feel unsettling at first, but it is real progress. The choice is closer than it feels. Trust what is now in front of you.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed. The answer is not clear-cut either way, and searching for more information may not change that. Decide based on what you already know rather than what you hope to discover. Clarity tends to follow the decision, not the other way round.
reversed.timing: A decision point is close. Things have dragged, but they are ready to move. Give yourself a short, clear deadline, perhaps a few days. Once you choose, events tend to pick up pace.
reversed.advice: Take off the blindfold and look plainly at what is there. Cut back the outside noise and listen to your own judgement. Pick one sensible next step and take it. You can adjust as you go.
reversed.thread: indecision breaking open as hidden matters finally ask to be faced

cards.name: Three of Swords
cards.image_prompt: A soft gold heart pierced by three slender swords, gentle rain falling from midnight clouds that are beginning to part.

upright.summary: Something tender is hurting, and it wants to be acknowledged rather than brushed aside. This could be a disappointment, a hard truth or the loss of something you hoped for. Naming the pain plainly, to yourself or to someone you trust, is the first step toward easing it. The ache is real, but it is not the whole story of your life.
upright.love: A painful truth may come out, or old hurts may be felt more sharply than before. Be gentle with yourself and with the other person, even if you feel let down. Try not to say things meant only to wound, as they are hard to take back. Giving yourself time to feel before you respond can protect both your heart and the relationship.
upright.career: A setback, a rejected proposal or blunt feedback may sting more than expected. It is natural to feel hurt, especially if you put a lot of yourself into the work. Give yourself a day before deciding what it means. Then keep the useful part of the lesson and leave the rest, because one disappointment does not define your worth or your future.
upright.money: A financial disappointment may need accepting, such as a plan that did not work out as hoped. Dwelling on blame will not help much now. Look calmly at what happened and note one or two lessons for next time. Then reset your budget or plans at a steady, realistic pace.
upright.health: Emotional pain often shows up in the body as a heavy chest, tiredness or poor sleep. Treat yourself with the care you would offer a friend going through the same thing. Talking to someone you trust, journalling or simply resting can help. If the heaviness lingers, reaching out to a counsellor or doctor is a sensible, caring step.
upright.family: A painful matter at home may come to light, perhaps something long left unsaid. People may react with tears, anger or silence. Listen with care, and give each person room to feel without rushing them to be fine. Healing in families often starts with simply being heard.
upright.general: Heartache is present here, and it is also honest. Something needed to be felt, and pretending otherwise would only push it deeper. Let yourself acknowledge the hurt without letting it become who you are. Feeling it fully, with support around you, is how it begins to ease.
upright.yes_no: This leans no. There may be disappointment around this question, or an answer you were not hoping to hear. Still, a clear no can make room for something that suits you better. Allow yourself to be sad about it before you look for the next door.
upright.timing: The sharpest part of this pain usually passes fairly quickly, like a sudden afternoon downpour. A softer tenderness may linger for a while after. Do not rush yourself to be over it. Allow a season of gentleness before expecting your usual energy to return.
upright.advice: Let yourself feel it, rather than numbing or distracting yourself from it. Cry, talk, write or walk, whatever helps the feeling move through. Avoid making big decisions while the hurt is raw. Then let it pass like a storm, trusting that clearer skies follow.
upright.thread: honest heartache that must be felt before it can ease

reversed.summary: The hurt is beginning to soften. You may still feel a twinge when you think about what happened, but it no longer takes over your whole day. You are slowly getting ready to forgive, whether that means others or yourself. This is a time to breathe more freely and let recovery take its natural course.
reversed.love: Old wounds in a relationship begin to heal, though the scar may still be sensitive. Kind words, patience and small acts of care help a great deal now. Forgiving yourself for your own part matters as much as forgiving the other person. If you are single, you may notice your heart opening again after a guarded season.
reversed.career: You are recovering from a rough patch at work and coming out of it wiser. The sting of criticism or a setback is fading, leaving useful lessons behind. Rebuild your confidence steadily, one solid piece of work at a time. There is no need to prove yourself in a rush; consistency will speak for you.
reversed.money: You are moving past a loss or disappointment and starting to rebuild. Keep to a sensible, sustainable pace rather than trying to make everything back quickly. Small, steady habits such as tracking your spending will help restore your sense of control. Be patient with yourself as your confidence returns.
reversed.health: Your mood is lifting, slowly but genuinely. Gentle routines like regular meals, some morning light, movement and good sleep help support that recovery. Time with people who make you feel at ease can be especially healing now. There may still be low days, and that is part of the process rather than a step backwards.
reversed.family: Tension at home is easing, and forgiveness is becoming possible. You may not need a big conversation to mend things; small gestures can count for a lot. Bringing over a favourite dish or sending a kind message can open the door. Let people return to warmth at their own pace.
reversed.general: Healing is under way, even if it does not feel complete yet. The key now is not to keep picking at the old wound by replaying it again and again. Notice when your thoughts circle back, and gently redirect them. Each day you choose to move on, the pain loosens a little more.
reversed.yes_no: This still leans no for now, though more softly than before. The situation is improving, but it is not yet ready for a clear yes. Give the healing more time before pushing for an answer. Things may look different once the dust has fully settled.
reversed.timing: Recovery here is gradual, unfolding over weeks rather than overnight. Some days will feel lighter than others. Measure progress by how you feel compared with a month ago, not with yesterday. Steady patience works better than forcing a quick fix.
reversed.advice: Choose healing over replaying the story. When the memory returns, acknowledge it, then turn your attention to something that nourishes you. Forgiveness can be slow and private, and it does not require pretending nothing happened. Let lightness return in its own time.
reversed.thread: pain easing into forgiveness and a lighter, gentler outlook

cards.name: Four of Swords
cards.image_prompt: A peaceful figure resting in a quiet temple hall, three gold swords on the wall and one beneath, soft midnight light through a window.

upright.summary: This is a time for genuine rest and recovery. After a stretch of strain, your mind and body need stillness to repair. Pausing now is not wasted time; it is what makes your next step stronger and clearer. Give yourself permission to stop without guilt.
upright.love: Some quiet space can be healthy for a relationship right now. That might mean calm evenings together without plans, or a little time apart to recharge. Space taken kindly and explained clearly does not have to mean distance. When both of you are rested, conversations tend to go much better.
upright.career: Stepping back from the rush could serve you well. A short break, even a few days of leave or a weekend truly offline, can sharpen your focus and judgement. Problems that felt tangled may look simpler after rest. If a break is not possible, protect small pockets of quiet during the workday.
upright.money: This is a good time to pause on big financial decisions. Let things settle before you commit to anything major. Use the stillness to review where you stand without any pressure to act. Clarity often arrives once you stop pushing for it.
upright.health: Your body and mind are asking for proper rest, not just another kopi to push through the afternoon. Prioritise sleep, quiet and unhurried meals for a while. Even short periods of lying down, stretching or sitting somewhere calm can help. If tiredness persists despite rest, checking in with a doctor is a sensible step.
upright.family: Home may need a slower rhythm for a while. Fewer obligations, quieter evenings and simple meals can help everyone recover. It is okay to decline a few gatherings if the household is stretched thin. A calm home becomes a place where people can truly recharge.
upright.general: Retreat is not failure here. It is a deliberate pause to gather your strength before the next stage begins. Step away from noise, demands and constant input for a while. You will return clearer, steadier and better able to judge what matters.
upright.yes_no: Mixed. Now is not the moment to push for an answer or act on one. Rest first, let things settle, and then revisit the question. The answer may become obvious once you are less tired.
upright.timing: Expect a pause lasting some days or a few weeks. Things are not stuck; they are resting. Action and momentum return once you have truly recovered. Rushing the pause usually makes it last longer.
upright.advice: Rest is part of the work, not a break from it. Schedule recovery the way you would schedule a meeting, and protect it. Switch off notifications for a while and let your mind wander. You will make better choices once your reserves are refilled.
upright.thread: a needed pause for rest and recovery before moving on

reversed.summary: You may be pushing on when you really need to stop, or cutting your rest short because stillness feels uncomfortable. Alternatively, you may be slowly getting ready to return after a break. Either way, the key is pacing. Coming back too fast can undo the good that rest has done.
reversed.love: Restless feelings may stir in the relationship, perhaps a sense of being stuck or unsettled. Instead of quietly withdrawing or shutting down, try to name what you are feeling. Your partner cannot respond to something they do not know about. A calm talk now can prevent bigger distance later.
reversed.career: Watch for signs of exhaustion or burnout, such as dreading Mondays or struggling to focus. If you are returning after leave or a quiet spell, ease back in at a steady pace rather than rushing to catch up. Tackle a few key tasks first. Your energy will rebuild more reliably that way.
reversed.money: Try to avoid big financial decisions while you are worn out. Tired choices are rarely your best, and urgency can feel stronger than it really is. If something can wait until you have rested, let it wait. Clear thinking will serve you better than speed.
reversed.health: Restlessness, poor sleep or a feeling of running on empty may be showing up. These are signals worth listening to now, before your body forces a stop. Build in real downtime, not just a switch from one screen to another. If exhaustion keeps returning, a check-in with a doctor can help.
reversed.family: Everyone at home may be tired and a little on edge. Small irritations grow bigger when people are drained. Lower expectations for a while and share the chores more evenly. A simple takeaway dinner and an early night can do more good than a perfectly run household.
reversed.general: Rest has been skipped or cut short, and you may be feeling the effects. The inner work now is to allow a proper recovery before you fully resume. Notice whether busyness has become a way to avoid stillness. Returning slowly is still returning.
reversed.yes_no: Mixed, but leaning no for the moment. You may not be ready to move forward yet, even if part of you wants to. Give yourself more time to recover, then ask again. A rested mind will read the situation more clearly.
